body.text: Śaṃkara (attrib.): Kaṭhopaniṣadbhāṣya
body.translated_text: <s>Śaṃkara</s> (attributed): <s>Kaṭhopaniṣadbhāṣya</s> (Commentary on the <s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s>)

body.text: kāṭhakopaniṣat
body.translated_text: <s>Kāṭhakopaniṣat</s>

body.text: oṃ saha nāv avatu / saha nau bhunaktu / saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai // tejasvi nāvadhītamastu mā vidviṣāvahai // oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ //
body.translated_text: Oṃ. May He protect us both. May He nourish us both. May we work together with vigor. May our study be brilliant. May we not quarrel with each other. Oṃ, peace, peace, peace.

body.text:
oṃ namo bhagavate vaivasvatāya mṛtyave brahmavidyācāryāya naciketase ca /
atha kāṭhakopaniṣadvallīnāṃ sukhārthaprabodhanārtham alpagranthā vṛttir ārabhyate / sader dhātor viśaraṇagatyavasād anārthasyopanipūrvasya kvippratyayāntasya rūpam idam upaniṣad iti / upaniṣacchabdena ca vyācikhyāsitagranthapratipādyavedyavastuviṣayā vidyocyate / kena punar arthayogenopaniṣacchabdena vidyocyata ity ucyate / ye mumukṣavo dṛṣṭānuśravikaviṣayavitṛṣṇāḥ santa upaniṣacchabdavācyāṃ vakṣyamāṇalakṣaṇāṃ vidyām upasadyopagamya tanniṣṭhatayā niścayena śīlayanti teṣām avidyādeḥ saṃsārabijasya viśaraṇād dhiṃsanād vināśanād ity anenārthayogena vidyopaniṣad ity ucyate / tathā ca vakṣyati

children.text: "nicāyya taṃ mṛtyumukhāt pramucyate" (KaU 3.15)
children.translated_text: "Having ascertained it, one is released from the jaws of death." (<s>KaU</s> 3.15)

children.text: iti / pūrvoktaviśeṣaṇān vā mumukṣūn paraṃ brahma gamayatīti brahmagamayitṛtvena yogād brahmavidyopaniṣat / tathā ca vakṣyati
children.translated_text: Or, because it leads those who have the aforementioned qualifications — the seekers of liberation — to the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, by the connection of being a conveyor to <s>Brahman</s>, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is called '<s>upaniṣad</s>.' And so it will be stated:

children.text: "brahmaprāpto virajo 'bhūd vimṛtyuḥ" (KaU 3.18)
children.translated_text: "Having attained <s>Brahman</s>, he became free from impurity, free from death." (<s>KaU</s> 3.18)

children.text: iti / lokādir brahmajajño yo 'gnis tadviṣayāyā vidyāyā dvitīyena vareṇa prārthyamānāyāḥ svargalokaphalaprāptihetutvena garbhavāsajanmajarādyupadravavṛndasya lokāntare paunaḥpunyena pravṛttasyāvasādayitṛtvena śaithilyāpādanena dhātvarthayogād agnividyāpy upaniṣad ity ucyate / tathā ca vakṣyati
children.translated_text: The knowledge of fire, beginning with the universe and born of <s>Brahman</s> — this knowledge, which is sought through the second boon, since it produces the result of attaining the heavenly worlds and thereby weakens and loosens the recurring mass of afflictions such as dwelling in the womb, birth, old age, etc. in the other world — by the connection with the root-meaning, even the knowledge of fire is called '<s>upaniṣad</s>.' And so it will be stated:

children.text: "svargalokā amṛtatvaṃ bhajante" (KaU 1.13)
children.translated_text: "The heavenly worlds partake of immortality." (<s>KaU</s> 1.13)

children.text: ity ādi / nanu copaniṣacchabdenādhyetāro grantham apy abhilapanti / upaniṣadam adhīmaha upaniṣadam adhyāpayāma iti ca / naiṣa doṣaḥ, avidyādisaṃsārahetuviśaraṇādeḥ sadi dhātvarthasya granthamātre 'sambhavād vidyāyāṃ ca sambhavāt / granthasyāpi tādarthyena tacchabdatvopapatter āyur vai dhṛtam ity ādivat / tasmād vidyāyāṃ mukhyayā vṛttyopaniṣacchabdo vartate, granthe tu bhaktyeti / evam upaniṣannirvacanenaiva viśiṣṭo 'dhikārī vidyāyām uktaḥ / viṣayaś ca viśiṣṭa ukto vidyāyāḥ paraṃ brahma pratyagātmabhūtam / prayojanaṃ cāsyā upaniṣada ātyantikī saṃsāranivṛttir brahmaprāptilakṣaṇā / sambandhaś caivaṃ bhūtaprayojanenoktaḥ / ato yathoktādhikāriviṣayaprayojanasambandhāyā vidyāyāḥ karatalanyastāmalakavat prakāśakatvena viśiṣṭādhikāriviṣayaprayojanasambandhā etā vallyo bhavantīti / atas tā yathāpratibhānaṃ vyācakṣmahe /
children.translated_text: and so on. Now, by the word '<s>upaniṣad</s>' the students also refer to the text itself — 'We study the <s>upaniṣad</s>,' 'We teach the <s>upaniṣad</s>.' There is no fault in this, for the root-meaning of '<s>sad</s>' — the destruction of <s>avidyā</s> and other causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> — is not possible in the mere text but is possible in the knowledge. And since even the text can be denoted by that word due to its subservience to that [knowledge] — just as in '<s>āyur vai ghṛtam</s>' (ghee is [called] life) and similar cases. Therefore, the word '<s>upaniṣad</s>' applies in its primary sense to the knowledge, and to the text only in a secondary sense. Thus, by the very etymology of '<s>upaniṣad</s>,' the qualified student (<s>adhikārī</s>) of the knowledge is indicated. The subject matter of the knowledge is also indicated as qualified — it is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> that is the innermost Self. The purpose of this <s>upaniṣad</s> is the absolute cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> characterized by the attainment of <s>Brahman</s>. And the connection [between text and meaning] is stated through such a purpose. Therefore, these <s>vallīs</s> (sections), by illuminating the knowledge that has the aforementioned qualified student, subject, purpose, and connection — like a myrobalan fruit placed on the palm — have their own distinguished student, subject, purpose, and connection. Therefore we shall explain them according to our understanding.

body.translated_text: Oṃ, obeisance to the blessed <s>Vaivasvata</s> (son of <s>Vivasvat</s>), <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), the teacher of <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>), and to <s>Naciketas</s>! Now, for the easy comprehension of the meaning, a brief commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on the <s>vallīs</s> (sections) of the <s>Kāṭhaka Upaniṣad</s> is begun. The word '<s>upaniṣad</s>' is a form derived from the root '<s>sad</s>' (meaning destruction, going, and loosening) with the prefixes '<s>upa</s>' and '<s>ni</s>' and the affix '<s>kvip</s>.' By the word '<s>upaniṣad</s>,' the knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) is denoted whose subject is the reality to be known, as presented in the text intended to be explained. By what connection of meaning, then, is knowledge denoted by the word '<s>upaniṣad</s>'? It is said: Those seekers of liberation (<s>mumukṣus</s>) who, having become free from craving for objects seen and heard of, approach and take up the knowledge described by the word '<s>upaniṣad</s>' — whose characteristics will be explained — and practice it with certainty and devotion; for them, there is the destruction (<s>viśaraṇa</s>), the annihilation, the removal of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and other seeds of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) — by this connection of meaning, the knowledge is called '<s>upaniṣad</s>.' And so it will be stated:

children.text:
oṃ
uśan ha vai vājaśravasaḥ sarvavedasaṃ dadau /
tasya ha naciketā nāma putra āsa // KaU_1.1/1,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Oṃ. <s>Uśan</s> indeed, <s>Vājaśravasa</s> gave away all his possessions. He had a son named <s>Naciketas</s>. ||<s>KaU</s> 1.1||

body.text: tatrākhyāyikā vidyāstutyarthā / uśan kāmayamāno ha vā iti vṛttārthasmaraṇārthau nipātau / vājamannaṃ taddānādinimittaṃ śravo yaśo yasya sa vājaśravā, rūḍhito vā, tasyāpatyaṃ vājaśravasaḥ / sa kila viśvajitā sarvamedheneje tatphalaṃ kāmayamānaḥ / tasmin kratau sarvavedasaṃ sarvasvaṃ dhanaṃ dadau dattavān / tasya yajamānasya ha naciketā nāma putraḥ kilāsa babhūva // KaUBh_1.1/1,1.1 //
body.translated_text: Here the narrative serves to praise the knowledge. '<s>Uśan</s>' means 'desiring'; '<s>ha</s>' and '<s>vai</s>' are particles for recalling a past event. '<s>Vājaśravas</s>' — he whose fame (<s>śravas</s>) arises from food (<s>vāja</s>, i.e., wealth) and its giving, or [the word is used] as a proper name. '<s>Vājaśravasaḥ</s>' means the son of <s>Vājaśravas</s>. He, desiring the fruit of the <s>Viśvajit</s> sacrifice and the <s>Sarvamedha</s>, performed the ritual. In that sacrifice, he gave — gave away — all his possessions, all his wealth. That sacrificer had a son named <s>Naciketas</s>. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 1.1||

body.text: taṃ ha kumāraṃ santaṃ dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu śraddhāviveśa so 'manyata // KaU_1.2/1,1.2 //
body.translated_text: While he was still a boy, as the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> (sacrificial gifts) were being led away, faith entered him. He thought: ||<s>KaU</s> 1.2||

body.text: taṃ ha naciketasaṃ kumāraṃ prathamavayasaṃ santam aprāptajananaśaktiṃ bālam eva śraddhāstikyabuddhiḥ pitur hitakāmaprayuktaviveśa praviṣṭavatī / kasmin kāla ity āha -- ṛtvigbhyaḥ sadasyebhyaś ca dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu vibhāgenopanīyamānāsu dakṣiṇārthāsu goṣu, sa āviṣṭaśraddho naciketā amanyata // KaUBh_1.2/1,1.2 //
body.translated_text: Into that <s>Naciketas</s>, while still a boy — of the first age, who had not yet attained the power of procreation, a mere child — faith, the conviction of belief, entered, impelled by the desire for his father's welfare. At what time? He says: when the <s>dakṣiṇās</s> — the cows intended as gifts — were being led away, being distributed among the <s>ṛtviks</s> (priests) and <s>sadasyā</s>s (assessors). That <s>Naciketas</s>, possessed by faith, thought: ||<s>KaUBh</s> 1.2||

children.text: pītodakā jagdhatṛṇā dugdhadohā nirindriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Those cows] whose water has been drunk, whose grass has been eaten, whose milk has been milked, which are barren —

children.text: anandā nāma te lokāstānsa gacchati tā dadat // KaU_1.3/1,1.3 //
children.translated_text: joyless indeed are those worlds to which he goes who gives such [cows]. ||<s>KaU</s> 1.3||

body.text: katham ity ucyate -- pītodakā ity ādinā dakṣiṇārthā gāvo viśeṣyante / pītam udakaṃ yābhis tāḥ pītodakāḥ / jagdhaṃ bhakṣitaṃ tṛṇaṃ yābhis tā jagdhatṛṇāḥ / dugdho dohaḥ kṣīrākhyo yāsāṃ tā dugdhadohāḥ / nirindriyā prajananāsamarthā jīrṇā niṣphalā gāva ity arthaḥ / yās tā evambhūtā gā ṛtvigbhyo dakṣiṇābuddhyā dadatprayacchannanandā anānandā asukhā nāmety etad ye te lokās tān sa yajamāno gacchati // KaUBh_1.3/1,1.3 //
body.translated_text: How so? — this is stated with 'whose water has been drunk' etc. The cows intended as gifts are described: those whose water has been drunk up — <s>pītodakāḥ</s>; those whose grass has been consumed — <s>jagdhatṛṇāḥ</s>; those whose milking, the yield called milk, has been exhausted — <s>dugdhadohāḥ</s>; barren (<s>nirindriyāḥ</s>) — incapable of procreation, old, fruitless cows — this is the meaning. He who gives such cows to the <s>ṛtviks</s> with the intention of a sacrificial gift — joyless, unhappy — those are the worlds, and he, the sacrificer, goes to them. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 1.3||

children.text: sa hovāca pitaraṃ tata kasmai māṃ dāsyasīti /
children.translated_text: He said to his father: "Father, to whom will you give me?"

children.text: dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ taṃ hovāca mṛtyave tvā dadāmīti // KaU_1.4/1,1.4 //
children.translated_text: A second and a third time [he asked]. [The father] said to him: "I give you to <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death)." ||<s>KaU</s> 1.4||

body.text: tad evaṃ kratvasampattinimittaṃ pitur aniṣṭaṃ phalaṃ mayā putreṇa satā nivāraṇīyam ātmapradānenāpi kratusampattiṃ kṛtvā ity evaṃ matvā pitaram upagamya sa hovāca pitaram -- he tata tāta kasmā ṛtvigviśeṣāya dakṣiṇārthaṃ māṃ dāsyasīti prayacchasīty etat / evam uktena pitropekṣyamāṇo 'pi dvitīyaṃ tṛtiyam apy uvāca kasmai māṃ dāsyasi kasmai māṃ dāsyasīti / nāyaṃ kumārasvabhāva iti kruddhaḥ san pitā taṃ ha putraṃ kilovāca mṛtyave vaivasvatāya tvā tvāṃ dadāmīti // KaUBh_1.4/1,1.4 //
body.translated_text: Thus [thinking], 'The undesirable fruit for my father arising from the imperfection of the sacrifice should be averted by me, the son, even by offering myself, thereby perfecting the sacrifice' — having thought thus and approaching his father, he said to his father: "O father! To which particular priest will you give me as a <s>dakṣiṇā</s>?" — meaning, will you hand me over? Though being ignored by his father even when spoken to thus, he said a second and even a third time: "To whom will you give me? To whom will you give me?" [The father, thinking] 'This is not a child's nature [to persist so],' became angry and said to that son: "I give you to <s>Mṛtyu</s>, to <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Yama</s>)." ||<s>KaUBh</s> 1.4||

children.text: bahūnām emi prathamo bahūnām emi madhyamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Among many I go as the first; among many I go as the middling.

children.text: kiṃ svid yamasya kartavyaṃ yan mayādya kariṣyati // KaU_1.5/1,1.5 //
children.translated_text: What task of <s>Yama</s>'s could there be that he will accomplish through me today? ||<s>KaU</s> 1.5||

body.text: sa evam uktaḥ putra ekānte paridevayāñ cakāra / katham ity ucyate -- bahūnāṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ putrāṇāṃ vā emi gacchāmi prathamaḥ sanmukhyayā śiṣyādivṛttyety arthaḥ / madhyamānāṃ ca bahūnāṃ madhyamo madhyamayaiva vṛttyaimi / nādhamayā kadācid api / tam evaṃ viśiṣṭaguṇam api putraṃ māṃ

children.text: "mṛtyave tvā dadāmi" (KaU 1.4)
children.translated_text: "I give you to <s>Mṛtyu</s>" (<s>KaU</s> 1.4)

children.text: ity uktavān pitā / sa kiṃ svid yamasya kartavyaṃ prayojanaṃ mayā prattena kariṣyati yatkartavyam adya? nūnaṃ prayojanam anapekṣyaiva krodhavaśād uktavān pitā / tathāpi tatpitur vaco mṛṣā mā bhūditi // KaUBh_1.5/1,1.5 //
children.translated_text: — what task of <s>Yama</s>'s, what purpose will he accomplish through me, given to him, today? Surely the father spoke without consideration of any purpose, under the sway of anger. Even so, let my father's word not become false! ||<s>KaUBh</s> 1.5||

body.translated_text: He, thus spoken to, the son, lamented in solitude. How? — this is stated: Among many disciples or sons, 'I go' (<s>emi</s>) as the first, that is, I conduct myself as the foremost in the primary mode of a disciple and the like. And among many who are middling, I conduct myself with middling conduct. Never with the lowest. Yet my father has said to me, of such distinguished qualities,

body.text: evaṃ matvā paridevanāpūrvakam āha pitaraṃ śokāviṣṭa kiṃ vā mayoktam iti --
body.translated_text: Having thought thus, and having lamented, he said to his father — overwhelmed with grief, as if [saying] 'what have I said?' —

children.text: anupaśya yathā pūrve pratipaśya tathāpare /
children.translated_text: Look back at how the earlier ones [acted]; look forward at how the later ones [act].

children.text: sasyam iva martyaḥ pacyate sasyam ivājāyate punaḥ // KaU_1.6/1,1.6 //
children.translated_text: Like grain a mortal ripens; like grain he is born again. ||<s>KaU</s> 1.6||

body.text: anupaśyālocaya vibhāvayānukrameṇa yathā yena prakāreṇa vṛtāḥ pūrve 'tikrāntāḥ pitṛpitāmahādayas tava / tān dṛṣṭrvā ca teṣāṃ vṛttam āsthātum arhasi / vartamānāś cāpare sādhavo yathā vartante tāṃś ca tathā pratipaśyālocaya / na ca teṣāṃ mṛṣākaraṇaṃ vṛttaṃ vartamānaṃ vāsti / tadviparītam asatāṃ ca vṛttaṃ mṛṣākaraṇam / na ca mṛṣābhūtaṃ kṛtvā kaścid ajarāmaro bhavati / yataḥ sasyam iva martyo manuṣyaḥ pacyate jīrṇo mriyate, mṛtvā ca sasyam ivājāyata āvirbhavati punar evam anitye jīvaloke kiṃ mṛṣākaraṇena / pālayātmanaḥ satyam / preṣaya māṃ yamāyety abhiprāyaḥ // KaUBh_1.6/1,1.6 //
body.translated_text: Look back — consider, reflect, in order, how — in what manner — the earlier ones, those who have passed, your fathers and grandfathers, conducted themselves. Having seen them, you should follow their conduct. And look forward at how the later ones, the virtuous ones of the present, conduct themselves — consider that too. There is no false conduct among them, either past or present. The opposite — false conduct — belongs to the unrighteous. And no one becomes free from old age and death by acting falsely. For like grain, a mortal man ripens — grows old and dies — and having died, like grain he is born again, comes into being. In such an impermanent mortal world, what is the use of acting falsely? Keep your word! Send me to <s>Yama</s>! — this is the purport. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 1.6||

children.text: vaiśvānaraḥ praviśati atithir brāhmaṇo gṛhān /
children.translated_text: Like fire, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> guest enters the houses.

children.text: tasyaitāṃ śāntiṃ kurvanti hara vaivasvatodakam // KaU_1.7/1,1.7 //
children.translated_text: They offer him this pacification: "Bring water, O son of <s>Vivasvat</s>!" ||<s>KaU</s> 1.7||

body.text: sa evam uktaḥ pitātmanaḥ satyatāyai preṣayāmāsa / sa ca yamabhavanaṃ gatvā tistro rātrīr uvāsa yame proṣite / proṣyāgataṃ yamam amātyā bhāryā vā ūcur bodhayanto vaiśvānaro 'gnir eva sākṣāt praviśaty atithiḥ san brāhmaṇo gṛhān dahann iva / tasya dāhaṃ śamayanta ivāgner etāṃ pādyāsanādidānalakṣaṇāṃ śāntiṃ kurvanti santo 'tither yataḥ, ato harāhara he vaivasvatodakaṃ naciketase pādyārtham / yataś cākaraṇepratyavāyaḥ śrūyate // KaUBh_1.7/1,1.7 //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the father, in order to remain true to his word, sent him [to <s>Yama</s>]. And he, having gone to <s>Yama</s>'s abode, stayed for three nights while <s>Yama</s> was away. When <s>Yama</s> returned from his journey, his ministers or wife said to him, instructing him: 'The <s>Vaiśvānara</s> fire itself directly enters [the house] — a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> guest, as it were burning the house. The good ones make this appeasing [offering] to the guest — characterized by the giving of water for washing the feet, a seat, and the like — as if to quench the burning of that fire. Therefore, day after day, O <s>Vaivasvata</s> (son of the Sun), [offer] water to <s>Naciketas</s> for washing his feet. And because failure to do so [produces] sin, as is heard [in scripture]. [KaUBh 1.7]

children.text: āśāpratīkṣe saṃgataṃ sūnṛtāṃ ca iṣṭāpūrte putrapaśūṃś ca sarvān /
children.translated_text: Hopes and expectations, the fruit of good company and truthful speech, the merit of <s>iṣṭa</s> (sacrifice) and <s>pūrta</s> (charitable works), and all sons and cattle —

children.text: etad vṛṅkte puruṣasyālpamedhaso yasyānaśnan vasati brāhmaṇo gṛhe // KaU_1.8/1,1.8 //
children.translated_text: all this is destroyed for a person of little intelligence in whose house a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> guest stays without eating. [KaU 1.8]

body.text: āśāpratīkṣa anirjñātaprāpyeṣṭārthaprārthanā āśā, nirjñātaprāpyārthapratīkṣaṇaṃ pratīkṣā, ta āśāpratīkṣe / saṅgataṃ satsaṃyogajaṃ phalam, sūnṛtāṃ ca sūnṛtā hi priyā vāktannimittajaṃ ca / iṣṭāpūrte iṣṭaṃ yāgajaṃ phalam, pūrtam ārāmādi kriyājaṃ phalam / putrapaśūṃś ca putrāṃś ca sarvān etat sarvaṃ yathoktaṃ vṛṅkte varjayati vināśayatīty etat, puruṣasyālpamedhaso 'lpaprajñasya / yasyānaśnannabhuñjāno brāhmaṇo gṛhe vasati / tasmād anupekṣaṇīyaḥ sarvāvasthāsv apy atithir ity arthaḥ // KaUBh_1.8/1,1.8 //
body.translated_text: '<s>Āśā</s>' (hope) is the desire for an object whose attainability is not yet ascertained; '<s>pratīkṣā</s>' (expectation) is the awaiting of an object whose attainability has been ascertained — these two are '<s>āśāpratīkṣe</s>.' '<s>Saṅgata</s>' means the fruit born of association with good people; '<s>sūnṛtā</s>' means pleasant speech — and the fruit born from that. '<s>Iṣṭāpūrte</s>': '<s>iṣṭa</s>' is the fruit born of sacrifice; '<s>pūrta</s>' is the fruit born of works like [the construction of] gardens and the like. 'Sons and cattle and all' — all this as described, '<s>vṛṅkte</s>' means removes, destroys — that is the meaning — for a person of little intelligence (<s>alpamedhasa</s>), i.e. of little wisdom. 'In whose house a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> stays without eating' — i.e. without having been fed. Therefore, the meaning is that a guest should not be disregarded under any circumstances. [KaUBh 1.8]

children.text: tisro rātrīr yad avatsīr gṛhe me anaśnan brahmann atithir namasyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since you have stayed three nights in my house without eating, O <s>Brahman</s>, [you who are] a venerable guest —

children.text: namas te 'stu brahman svasti me 'stu tasmāt prati trīn varān vṛṇīṣva // KaU_1.9/1,1.9 //
children.translated_text: salutations to you, O <s>Brahman</s>! May there be well-being for me! Therefore, choose three boons. [KaU 1.9]

body.text: evam ukto mṛtyur uvāca naciketasam upagamya pūjāpuraḥsaram / tistro rātrīr yad yasmād avātsīr uṣitavānasi gṛhe me mamānaśnan he brahmann atithiḥ san namasyo namaskārārhaś ca, tasmān namaste tubhyam astu bhavatu / he brahman svasti bhadraṃ me 'stu / tasmād bhavato 'naśanena madgṛhavāsanimittād doṣāt / tatprāptyupaśamena yady api bhavad anugraheṇa sarvaṃ mama svasti syāt tathāpi tvadadhikasamprasādanārtham anaśanenoṣitām ekaikāṃ rātriṃ prati trīn varān vṛṇīṣv ābhipretārthaviśeṣān prārthayasva mattaḥ // KaUBh_1.9/1,1.9 //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, Death (<s>Mṛtyu</s>) approached <s>Naciketas</s> and said, preceded by worship: 'Since you have stayed — meaning 'lived' — three nights in my house without eating, O <s>Brahman</s>, being a guest worthy of salutation — therefore, salutations to you — may they be! O <s>Brahman</s>, may there be well-being, prosperity, for me. Therefore, due to the fault arising from your staying in my house without eating — though by your grace all may be well for me even through the cessation of that [fault] — nevertheless, for the purpose of further propitiating you, for each of the nights you stayed without eating, choose three boons — request from me three particular desired objects.' [KaUBh 1.9]

children.text: śāntasaṅkalpaḥ sumanā yathā syād vītamanyur gautamo mābhi mṛtyo /
children.translated_text: May [my father <s>Gautama</s>] be of calmed resolve, of good mind, free from anger toward me, O Death!

children.text: tvatprasṛṣṭaṃ mābhivadet pratīta etat trayāṇāṃ prathamaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe // KaU_1.10/1,1.10 //
children.translated_text: Released by you, may he greet me with recognition — this I choose as the first of the three boons. [KaU 1.10]

body.text: naciketās tv āha -- yadi ditsur varān śāntasaṅkalpa upaśāntaḥ saṅkalpo yasya māṃ prati, yamaṃ prāpya kin nu kariṣyati mama putra iti, sa śāntasaṅkalpaḥ sumanāḥ prasannamanāś ca yathā syād vītamanyur vigataroṣaś ca gautamo mama pitā mābhi māṃ prati he mṛtyo, kiñ ca tvatprasṛṣṭaṃ tvayā vinirmuktaṃ preṣitaṃ gṛhaṃ prati mām abhivadet pratīto labdhasmṛtiḥ, sa evāyaṃ putro mamāgata ity evaṃ pratyabhijānann ity arthaḥ / etat prayojanaṃ trayāṇāṃ varāṇāṃ prathamam ādyaṃ varaṃ vṛṇe prārthaye yatpituḥ paritoṣaṇam // KaUBh_1.10/1,1.10 //
body.translated_text: <s>Naciketas</s> said: If you are willing to grant boons — '<s>śāntasaṅkalpa</s>' means one whose resolve regarding me has subsided — [i.e.] 'Having reached <s>Yama</s>, what will become of my son?' — such [anxiety being] calmed, he is '<s>śāntasaṅkalpa</s>.' And '<s>sumanāḥ</s>' — of clear mind. 'May he be so' — and free from anger, with rage gone. '<s>Gautama</s>' — my father. '<s>Mābhi</s>' — toward me, O Death. Moreover, '<s>tvatprasṛṣṭam</s>' — released by you, sent home. 'May he greet me with recognition' (<s>pratīta</s>) — having recovered his memory, recognizing 'This is indeed my son, returned' — that is the meaning. This purpose — the gratification of my father — I choose as the first, the primary, of the three boons. [KaUBh 1.10]

children.text: yathā purastād bhavitā pratīta auddālakir āruṇir matprasṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as before, <s>Auddālaki Āruṇi</s>, released by me, will be

children.text: sukhaṃ rātrīḥ śayitā vītamanyus tvāṃ dadṛśivān mṛtyumukhāt pramuktam // KaU_1.11/1,1.11 //
children.translated_text: well-disposed [toward you]; he will sleep peacefully at night, free from anger, having seen you released from the jaws of Death. [KaU 1.11]

body.text: mṛtyur uvāca -- yathā buddhis tvayi purastāt pūrvam āsīt snehasamanvitā pitus tava bhavitā prītisamanvitas tava pitā tathaiva pratītaḥ pratītavān sann auddālakir uddālaka evauddālakiḥ, aruṇasyāpatyam āruṇir dvyāmuṣyāyaṇo vā matprasṛṣṭo mayānujñātaḥ sann uttarā api rātrīḥ sukhaṃ prasannamanāḥ śayitā svaptā vītamanyur vigatamanyuś ca bhavati syāt tvāṃ putraṃ dadṛśivān dṛṣṭavān san mṛtyumukhān mṛtyugocarāt pramuktaṃ santam // KaUBh_1.11/1,1.11 //
body.translated_text: Death (<s>Mṛtyu</s>) said: Just as the affectionate disposition of your father toward you existed before — so will he be well-disposed, having recognized [you]. '<s>Auddālaki</s>' — descendant of <s>Uddālaka</s>; '<s>Āruṇi</s>' — son of <s>Aruṇa</s> (or <s>dvyāmuṣyāyaṇa</s>, of dual lineage). 'Released by me' — permitted by me. He will sleep — he will rest peacefully through the remaining nights too, with a clear mind, free from anger. He will have seen you, his son, released — i.e. freed — from the vicinity of Death. [KaUBh 1.11]

children.text: svarge loke na bhayaṃ kiṃcanāsti na tatra tvaṃ na jarayā bibheti /
children.translated_text: In the heavenly world there is no fear whatsoever; you are not there, nor does one fear old age.

children.text: ubhe tīrtvā aśanāyāpipāse śokātigo modate svargaloke // KaU_1.12/1,1.12 //
children.translated_text: Having crossed beyond both hunger and thirst, having passed beyond sorrow, one rejoices in the heavenly world. [KaU 1.12]

body.text: naciketā uvāca -- svarge loke rogādinimittaṃ bhayaṃ kiñcana kiñcid api nāsti / na ca tatra tvaṃ mṛtyo sahasā prabhavasi, ato jarayā yukta iha lokavat tvatto na bibheti kaścit tatra / kiñcobha aśanāyāpipāse tīrtvātikramya śokam atītya gacchatīti śokātigaḥ san mānasena duḥkhena varjito modate hṛṣyati svargaloke divye // KaUBh_1.12/1,1.12 //
body.translated_text: <s>Naciketas</s> said: In the heavenly world there is no fear whatsoever — not even a little — caused by disease and the like. And you, O Death, do not prevail there suddenly; therefore, no one there fears old age — as [people do] in this world — [because there is no fear] of you. Moreover, having crossed beyond — having transcended — both hunger and thirst, having gone beyond sorrow — '<s>śokātiga</s>' means one who has transcended sorrow — being free from mental suffering, one rejoices, is delighted, in the heavenly world, the divine [realm]. [KaUBh 1.12]

children.text: sa tvam agniṃ svargyam adhyeṣi mṛtyo prabrūhi taṃ śraddadhānāya mahyam /
children.translated_text: You, O Death, know the fire [ritual] that leads to heaven. Teach it to me who am full of faith.

children.text: svargalokā amṛtatvaṃ bhajanta etad dvitīyena vṛṇe vareṇa // KaU_1.13/1,1.13 //
children.translated_text: Those whose world is heaven partake of immortality — this I choose as the second boon. [KaU 1.13]

body.text: evaṅ guṇaviśiṣṭasya svargalokasya prāptisādhanabhūtaṃ svargyam agniṃ sa tvaṃ mṛtyur adhyeṣi smarasi jānāsīty arthaḥ / he mṛtyo yatas taṃ prabrūhi kathaya śraddadhānāya śraddhāvate mahyaṃ svargārthine / yenāgninā citena svargalokaḥ svargo loko yeṣāṃ te svargalokā yajamānā amṛtatvam amaraṇatāṃ devatvaṃ bhajante prāpnuvanti tad etad agnivijñānaṃ dvitīyena vareṇa vṛṇe // KaUBh_1.13/1,1.13 //
body.translated_text: The fire [ritual] that leads to heaven — the means of attaining the heavenly world endowed with such qualities — that heavenly fire, you, O Death, know — you remember, you understand, that is the meaning. O Death, since [you know it], teach it — declare it — to me who am full of faith (<s>śraddadhāna</s>), who desires heaven. Those whose world is heaven — the sacrificers — partake of, attain, immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>), i.e. the state of non-dying, divinity. This — the knowledge of the fire [ritual] — I choose as the second boon. [KaUBh 1.13]

children.text: pra te bravīmi tad u me nibodha svargyam agniṃ naciketaḥ prajānan /
children.translated_text: I shall declare it to you — now learn it from me, the heavenly fire, O <s>Naciketas</s>, knowing [it well].

children.text: anantalokāptim atho pratiṣṭhāṃ viddhi tvam etaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyām // KaU_1.14/1,1.14 //
children.translated_text: Know this [fire] — the attainment of infinite worlds and the foundation — as hidden in the cave [of the heart]. [KaU 1.14]

body.text: mṛtyoḥ pratijñā iyam -- pra te tubhyaṃ prabravīmi / yat tvayā prārthitaṃ tadu me mama vacaso nibodha budhyasvaikāgramanāḥ san svargyaṃ svargāya hitaṃ svargasādhanam agniṃ he naciketaḥ prajānan vijñātavān sann aham ity arthaḥ / prabravīmi tan nibodheti ca śiṣyabuddhisamādhānārthaṃ vacanam / adhunāgniṃ stauti -- anantaṃ lokāpti svargalokaphalaprāptisādhanam ity etat / atho 'pi pratiṣṭhām āśrayaṃ jagato virāḍrūpeṇa tam etam agniṃ mayocyamānaṃ viddhi vijānīhi tvaṃ nihitaṃ sthitaṃ guhāyāṃ viduṣāṃ buddhau niviṣṭam ity arthaḥ // KaUBh_1.14/1,1.14 //
body.translated_text: This is the promise of Death (<s>Mṛtyu</s>): 'I shall declare it to you. That which you have requested — learn it from my words, with one-pointed mind — the heavenly fire, the means conducive to heaven, O <s>Naciketas</s>; I who know it' — that is the meaning. 'I declare it, now learn' — this statement is for the purpose of composing the disciple's mind. Now he praises the fire: 'Infinite-world-attainment' — the means of attaining the fruit of the heavenly world — this is what it means. 'And furthermore, the foundation' (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) — the support of the universe in the form of <s>Virāṭ</s>. This fire, as declared by me — know it, understand it — as placed, established in the cave — meaning deposited in the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) of the wise. [KaUBh 1.14]

children.text: lokādim agniṃ tam uvāca tasmai yā iṣṭakā yāvatīr vā yathā vā /
children.translated_text: He told him the fire that is the origin of the worlds — what the bricks are, how many, and in what manner.

children.text: sa cāpi tat pratyavadad yathoktam athāsya mṛtyuḥ punar āha tuṣṭaḥ // KaU_1.15/1,1.15 //
children.translated_text: And he [<s>Naciketas</s>] too repeated it back just as it was told; then Death, pleased, spoke again. [KaU 1.15]

body.text: idaṃ śruter vacanam / lokādiṃ lokānām ādiṃ pratham aśarīritvād agniṃ taṃ prakṛtaṃ naciketasā prārthitam uvācoktavān mṛtyus tasmai naciketase / kiñ ca yā iṣṭakāś cetavyāḥ svarūpeṇa, yāvatīr vā saṅkhyayā, yathā vā ciyate 'gnir yena prakāreṇa sarvam etad uktavān ity arthaḥ / sa cāpi naciketās tan mṛtyunoktaṃ pratyavadad yathāvat pratyayenāvadat pratyuccāritavān / athāsya pratyuccāraṇena tuṣṭaḥ san mṛtyuḥ punar evāha varatrayavyatirekeṇānyaṃ varaṃ ditsuḥ // KaUBh_1.15/1,1.15 //
body.translated_text: This is the statement of scripture. The fire that is the origin (<s>ādi</s>) of the worlds — the first, being incorporeal — this aforementioned fire, requested by <s>Naciketas</s>, Death told to <s>Naciketas</s>. And furthermore: what the bricks are by nature, how many by number, and in what manner the fire is built — by what method — all this he told — that is the meaning. And <s>Naciketas</s> too repeated back accurately what was told by Death — pronounced it in return. Then, pleased by his repeating it back, Death spoke again — wishing to give yet another boon beyond the three. [KaUBh 1.15]

children.text: tam abravīt prīyamāṇo mahātmā varaṃ tavehādya dadāmi bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Greatly pleased, the noble-souled one said to him: 'I grant you yet another boon today.

children.text: tavaiva nāmnā bhavitāyam agniḥ sṛṅkāṃ cemām anekarūpāṃ gṛhāṇa // KaU_1.16/1,1.16 //
children.translated_text: This fire shall be known by your name alone. And accept this garland of many forms.' [KaU 1.16]

body.text: kathaṃ taṃ naciketasam abravīt prīyamāṇaḥ śiṣyasya yogyatāṃ paśyan prīyamāṇaḥ prītim anubhavan mahātmākṣudrabuddhir varaṃ tava caturtham iha prītinimittam adyedānīṃ dadāmi bhūyaḥ punaḥ prayacchāmi / tavaiva naciketaso nāmnābhidhānena prasiddho bhavitā mayocyamāno 'yam agniḥ / kiñ ca sṛṅkāṃ śabdavatīṃ ratnamayīṃ mālām imām anekarūpāṃ vicitrāṃ gṛhāṇa svīkuru / yad vā, sṛṅkām akutsitāṃ gatiṃ karmamayīṃ gṛhāṇa / anyad api karmavijñānam anekaphalahetutvāt svīkurvity arthaḥ // KaUBh_1.16/1,1.16 //
body.translated_text: How did he [<s>Yama</s>] address that <s>Naciketas</s>? Being pleased (<s>prīyamāṇaḥ</s>), seeing the student's fitness, experiencing delight — the great-souled one, not of petty intellect, [said]: 'I give you a fourth boon here, arising from [my] pleasure, now, today; I grant [it] again.' [The fire] will become famous by the designation of your very name, <s>Naciketas</s>...

body.text: punar api karmastutim evāha --
body.translated_text: Again, he [<s>Yama</s>] states a praise of the ritual action —

children.text: triṇāciketas tribhir etya sandhiṃ trikarmakṛt tarati janmamṛtyū /
children.translated_text: The one who has thrice built the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire, having attained union with the three, performing the threefold action, crosses over birth and death;

children.text: brahmajajñaṃ devam īḍyaṃ viditvā nicāyyemāṃ śāntim atyantam eti // KaU_1.17/1,1.17 //
children.translated_text: Knowing the <s>Brahman</s>-born, divine, adorable [fire], and realizing this [peace], he attains absolute peace. (<s>KaU</s> 1.17)

body.text: triṇāciketas triḥkṛtvā nāciketo 'gniś cito yena sa triṇāciketas tadvijñānatadadhyayanatadanuṣṭhānavān vā / tribhir mātṛpitrācāryair etya prāpya sandhiṃ sandhānaṃ sambandhaṃ mātrādyanuśāsanaṃ yathāvat prāpyety etat / tad dhi prāmāṇyakāraṇaṃ śrutyantarād avagamyate

children.text: "yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān" (BĀU 4,1.2)
children.translated_text: 'As one who has a mother, as one who has a father' (<s>BĀU</s> 4.1.2)

children.text: ity ādeḥ / vedasmṛtiśiṣṭair vā pratyakṣānumānāgamair vā / tebhyo hi viśuddhiḥ pratyakṣā / trikarmakṛt ijyādhyayanadānānāṃ kartā taraty atikrāmati janmamṛtyū / kiñ ca brahmajajñaṃ brahmaṇo hiraṇyagarbhāj jāto brahmajaḥ, brahmajaś cāsau jñaś ceti brahmajajñaḥ sarvajño hy asau / taṃ devaṃ dyotanāñ jñānādiguṇavantam īḍyaṃ stutyaṃ viditvā śāstrato, nicāyya dṛṣṭvā cātmabhāvenemāṃ svabuddhipratyakṣāṃ śāntim uparatim atyantam ety atiśayenaiti / vairājaṃ padaṃ jñānakarmasamuccayānuṣṭhānena prāpnotīty arthaḥ // KaUBh_1.17/1,1.17 //
children.translated_text: and so on. Or [the three are]: the Vedas, <s>smṛtis</s>, and learned authorities; or perception, inference, and scripture. For from these comes purification directly. '<s>Trikarmakṛt</s>' — the performer of the three actions: sacrifice (<s>ijyā</s>), study (<s>adhyayana</s>), and charity (<s>dāna</s>) — crosses over, i.e., transcends birth and death. Moreover, '<s>brahmajajña</s>' — born from <s>Brahman</s>, i.e., <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, hence '<s>brahmaja</s>'; and being both '<s>brahmaja</s>' and '<s>jña</s>' (known/knowable), [it is called] '<s>brahmajajña</s>'...

body.translated_text: <s>Triṇāciketas</s> — one by whom the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire has been built three times, or one who possesses the knowledge of it, its study, and its practice. '<s>Tribhir etya sandhim</s>' — having attained (<s>etya</s>, i.e., <s>prāpya</s>) union (<s>sandhāna</s>), connection (<s>sambandha</s>), i.e., the instruction from the three — mother, father, and teacher — properly. For that is the cause of authoritative validity, [as stated] in another <s>śruti</s>...

body.text: idānīm agnivijñānacayanaphalam upasaṃharati prakaraṇa ca --
body.translated_text: Now he concludes with the fruit of the knowledge, building, and [the topic of] this section —

children.text: triṇāciketas trayam etad viditvā ya evaṃ vidvāṃś cinute nāciketam /
children.translated_text: The one who has thrice built the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire, having known this threefold [teaching], and who, knowing thus, builds the <s>Nāciketa</s> [fire],

children.text: sa mṛtyupāśān purataḥ praṇodya śokātigo modate svargaloke // KaU_1.18/1,1.18 //
children.translated_text: He, casting off the snares of death before [him], free from sorrow, rejoices in the heavenly world. (<s>KaU</s> 1.18)

body.text: triṇāciketas trayaṃ yathoktaṃ

children.text: "yā iṣṭakā yāvatīrvā yathā vā" (KaU 1.15)
children.translated_text: 'Whatever bricks, however many, and in whatever manner' (<s>KaU</s> 1.15)

children.text: ity etad viditvāvagamya yaś caivam ātmarūpeṇāgniṃ vidvāṃś cinute nirvartayati nāciketam agniṃ kratuṃ sa mṛtyupāśān adharmājñānarāgadveṣādilakṣaṇān purato 'grataḥ pūrvam eva śarīrapātād ity arthaḥ praṇodyāpahāya śokātigo mānasair duḥkhair varjita ity etan modate svargaloke vairāje virāḍātmasvarūpapratipattyā // KaUBh_1.18/1,1.18 //
children.translated_text: — having known (<s>avagamya</s>) this, and whosoever, knowing the fire as the <s>Ātman</s> in its own nature, builds, i.e., completes, the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire-ritual — he, having cast away (<s>praṇodya</s>, i.e., <s>apahāya</s>) the snares of death — characterized by <s>adharma</s>, ignorance, desire, hatred, and the like — before [him] (<s>purataḥ</s>), i.e., even before the fall of the body — this is the meaning — free from sorrow (<s>śokātiga</s>), i.e., freed from mental sufferings, rejoices...

body.translated_text: <s>Triṇāciketas</s> — having known the threefold [teaching] as stated —

children.text: eṣa te 'gnir naciketaḥ svargyo yam avṛṇīthā dvitīyena vareṇa /
children.translated_text: This is your fire, O <s>Naciketas</s>, the heavenly [one], which you chose with the second boon;

children.text: etam agniṃ tavaiva pravakṣyanti janāsas tṛtīyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva // KaU_1.19/1,1.19 //
children.translated_text: People will proclaim this fire by your very name. Choose the third boon, O <s>Naciketas</s>. (<s>KaU</s> 1.19)

body.text: eṣa te tubhyam agnir varo he naciketaḥ, svargyaḥ svargasādhano yam agniṃ varam avṛṇīthāḥ prārthitavānasi dvitīyena vareṇa, so 'gnir varo datta ity uktopasaṃhāraḥ / kiñ caitam agniṃ tavaiva nāmnā pravakṣyanti janāso janā ity etat / eṣa varo datto mayā caturthas tuṣṭena / tṛtīyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva / tasmin hy adatta ṛṇavān evāham ity ābhiprāyaḥ // KaUBh_1.19/1,1.19 //
body.translated_text: This [fire is] for you — the boon [is] yours, O <s>Naciketas</s>! The heavenly one, the means to heaven, which fire-boon you chose — you requested — with the second boon; that fire-boon has been given — thus the conclusion is stated. Moreover, people (<s>janāsaḥ</s>, i.e., <s>janāḥ</s>) will proclaim this fire by your very name — this is the meaning. This boon has been given by me...

body.text: etāvad dhy atikrāntena vidhipratiṣedhārthena mantrabrāhmaṇenāvagantavyaṃ yadvaradvayasūcitaṃ vastu nātmatattvaviṣayayāthātmyavijñānam / ato vidhipratiṣedhārthaviṣayasyātmani kriyākārakaphalādhyāropaṇalakṣaṇasya svābhāvikasyājñānasya saṃsārabījasya nivṛttyarthaṃ tadviparītabrahmātmaikatvavijñānaṃ kriyākārakaphalādhyāropaṇalakṣaṇaśūnyam ātyantikaniḥśreyasaprayojanaṃ vaktavyam ity uttaro grantha ārabhyate / tam etam arthaṃ dvitīyavaraprāptyāpy akṛtārthatvaṃ tṛtīyavaragocaram ātmajñānam antareṇa ity ākhyāyikayā prapañcayati --
body.translated_text: For by the preceding Vedic texts — both injunctive and prohibitive, both <s>mantra</s> and <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — what is to be understood is the subject-matter indicated by the two boons [already granted], not the knowledge of the true nature of the <s>Ātman</s>-reality. Therefore, for the removal of the natural ignorance — which is the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s>, characterized by the superimposition of action, agency, and result upon the <s>Ātman</s>, and which has as its subject-matter the domain of injunctions and prohibitions...

children.text: yeyaṃ prete vicikitsā manuṣye astīty eke nāyam astīti caike /
children.translated_text: This doubt regarding a person who has departed — some [say] 'it exists,' others [say] 'this does not exist';

children.text: etad vidyām anuśiṣṭas tvayāhaṃ varāṇām eṣa varas tṛtīyaḥ // KaU_1.20/1,1.20 //
children.translated_text: I wish to know this, instructed by you — this is the third of the boons. (<s>KaU</s> 1.20)

body.text: yataḥ pūrvasmāt karmagocarāt sādhyasādhanalakṣaṇād anityād viraktasyātmajñāne 'dhikāra iti tannindārtha putrādyupanyāsena pralobhanaṃ kriyate / naciketā uvāca

children.text: "tṛtīyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva" (KaU 1.19)
children.translated_text: 'Choose the third boon, O <s>Naciketas</s>' (<s>KaU</s> 1.19)

children.text: ity uktaḥ san -- yeyaṃ vicikitsā saṃśayaḥ prete mṛte manuṣye, astīty eke 'sti śarīrendriyamanobuddhivyatirikto dehāntarasambandhyātmety eke manyante, nāyam astīti caike, nāyam evaṃvidho 'stīti caike / ataś cāsmākaṃ na pratyakṣeṇa nāpi vānumānena nirṇayavijñānam / etad vijñānādhīno hi paraḥ puruṣārtha ity ata etad vidyāṃ vijānīyām aham anuśiṣṭo jñāpitas tvayā / varāṇām eṣa varas tṛtīyo 'vaśiṣṭaḥ // KaUBh_1.20/1,1.20 //
children.translated_text: — having been thus told: 'This doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), this uncertainty, regarding a person who has departed (<s>preta</s>), i.e., who has died — some think: "It exists — there is a self connected with another body, distinct from body, senses, mind, and intellect"; and others [think]: "This does not exist — there is no such [self]." And therefore, for us, neither by perception nor even by inference can it be determined...

body.translated_text: Since one who has become dispassionate toward the prior realm of action — characterized by means and ends, and being impermanent — is qualified for <s>Ātma-jñāna</s> (Self-knowledge), in order to censure that [realm], temptation is offered through the presentation of sons and the like. <s>Naciketas</s> spoke —

body.text: kim ayam ekāntato niḥśreyasasādhanātmajñānārho na vety etat parīkṣaṇārtham āha --
body.translated_text: [<s>Yama</s> speaks] in order to test whether this [<s>Naciketas</s>] is absolutely worthy of <s>Ātma-jñāna</s>, the means to the supreme good, or not —

children.text: devair atrāpi vicikitsitaṃ purā na hi sujñeyam aṇur eṣa dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the gods had doubt about this matter formerly, for this <s>dharma</s> (truth) is not easily known — it is subtle.

children.text: anyaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva mā moparotsīr ati mā sṛjainam // KaU_1.21/1,1.21 //
children.translated_text: Choose another boon, O <s>Naciketas</s>! Do not press me; release me from this! (<s>KaU</s> 1.21)

body.text: devair apy atraitasmin vastuni vicikitsitaṃ saṃśayitaṃ purā pūrvam / na hi suvijñeyaṃ suṣṭhu jñeyam asakṛt śrutam api prākṛtair janair yato 'ṇuḥ sūkṣma eṣa ātmākhyo dharmaḥ / ato 'nyam asan digdhaphalaṃ varaṃ naciketo vṛṇīṣva, mā moparotsīr uparodhaṃ mā kārṣīr adharmaṇam ivottamarṇaḥ / atisṛja vimuñcainaṃ varaṃ mā māṃ prati // KaUBh_1.21/1,1.21 //
body.translated_text: Even by the gods, regarding this matter — this subject — doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), i.e., uncertainty, arose formerly (<s>purā</s>). For it is not easily known (<s>suvijñeya</s>), not [something] well-understood even when heard many times by ordinary people, because this truth called the <s>Ātman</s> is subtle (<s>aṇu</s>, i.e., <s>sūkṣma</s>). Therefore, choose another boon, O <s>Naciketas</s> — one whose fruit is not doubtful. Do not press me...

body.text: evam ukto naciketā āha --
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Naciketas</s> said —

children.text: devair atrāpi vicikitsitaṃ kila tvaṃ ca mṛtyo yan na sujñeyam āttha /
children.translated_text: Even the gods had doubt about this, indeed! And you, O Death, say that it is not easily known.

children.text: vaktā cāsya tvādṛg anyo na labhyo nānyo varas tulya etasya kaścit // KaU_1.22/1,1.22 //
children.translated_text: Another speaker like you on this [subject] cannot be found; no other boon is equal to this one. (<s>KaU</s> 1.22)

body.text: devair atrāpy etasmin vastuni vicikitsitaṃ kileti bhavata eva naḥ śrutam / tvaṃ ca mṛtyo yady asmān na sujñeyam ātmatattvam āttha kathayasi / ataḥ paṇḍitair apy avadanīyatvād vaktā cāsya dharmasya tvādṛk tvattulyo 'nyaḥ paṇḍitaś ca na labhyo 'nviṣyamāṇo 'py ayaṃ tu varo niḥśreyasaprāptihetuḥ / ato nānyo varas tulyaḥ sadṛśo 'sty etasya kaścid apy, anityaphalatvād anyasya sarvasyaivety abhiprāyaḥ // KaUBh_1.22/1,1.22 //
body.translated_text: Even the gods had doubt about this very matter, indeed — so we have heard from you yourself. And you, O Death, say (<s>āttha</s>, i.e., <s>kathayasi</s>) that the <s>Ātman</s>-reality is not easily known. Therefore, since even by the learned it cannot [easily] be expounded, another speaker of this truth, equal to you (<s>tvādṛk</s>, i.e., <s>tvattulya</s>) — another scholar — cannot be found even when sought...

body.text: evam ukto 'pi punaḥ pralobhayann uvāca mṛtyuḥ --
body.translated_text: Even when thus addressed, Death spoke again, tempting [him] —

children.text: śatāyuṣaḥ putrapautrān vṛṇīṣva bahūn paśūn hastihiraṇyam aśvān /
children.translated_text: Choose sons and grandsons who live a hundred years, many cattle, elephants, gold, and horses;

children.text: bhūmer mahad āyatanaṃ vṛṇīṣva svayaṃ ca jīva śarado yāvad icchasi // KaU_1.23/1,1.23 //
children.translated_text: Choose a great domain on the earth, and live yourself as many autumns as you wish! (<s>KaU</s> 1.23)

body.text: śatāyuṣaḥ śataṃ varṣāṇy āyūṃṣi yeṣāṃ tān śatāyuṣaḥ putrapautrān vṛṇīṣva / kiñ ca gavādilakṣaṇān bahūn paśūn, hastihiraṇyaṃ hastī ca hiraṇyaṃ ca hastihiraṇyam, aśvāṃś ca / kiñ ca bhūmeḥ pṛthivyā mahad vistīrṇam āyatanam āśrayaṃ maṇḍalaṃ sāmrājyaṃ vṛṇīṣva / kiñ ca sarvam apy etad anarthakaṃ svayaṃ ced alpāyur ity ata āha -- svayaṃ ca tvaṃ jīva dhāraya śarīraṃ samagrendriyakalāpaṃ śarado varṣāṇi yāvad icchasi jīvitum // KaUBh_1.23/1,1.23 //
body.translated_text: '<s>Śatāyuṣaḥ</s>' — those whose life-spans are a hundred years — choose such sons and grandsons who live a hundred years. Moreover, many cattle (<s>paśu</s>) characterized as cows and the like; elephants and gold (<s>hastihiraṇya</s> — elephants and gold [as a compound]); and horses. Moreover, choose a great (<s>mahat</s>), i.e., vast, domain (<s>āyatana</s>), i.e., abode, territory, sovereignty, on the earth...

children.text: etat tulyaṃ yadi manyase varaṃ vṛṇīṣva vittaṃ cirajīvikāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: If you consider a boon equal to this, choose wealth and long life!

children.text: mahābhūmau naciketas tvam edhi kāmānāṃ tvā kāmabhājaṃ karomi // KaU_1.24/1,1.24 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Naciketas</s>, prosper on the great earth! I shall make you the enjoyer of [all] desires. (<s>KaU</s> 1.24)

body.text: etat tulyam etena yathopadiṣṭena sadṛśamanyam api yadi manyase varaṃ tam api vṛṇīṣva / kiñ ca vittaṃ prabhūtaṃ hiraṇyaratnādi cirajīvikāṃ ca saha vittena vṛṇīṣvety etat / kiṃ bahunā, mahābhūmau mahatyāṃ bhūmau rājā naciketas tvam edhi bhava / kiñ cānyat kāmānāṃ divyānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca tvā tvāṃ kāmabhājaṃ kāmabhāginaṃ kāmārhaṃ karomi, satyasaṅkalapo hy ahaṃ devaḥ // KaUBh_1.24/1,1.24 //
body.translated_text: This is equal — if you think of anything else similar to what has been taught, choose that boon as well. Moreover, choose wealth — abundant gold, gems, and the like — along with long life; this is the meaning. Why say more? O <s>Naciketas</s>, become a king over a great territory, a vast land. And further, I shall make you <s>kāmabhāj</s> (a partaker of desires), <s>kāmabhāgin</s> (an enjoyer of desires), worthy of [all] desires — both divine and human. For I am a god whose resolve is truth.

children.text:
ye ye kāmā durlabhā martyaloke sarvān kāmāṃś chandataḥ prārthayasva /
imā rāmāḥ sarathāḥ satūryā na hīdṛśā lambhanīyā manuṣyaiḥ /
ābhir matprattābhiḥ paricārayasva naciketo maraṇaṃ mānuprākṣīḥ // KaU_1.25/1,1.25 //
children.translated_text: Whatever desires are hard to obtain in the mortal world, ask for all those desires according to your wish. Here are these <s>rāmāḥ</s> (beautiful maidens) with chariots, with musical instruments — such as these are not to be obtained by mortals. Let yourself be served by these, given by me. O <s>Naciketas</s>, do not ask about death.

body.text: ye ye kāmāḥ prārthanīyā durlabhāś ca matryaloke sarvās tān kāmāñ chandata icchātaḥ prārthayasva / kiñ cemā divyā apsaraso, ramayanti puruṣān iti rāmāḥ, saha rathair vartanta iti sarathāḥ, satūryāḥ savāditrāḥ, tāś ca na hi lambhanīyāḥ prāpaṇīyā īdṛśā evaṃvidhā manuṣyair matyair asmadādiprasādam antareṇa / ābhir matprattābhir mayā pradattābhiḥ paricāriṇībhiḥ paricārayasvātmānam, pādaprakṣālanādiśuśrūṣāṃ kārayātmana ity arthaḥ / naciketo, maraṇaṃ maraṇasambaddhaṃ praśnaṃ prete 'sti nāstīti kākadantaparīkṣārūpaṃ mānuprākṣīr maivaṃ praṣṭum arhasi // KaUBh_1.25/1,1.25 //
body.translated_text: Whatever desires are worth seeking and are hard to obtain in the mortal world, ask for all those desires according to your wish, that is, as you please. Moreover, these divine <s>Apsaras</s> — they are called <s>rāmāḥ</s> because they delight (<s>ramayanti</s>) men — <s>sarathāḥ</s> means accompanied by chariots, <s>satūryāḥ</s> means with musical instruments; and such ones are indeed not <s>lambhanīyāḥ</s> (obtainable) — not attainable — of this kind, by mortals, by human beings, without the grace of one such as me. With these attendants given by me, have yourself served — that is, have the service of foot-washing and the like performed for yourself; this is the meaning. O <s>Naciketas</s>, do not ask about death — the question connected with death, of the form 'does [the soul] exist or not after death,' which is like examining the teeth of a crow [i.e., a futile inquiry]; you should not ask thus.

body.text: evaṃ pralobhyamāno 'pi naciketā mahāhradavadakṣobhya āha --
body.translated_text: Even though being thus tempted, <s>Naciketas</s>, unshakeable like a great lake, said —

children.text: śvobhāvā martyasya yad antakaitat sarvendriyāṇāṃ jarayanti tejaḥ /
children.translated_text: These are things that last only till tomorrow, O <s>Antaka</s> (Death); they wear away the vigor of all the senses.

children.text: api sarvaṃ jīvitam alpam eva tavaiva vāhās tava nṛtyagīte // KaU_1.26/1,1.26 //
children.translated_text: Moreover, all life is short indeed; let the chariots, the dance, and the song remain yours alone.

body.text: śvo bhaviṣyanti na bhaviṣyanti veti sandihyamāna eva yeṣāṃ bhāvo bhavanaṃ tvayopanyastānāṃ bhogānāṃ te śvobhāvāḥ / kiñ ca matryasya manuṣyasyāntaka he mṛtyo, yad etat sarvendriyāṇāṃ tejas taj jarayanty apakṣayanty apsaraḥprabhṛtayo bhogā anarthāyaivate dharmavīryaprajñātejoyaśaḥprabhṛtīnāṃ kṣapayitṛtvāt / yāṃ cāpi dīrghajīvikāṃ tvaṃ ditsasi tatrāpi śṛṇu / sarvaṃ yad brahmaṇo 'pi jīvitam āyur alpam eva, kim utāsmadādidīrghajīvikā / atas tavaiva tiṣṭhantu vāhā rathādayas tathā tava nṛtyagīte ca // KaUBh_1.26/1,1.26 //
body.translated_text: Those whose existence is doubtful — whether they will exist tomorrow or not — the enjoyments presented by you are <s>śvobhāvāḥ</s> (lasting only till tomorrow). Moreover, O <s>Antaka</s>, O Death, these enjoyments such as <s>Apsaras</s> and others wear away, diminish, the vigor of all the senses of a mortal, a human being — they are indeed for harm alone, because they destroy <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>vīrya</s> (strength), <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>tejas</s> (splendor), <s>yaśas</s> (fame), and the like. And regarding the long life that you wish to give, hear this too: all life, even that of <s>Brahmā</s>, is short indeed — how much more so a long life such as ours? Therefore, let the chariots and other vehicles remain yours, and likewise the dance and song.

children.text: na vittena tarpaṇīyo manuṣyo lapsyāmahe vittam adrākṣma cet tvā /
children.translated_text: A person is not to be satisfied by wealth. We shall obtain wealth if we have but seen you.

children.text: jīviṣyāmo yāvad īśiṣyasi tvaṃ varas tu me varaṇīyaḥ sa eva // KaU_1.27/1,1.27 //
children.translated_text: We shall live as long as you shall rule. But the boon to be chosen by me is that one alone.

body.text: kiñ ca na prabhūtena vittena tarpaṇīyo manuṣyaḥ / na hi loke vittalābhaḥ kasyacit tṛptikaro dṛṣṭaḥ / yadi nāmāsmākaṃ vittatṛṣṇā syāl lapsyāmahe prāpsyāmahe vittam adrākṣma dṛṣṭavanto vayaṃ cet tvā tvām / jīvitam api tathaiva, jīviṣyāmo yāvad yāmye pade tvam īśiṣyasīśiṣyase prabhuḥ syāḥ / kathaṃ hi martyas tvayā sametyālpadhanāyur bhavet / varas tu me varaṇīyaḥ sa eva yadātmavijñānam // KaUBh_1.27/1,1.27 //
body.translated_text: Moreover, a person is not to be satisfied by abundant wealth. For in the world, the acquisition of wealth has never been seen to bring satisfaction to anyone. If indeed we had a thirst for wealth, we shall obtain, we shall acquire wealth, having seen you. Life too is likewise — we shall live as long as you shall rule, as long as you shall be lord in the realm of <s>Yama</s>. For how could a mortal, having met you, remain with meager wealth and short life? But the boon to be chosen by me is that one alone — namely, the knowledge of the Self.

children.text: ajīryatām amṛtānām upetya jīryan martyaḥ kvadhaḥsthaḥ prajānan /
children.translated_text: Having approached the immortals who do not age, what mortal dwelling here below, knowing [this],

children.text: abhidhyāyan varṇaratipramodān atidīrghe jīvite ko rameta // KaU_1.28/1,1.28 //
children.translated_text: contemplating the pleasures of beauty, enjoyment, and delight, would rejoice in an exceedingly long life?

body.text: yataś cājīryatāṃ vayohāṇim aprāpnuvatām amṛtānāṃ sakāśam upetyopagamyātmana utkṛṣṭaṃ prayojanāntaraṃ prāptavyaṃ tebhyaḥ prajānann upalabhamānaḥ svayaṃ tu jīryan martyo jarāmaraṇavān kvadhaḥsthaḥ kuḥ pṛthivy adhaś cāsāv āntarikṣādilokāpekṣayā tasyāṃ tiṣṭhatīti kvadhaḥsthaḥ san katham evam avivekibhiḥ prārthanīyaṃ putravittādyasthiraṃ vṛṇīte / "kva tadāsthaḥ" iti vā pāṭhāntaram / asmin pakṣe caivam akṣarayojanā teṣu putrādiṣv āsthā sthitis tātparyeṇa vartanaṃ yasya sa tadāsthaḥ, tato 'dhikataraṃ puruṣārthaṃ duṣprāpam api prāpipayiṣuḥ kva tadāstho bhavet ? na kaścit tadasārajñas tadarthī syād ity arthaḥ / sarvo hy uparyuparyeva bubhūṣati lokas tasmān na putravittādilobhaiḥ pralobhyo 'ham / kiñ cāpsaraḥ pramukhān varṇaratipramodānanavasthitarūpatayābhidhyāyannirūpayanyathāvad atidīrghe jīvite ko vivekī rameta // KaUBh_1.28/1,1.28 //
body.translated_text: And since, having approached — having come near — the immortals, those who do not undergo decay of age, and having perceived a superior purpose to be attained from them beyond oneself, [one who is] himself aging, a mortal subject to old age and death, <s>kvadhaḥsthaḥ</s> — '<s>ku</s>' means the earth, and 'below' in comparison to the intermediate and other worlds, one who dwells on it is <s>kvadhaḥsthaḥ</s> — being such, how would he choose what is impermanent, such as sons and wealth, which is sought only by the undiscriminating? Or the alternative reading is '<s>kva tadāsthaḥ</s>' — in this reading, the analysis of syllables is thus: one whose <s>āsthā</s> (attachment), whose <s>sthiti</s> (abiding), whose earnest engagement is in those [things] such as sons and the like — such a <s>tadāstha</s>, even wishing to attain a higher <s>puruṣārtha</s> (human goal) that is hard to obtain, where would he be <s>tadāstha</s>? No one who knows its essence would seek such [fleeting things]; this is the meaning. For everyone in the world wishes to rise ever higher and higher; therefore I am not to be tempted by enticements of sons, wealth, and the like. Moreover, contemplating — examining as they truly are — the pleasures of beauty, enjoyment, and delight, with <s>Apsaras</s> as their chief, which are of unstable nature, what discerning person would rejoice in an exceedingly long life?

children.text: yasminn idaṃ vicikitsanti mṛtyo yat sāmparāye mahati brūhi nas tat /
children.translated_text: O Death, that about which they have doubt regarding one who has died, in the great [question of] the hereafter — tell us that.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ varo gūḍham anupraviṣṭo nānyaṃ tasmān naciketā vṛṇīte // KaU_1.29/1,1.29 //
children.translated_text: This boon that has entered into what is hidden — <s>Naciketas</s> chooses no other than this.

body.text: iti kāṭhakopaniṣadi prathamā vallī // 1 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>Vallī</s> (section) of the <s>Kāṭhakopaniṣad</s>.

body.text: ato vihāyānityaiḥ kāmaiḥ pralobhanaṃ yanmayā prārthitaṃ yasmin preta idaṃ vicikitsanaṃ vicikitsanty asti nāstīty evaṃ prakāram, he mṛtyo, sāmparāye paralokaviṣaye mahati mahatprayojananimitta ātmano nirṇayavijñānaṃ yat tad brūhi kathaya no 'smabhyam / kiṃ bahunā / yo 'yaṃ prakṛta ātmaviṣayo varo gūḍhaṃ gahanaṃ durvivecanaṃ prāpto 'nupraviṣṭaḥ, tasmād varād anyam avivekibhiḥ prārthanīyam anityaviṣayaṃ varaṃ naciketā na vṛṇīte manasāpīti śruter vacanam iti // KaUBh_1.29/1,1.29 //
body.translated_text: Therefore, setting aside the temptation with impermanent desires, regarding that which I have requested — about which, concerning the departed, there is this doubt, they doubt whether it exists or not, of such a nature — O Death, tell us, explain to us, the definitive knowledge of the Self regarding the hereafter, concerning the next world, which has a great purpose, which is the cause of a great goal. Why say more? This boon that is under discussion, pertaining to the Self, which has entered into what is <s>gūḍha</s> (hidden), <s>gahana</s> (profound), hard to discern — a boon other than this, one pertaining to impermanent objects sought by the undiscriminating, <s>Naciketas</s> does not choose, not even in his mind — such is the declaration of the <s>śruti</s> (scripture).

body.text: iti kaṭhavallyāṃ prathamavallībhāṣyam // 1 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the commentary on the first <s>Vallī</s> of the <s>Kaṭhavallī</s>.

body.text:
atha dvitīyā vallī /
parīkṣya śiṣyaṃ vidyāyogyatāṃ cāvagamyāha --
body.translated_text: Now the second <s>Vallī</s>. Having examined the student and having ascertained his fitness for knowledge, [<s>Yama</s>] said —

children.text: anyac chreyo 'nyad utaiva preyas te ubhe nānārthe puruṣaṃ sinītaḥ /
children.translated_text: The good (<s>śreyas</s>) is one thing, and the pleasant (<s>preyas</s>) is quite another; these two, serving different purposes, bind a person.

children.text: tayoḥ śreya ādadānasya sādhu bhavati hīyate 'rthād ya u preyo vṛṇīte // KaU_2.1/1,2.1 //
children.translated_text: Of these two, it goes well for the one who chooses the good; the one who chooses the pleasant falls away from the [true] goal.

body.text: anyat pṛthag eva śreyo niḥśreyasaṃ tathānyad utaivāpi ca preyaḥ priyataram api te preyaḥ śreyasy ubhe nānārthe bhinnaprayojane satī puruṣam adhikṛtaṃ varṇāśramādiviśiṣṭaṃ sinīto badhnītas tābhyāṃ vidyāvidyābhyām ātmakartavyatayā prayujyate sarvaḥ puruṣaḥ / śreyaḥ preyasor hy abhyudayāmṛtatvārthī puruṣaḥ pravartate / ataḥ śreyaḥ preyaḥ prayojanakartavyatayā, tābhyāṃ buddha ity ucyate sarvaḥ puruṣaḥ / te yady apy ekaikapuruṣārthasambandhinī vidyāvidyārūpatvād viruddhe ity anyatarāparityāgenaikena puruṣena sahānuṣṭhātum aśakyatvāt tayor hitvāvidyārūpaṃ preyaḥ, śreya eva kevalam ādadānasyopādānaṃ kurvataḥ sādhu śobhanaṃ śivaṃ bhavati / yas tv adūradarśī vimūḍho hīyate viyujyate 'rthāt puruṣārthāt pāramārthikāt prayojanān nityāt pracyavata ity arthaḥ / ko 'sau ya u preyo vṛṇīta upādatta ity etat // KaUBh_2.1/1,2.1 //
body.translated_text: The good (<s>śreyas</s>), which is distinct, is <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (the highest good, liberation); and likewise the pleasant (<s>preyas</s>), the more agreeable, is also different. Both the pleasant and the good, serving different purposes, having distinct goals, bind — that is, engage — a person who is qualified, distinguished by <s>varṇa</s> (social class), <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), and the like. Through these two — <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — every person is impelled as having something to accomplish for himself. For a person acts seeking either worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>) or immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>), which correspond to the pleasant and the good respectively. Therefore, having the good and the pleasant as purposes to be accomplished, every person is said to be 'bound' by them. Although these two, belonging to a single individual's <s>puruṣārtha</s> (goal of life), being of the nature of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s>, are opposed — and because it is impossible for one person to pursue both without abandoning one — of these two, for the one who, having abandoned the pleasant which is of the nature of <s>avidyā</s>, takes up, adopts the good alone exclusively, it goes well — it is auspicious, it is blessed. But the one who is short-sighted, deluded, falls away — is separated — from the <s>puruṣārtha</s> (true human goal), from the ultimate purpose; he lapses from the eternal goal; this is the meaning. Who is he? The one who chooses, who takes up the pleasant.

children.text: śreyaś ca preyaś ca manuṣyam etas tau saṃparītya vivinakti dhīraḥ /
children.translated_text: Both the good and the pleasant approach a person; the wise one, having examined them both, discriminates between them.

children.text: śreyo hi dhīro 'bhi preyaso vṛṇīte preyo mando yogakṣemād vṛṇīte // KaU_2.2/1,2.2 //
children.translated_text: The wise one chooses the good over the pleasant; the dull-witted one chooses the pleasant for the sake of acquisition and preservation [of worldly goods].

body.text: yady ubhe 'pi kartuṃ svāyatte puruṣeṇa, kim arthaṃ preya evādatte bāhulyena loka ity ucyate -- satyaṃ svāyatte, tathāpi sādhanataḥ phalataś ca mandabuddhīnāṃ durvivekarūpe satī vyāmiśrībhūta iva manuṣyaṃ puruṣam etaḥ prāpnutaḥ śreyaś ca preyaś ca / ato haṃsa ivāmbhasaḥ payaḥ, tau śreyaḥ preyaḥ padārthau samparītya samyak parigamya manāsālocya gurulāghavaṃ vivinakti pṛthak karoti dhīro dhīmān / vivicya ca śreyo hi śreya evābhivṛṇīte preyaso 'bhyarhitatvāt / ko 'sau dhīraḥ / yas tu mando 'lpabuddhiḥ sa sadasadvivekāsāmarthyād yogakṣemād yogakṣemanimitaṃ śarīrādyupacayarakṣaṇanimittam ity etat preyaḥ paśuputrādilakṣaṇaṃ vṛṇīte // KaUBh_2.2/1,2.2 //
body.translated_text: If both are within a person's power to accomplish, why does the world largely choose only the pleasant? It is said: True, both are within one's power; nevertheless, being of a nature hard to discriminate for those of dull intellect, in terms of both means and results, and becoming as if mixed together, both the good and the pleasant approach, reach a person, a human being. Therefore, like a swan [separating] milk from water, having fully examined, thoroughly considered, and weighed the relative importance of both — the good and the pleasant — the wise one, the one possessed of wisdom, discriminates, separates them. And having discriminated, the wise one chooses the good alone, because it is more worthy than the pleasant. Who is this wise one? But the one who is <s>manda</s> (dull-witted), of little understanding — he, due to his inability to discriminate between the real and the unreal, chooses the pleasant, characterized by cattle, sons, and the like, for the sake of <s>yogakṣema</s> (acquisition and preservation) — that is, for the purpose of acquiring and protecting the body and its accessories.

children.text: sa tvaṃ priyān priyarūpāṃś ca kāmān abhidhyāyan naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ /
children.translated_text: You, having contemplated the dear ones and the objects of desire that are of pleasing form, O <s>Naciketas</s>, have relinquished [them all].

children.text: naitāṃ sṛṅkāṃ vittamayīm avāpto yasyāṃ majjanti bahavo manuṣyāḥ // KaU_2.3/1,2.3 //
children.translated_text: You have not entered this chain made of wealth, in which many mortals sink. // KaU 2.3 //

body.text: sa tvaṃ punaḥ punar mayā pralobhyamāno 'pi priyān putrādīn priyarūpāṃś cāpsaraḥprabhṛtilakṣaṇān kāmān abhidhyāyaṃś cintayaṃs teṣām anityatvāsāratvādidoṣān he naciketotyastrākṣīratisṛṣṭavān parityaktavān asyaho buddhimattā tava / naitām avāptavān asi sṛṅktāṃ sṛtiṃ kutsitāṃ mūḍhajanapravṛttāṃ vittamayī dhanaprāyām / yasyāṃ sṛtau majjanti sīdanti bahavo 'neke mūḍhā manuṣyāḥ // KaUBh_2.3/1,2.3 //
body.translated_text: You, though repeatedly tempted by me, having contemplated — that is, reflected upon the faults of impermanence, insubstantiality, and the like — the dear ones such as sons and the desired objects characterized by <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) and similar [pleasures], O <s>Naciketas</s>, have relinquished them, have given them up, have abandoned them — how wondrous is your intelligence! You have not entered — have not attained — this chain, this path, this contemptible [way] trodden by the deluded, consisting mostly of wealth. In which path many — numerous — deluded mortals sink and perish. // KaUBh 2.3 //

children.text: dūram ete viparīte viṣūcī avidyā yā ca vidyeti jñātā /
children.translated_text: Far apart are these two, going in opposite directions — that which is known as <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and that which is known as <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge).

children.text: vidyābhīpsinaṃ naciketasaṃ manye na tvā kāmā bahavo 'lolupanta // KaU_2.4/1,2.4 //
children.translated_text: I consider <s>Naciketas</s> as one who desires <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge); the many desires did not distract you. // KaU 2.4 //

children.text: "tayoḥ, śreya ādadanasya sādhu bhavati hīyate 'rthādya u preyo vṛṇīte" (KaU 2.1)
children.translated_text: 'Of the two, for one who chooses the good (<s>śreyas</s>), it goes well; one who chooses the pleasant (<s>preyas</s>) falls from the true goal' (KaU 2.1)

children.text: ity uktaṃ tatkasmāt ? yato dūraṃ dūreṇa mahatāntareṇaite viparīta anyonyavyāvṛttarūpe vivekāvivekātmakatvāt tamaḥprakāśāv iva viṣūcī viṣūcyau nānāgatī bhinnaphale saṃsāramokṣahetutvenety etat / ke ta ity ucyate -- yā cāvidyā preyoviṣayā vidyeti ca śreyoviṣayā jñātā nirjñātāvagatā paṇḍitais tatra vidyābhīpsinaṃ vidyārthinaṃ naciketasaṃ tvām ahaṃ manye / kasmād yasmād avidvad buddhipralobhinaḥ kāmā apsaraḥprabhṛtayo bahavo 'pi tvā tvāṃ nālolupanta na vicchedaṃ kṛtavantaḥ śreyomārgād ātmopabhogābhivāñchāsampādanena / ato vidyārthinaṃ śreyobhājanaṃ manya ity abhiprāyaḥ // KaUBh_2.4/1,2.4 //
children.translated_text: — this was stated. Why? Because these two are far apart — separated by a great distance — of opposite nature, of mutually exclusive forms, being of the nature of discrimination and non-discrimination respectively, like darkness and light; going in different directions (<s>viṣūcī</s>), of different fruits, being respectively the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly bondage) and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — this is the meaning. What are they? — it is said: that which is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), pertaining to the pleasant (<s>preyas</s>), and that which is known as <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), pertaining to the good (<s>śreyas</s>) — known, ascertained, understood by the wise. Among these, I consider you, <s>Naciketas</s>, as one who desires <s>vidyā</s>, who seeks knowledge. Why? Because the many desires — <s>apsarases</s> and other [pleasures] — that tempt the intellects of the ignorant, have not distracted you, have not caused a break from the path of the good by producing a desire for self-enjoyment. Therefore, I consider [you] as one who seeks knowledge, as a vessel for the good — this is the purport. // KaUBh 2.4 //

children.text: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃ manyamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Abiding in the midst of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), [yet] regarding themselves as wise and learned,

children.text: dandramyamāṇāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ // KaU_2.5/1,2.5 //
children.translated_text: the deluded go about staggering, led as if by the blind, like the blind [themselves]. // KaU 2.5 //

body.text: ye tu saṃsārabhājo janā avidyāyām antare madhye ghanībhūta iva tamasi vartamānā veṣṭyamānāḥ putrapaśvāditṛṣṇāpāśaśataiḥ, svayaṃ dhīrāḥ prajñāvantaḥ paṇḍitāḥ śāstrakuśalaś ceti manyamānās te dandramyamāṇā atyarthaṃ kuṭilām anekarūpāṃ gatiṃ gacchanto jarāmaraṇarogādiduḥkhaiḥ pariyanti parigacchanti mūḍhā avivekino 'ndhenaiva dṛṣṭivihīnenaiva nīyamānā viṣame pathi yathā bahavondhā mahāntam anartham ṛcchanti tadvat // KaUBh_2.5/1,2.5 //
body.translated_text: But those people who are destined for <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), abiding in the midst — as if in dense darkness — of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), being entangled by hundreds of nooses of craving for sons, cattle, and the like; regarding themselves as wise, intelligent, learned, and proficient in scriptures — they, staggering, going along exceedingly crooked and manifold paths, afflicted by the sufferings of old age, death, disease, and the like, go about — traverse [<s>saṃsāra</s>] — deluded, lacking discrimination, being led by the blind — by one who is himself devoid of sight — on a perilous path, just as many blind people meet with great calamity — so too [these deluded ones]. // KaUBh 2.5 //

children.text: na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti bālaṃ pramādyantaṃ vittamohena mūḍham /
children.translated_text: The hereafter does not become apparent to the childish one, who is heedless and deluded by the infatuation of wealth.

children.text: ayaṃ loko nāsti para iti mānī punaḥ punar vaśam āpadyate me // KaU_2.6/1,2.6 //
children.translated_text: Thinking 'this world [alone exists], there is no other' — such a conceited one falls again and again under my power. // KaU 2.6 //

body.text: ata eva mūḍhatvān na sāmparāyaḥ pratibhāti / sampareyata iti sāmparāyaḥ paralokas tatprāptiprayojanaḥ sādhanaviśeṣaḥ śāstrīyaḥ sāmparāyaḥ sa ca bālam avivekinaṃ prati na pratibhāti na prakāśate nopatiṣṭhata ity etat / pramādyantaṃ pramādaṃ kurvantaṃ putrapaśvādiprayojaneṣv āsaktamanasaṃ tathā vittamohena vittanimittenāvivekena mūḍhaṃ tamasācchannam / sa tv ayam eva loko yo 'yaṃ dṛśyamānaḥ stryannapānādiviśiṣṭo nāsti paro 'dṛṣṭo loka ity evaṃ mananaśīlo mānī punaḥ punar janitvā vaśaṃ me 'dhīnatāmāpadyate mṛtyor mama jananamaraṇādilakṣaṇaduḥkhaprabandhārūḍha eva bhavatīty arthaḥ / prāyeṇa hy evaṃvidha eva lokaḥ // KaUBh_2.6/1,2.6 //
body.translated_text: Precisely because of being deluded, the hereafter does not become apparent. <s>Sāmparāya</s> means: that which is gone to — the other world; or the specific scriptural means whose purpose is the attainment of that [other world] — that <s>sāmparāya</s> does not become apparent to, does not shine forth for, does not present itself to the childish one — the undiscriminating person — this is the meaning. [He is] heedless — engaging in heedlessness, with a mind attached to purposes such as sons, cattle, and the like; likewise deluded by the infatuation of wealth — by the lack of discrimination caused by wealth, covered by darkness. He [thinks:] 'Only this world — this visible one, distinguished by women, food, drink, and the like — [exists]; there is no unseen other world' — having such a disposition, such a conceited one, again and again — being born repeatedly — falls under my power, under the subjection of <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) — meaning, he is indeed mounted upon the continuous stream of suffering characterized by birth, death, and the like. For the world is generally of this very nature. // KaUBh 2.6 //

children.text: śravaṇāyāpi bahubhir yo na labhyaḥ śṛṇvanto 'pi bahavo yaṃ na vidyuḥ /
children.translated_text: That [<s>Ātman</s>] which is not available even for hearing to many, which many, even hearing, do not know —

children.text: āścaryo vaktā kuśalo 'sya labdhā āścaryo jñātā kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ // KaU_2.7/1,2.7 //
children.translated_text: wonderful is the teacher [of it], skillful is the one who attains [it]; wonderful is the knower, instructed by the skillful. // KaU 2.7 //

body.text: yas tu śreyorthī sahasreṣu kaścid evātmavidbhavati tvad vidho yasmāc chravaṇāyāpi śravaṇārthaṃ śrotam api yo na labhya ātmā bahubhir anekaiḥ śṛṇvanto 'pi bahavo 'neke 'nye yam ātmānaṃ na vidyur na vidanty abhāgino 'saṃskṛtātmāno na vijānīyuḥ / kiñ cāsya vaktāpy āścaryo 'dbhutavad evānekeṣu kaścid eva bhavati / tathā śrutvāpy asyātmanaḥ kuśalo nipuṇa evānekeṣu labdhā kaścid eva bhavati / yasmād āścaryo jñātā kaścid eva kuśalānuśiṣṭaḥ kuśalena nipuṇenācāryeṇānuśiṣṭaḥ (saṃśikṣita ity adhyāhāryam) san // KaUBh_2.7/1,2.7 //
body.translated_text: But that rare seeker of the good who, among thousands, becomes a knower of the <s>Ātman</s> — one like you — because this <s>Ātman</s> is not available even for hearing — even for the purpose of hearing — to many, to numerous [people]; and many others — numerous — even hearing, do not know, do not understand this <s>Ātman</s> — being unfortunate, of uncultivated minds, they cannot comprehend [it]. Moreover, even the teacher of this [<s>Ātman</s>] is wonderful — like a marvel — among many, only some rare one exists. Similarly, even after hearing, a skillful — adept — attainer of this <s>Ātman</s> is only some rare one among many. Because the knower is wonderful — only some rare one — instructed by the skillful, by a proficient, expert teacher (the word 'trained' is to be supplied). // KaUBh 2.7 //

children.text: na nareṇāvareṇa prokta eṣa suvijñeyo bahudhā cintyamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: This [<s>Ātman</s>], when taught by an inferior person, is not easily known, though pondered upon in many ways.

children.text: ananyaprokte gatir atra nāsty aṇīyān hy atarkyam aṇupramāṇāt // KaU_2.8/1,2.8 //
children.translated_text: There is no access to it unless taught by another [who is one with it]; for it is subtler than the subtle, beyond reasoning. // KaU 2.8 //

body.text: kasmāt ? na hi nareṇa manuṣyeṇāvareṇa prokto 'vareṇa hīnena prakṛtabuddhinety etad ukta eṣa ātmā yaṃ tvaṃ māṃ pṛcchasi / na hi suṣṭhu samyag vijñeyo vijñātuṃ śakyo yasmād bahudhāsti nāsti kartākartā śuddho 'śuddha ity ādyanekadhā cintyamāno vādibhiḥ / kathaṃ punaḥ suvijñeya ity ucyate -- ananyaprokte 'nanyenāpṛthag darśinācāryeṇa pratipādyabrahmātmabhūtena prokta ukta ātmani gatir anekadhāstināstīty ādilakṣaṇā cintā gatir atrāsminn ātmani nāsti na vidyate sarvavikalpagatipratyastamitatvād ātmanaḥ / athavā svātmabhūte 'nanyasminn ātmani prokte 'nanyaprokte gatir atrānyāvagatir nāsti jñeyasyānyasyābhāvāt / jñānasya hy eṣā parā niṣṭhā yad ātmaikatvavijñānam / ato 'vagantavyābhāvān na gatir atrāvaśiṣyate, saṃsāragatir vātra nāsty ananya ātmani prokte nāntarīyakatvāt tadvijñānaphalasya mokṣasya / athavā procyamānabrahmātmabhūtenācāryeṇānanyatayā prokta ātmany agatir anavabodho 'parijñānam atra nāsti / bhavaty evāvagatis tadviṣayā śrotus tadananyo 'ham ity ācāryasyevety arthaḥ / evaṃ suvijñeya ātmāgamavatācāryeṇānanyatayā proktaḥ / itarathā hy aṇīyān aṇutaro 'ṇupramāṇād api sampadyata ātmā / atarkyam atarkyaḥ svabuddhyabhyūhena kevalena tarkeṇa / tarkyamāṇe 'ṇuparimāṇe kenacit sthāpita ātmani tato 'ṇutaram anyo 'bhyūhati, tato 'py anyo 'ṇutaram, iti na hi tarkasya niṣṭhā kvacid vidyate // KaUBh_2.8/1,2.8 //
body.translated_text: Why? For when taught by an inferior person — by a human being, by one who is inferior, of ordinary intelligence — this is what is meant — this <s>Ātman</s> about which you ask me is not well, not properly knowable — not capable of being known — because it is pondered upon in many ways by disputants — 'it exists,' 'it does not exist,' 'it is an agent,' 'it is not an agent,' 'it is pure,' 'it is impure,' and so on in manifold ways. How then is it properly knowable? — it is said: when taught as non-different [from the teacher] — when taught by a teacher who sees no difference, who has become one with the <s>Brahman</s>-<s>Ātman</s> that is to be taught — there is no <s>gati</s> (movement of thought) in this <s>Ātman</s> characterized by the manifold deliberation of 'it exists,' 'it does not exist,' and so on, because all alternative views are extinguished regarding the <s>Ātman</s>. Or alternatively: when the <s>Ātman</s>, which is non-different, which is one's own self, is taught — when it is 'taught as non-different' — there is no other understanding regarding it, because there is nothing else to be known. For the highest culmination of knowledge is the realization of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s>. Therefore, since there is nothing [else] to be understood, no further course remains. Or: when the <s>Ātman</s> is taught [as non-different from <s>Brahman</s>], there is no <s>saṃsāra-gati</s> (course of worldly existence), because <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which is the fruit of that knowledge, is not separate [from that teaching]. Or: when the <s>Ātman</s> is taught by a teacher who has become one with the <s>Brahman</s>-<s>Ātman</s> being expounded, as non-different — there is no non-comprehension, no failure of understanding regarding it. Understanding of that subject does indeed arise for the listener — [the understanding] 'I am not different from that' — just as for the teacher — this is the meaning. Thus the <s>Ātman</s> is properly knowable when taught as non-different by a teacher who possesses the [scriptural] tradition. Otherwise, the <s>Ātman</s> becomes subtler — more subtle — than even the atomic measure. It is beyond reasoning — beyond [mere] logical conjecture of one's own intellect alone. When the <s>Ātman</s> is established by someone as of atomic measure through reasoning, another conjectures it as subtler than that, and yet another as subtler still — for reasoning never reaches a conclusive end anywhere. // KaUBh 2.8 //

children.text: naiṣā tarkeṇa matir āpaneyā proktānyenaiva sujñānāya preṣṭha /
children.translated_text: This understanding is not to be attained by reasoning; [it is] taught by another [who is one with it] alone for true knowledge, O dearest one.

children.text: yāṃ tvam āpaḥ satyadhṛtir batāsi tvādṛṅ no bhūyān naciketaḥ preṣṭā // KaU_2.9/1,2.9 //
children.translated_text: Which you have attained, being of steadfast truth — O <s>Naciketas</s>, may there be more questioners like you, dear [to us]. // KaU 2.9 //

body.text: ato 'nanyaprokta ātmany utpannā yeyam āgamapratipādyātmamatir naiṣā tarkeṇa svabuddhyābhyūhamātreṇāpaneyā na prāpaṇīyety arthaḥ / nāpanetavyā vā, na hātavyā / tārkiko hy anāgam ajñaḥ svabuddhiparikalpitaṃ yat kiñcid eva kalpayati / ata eva ca yeyam āgamaprabhūtā matis tārkikād anyenaivāgamābhijñenācāryeṇaiva proktā satī sujñānāya bhavati he preṣṭha priyatama / kā punaḥ sā tarkāgamyā matir ity ucyate / yāṃ tvaṃ matiṃ madvarapradānenāpaḥ prāptavān asi / satyā avitathaviṣayā dhṛtir yasya tava sa tvaṃ satyadhṛtiḥ / batāsīty anukampayann āha mṛtyur naciketasaṃ vakṣyamāṇavijñānastutaye / tvādṛk tv atulyo no 'smabhyaṃ bhūyād bhavatādbhavatvanyaḥ putraḥ śiṣyo vā praṣṭā / kīdṛk ? yādṛktvaṃ he naciketaḥ praṣṭā // KaUBh_2.9/1,2.9 //
body.translated_text: Therefore, this understanding of the <s>Ātman</s> that arises in the <s>Ātman</s> taught as non-different [from <s>Brahman</s>] — which is to be conveyed by the <s>āgama</s> (scriptural tradition) — is not to be attained by reasoning, that is, not to be reached by mere conjecture of one's own intellect — this is the meaning. Or: it is not to be taken away, not to be abandoned. For a logician who is without the tradition, who is ignorant, constructs whatever [theory] is fashioned by his own intellect alone. And therefore, this understanding that originates from the <s>āgama</s> (scripture), when taught by someone other than a [mere] logician — by a teacher who is versed in the <s>āgama</s> — becomes [the means] for true knowledge, O dearest one, O most beloved. What then is this understanding that is inaccessible to reasoning? — it is said: that understanding which you have attained through the boons I granted. [You are] of steadfast truth — [you whose] conviction is in the unfailing object — such are you. 'Alas!' — <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) says this with compassion toward <s>Naciketas</s>, in praise of the knowledge about to be expounded. May there be one like you — unequalled — for us, another son or student as a questioner. Of what kind? Like you, O <s>Naciketas</s>, as a questioner. // KaUBh 2.9 //

children.text: jānāmy ahaṃ śevadhir ity anityaṃ na hy adhruvaiḥ prāpyate hi dhruvaṃ tat /
children.translated_text: I know that what is called treasure is impermanent; for the permanent is not attained through impermanent [means].

children.text: tato mayā nāciketaś cito 'gnir anityair dravyaiḥ prāptavān asmi nityam // KaU_2.10/1,2.10 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire has been built by me with impermanent materials, [and yet] I have attained the eternal. // KaU 2.10 //
