body.text: punar api tuṣṭa āha -- jānāmy ahaṃ śevadhir nidhiḥ karmaphalalakṣaṇo nidhir iva prāthyata iti / asāv anityam anitya iti jānāmi / na hi yasmād anityair adhruvair yan nityaṃ dhruvaṃ tatprāpyate paramātmākhyaḥ śevadhiḥ / yas tv anityasukhātmakaḥ śevadhiḥ sa evānityair dravyaiḥ prāpyate hi yatas tatas tasmān mayā jānatāpi nityam anityasādhanaiḥ prāpyata iti nāciketaś cito 'gnir anityair dravyaiḥ paśvādibhiḥ svargasukhasādhanabhūto 'gnir nirvartita ity arthaḥ / tenāham adhikārāpanno nityaṃ yāmyaṃ sthānaṃ svargākhyaṃ nityam āpekṣikaṃ prāptavān asmi // KaUBh_2.10/1,2.10 //
body.translated_text: Again, being pleased, he [<s>Yama</s>] says: I know that the treasure (<s>śevadhi</s>) — the hoard characterized by the fruit of ritual action — is impermanent, like a treasure that is sought. I know it to be impermanent. For by impermanent, non-eternal [means], the eternal, the permanent — the treasure called the supreme Self — cannot be attained. But the treasure that consists of impermanent pleasure — that indeed is obtained through impermanent substances. Therefore, even though I, knowing [this], have [nevertheless] built the <s>Nāciketa</s> fire — [a fire] that is the means to heavenly pleasure, accomplished through impermanent substances such as animals — by that I, having qualified [myself], have attained the eternal abode of <s>Yama</s> called heaven — 'eternal' in a relative sense. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 2.10||

children.text: kāmasya āptiṃ jagataḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ krator anantyam abhayasya pāram /
children.translated_text: The fulfillment of desire, the foundation of the world, the endlessness of ritual action, the far shore of fearlessness,

children.text: stomamahad urugāyaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ dṛṣṭvā dhṛtyā dhīro naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ // KaU_2.11/1,2.11 //
children.translated_text: the great praise, the wide-extending [goal], the foundation — having seen [all this], you, O wise <s>Naciketas</s>, have firmly renounced [it all]. ||<s>KaU</s> 2.11||

body.text: tvaṃ tu kāmasyāptiṃ samāptim, atraiva hi sarve kāmāḥ parisamāptāḥ, jagataḥ sādhyātmādhibhūtādhidaivādeḥ pratiṣṭhāmāśrayaṃ sarvātmakatvāt, krator upāsanāyāḥ phalaṃ hairaṇyagarbhapadam anantyamānantyam / abhayasya ca pāraṃ parāṃ niṣṭhām / stomaṃ stutyaṃ mahadaṇimādyaiśvaryādyanekaguṇasaṃhatam, stomaṃ ca tanmahac ca niratiśayatvāt stomamahat / urugāyaṃ vistīrṇāṃ gatim / pratiṣṭhāṃ sthitim ātmano 'nuttamām api dṛṣṭvā dhṛtyā dhairyeṇa dhīge dhīmān san naciketo 'tyasrākṣīḥ param evākāṅkṣann atisṛṣṭvān asi sarvam etat saṃsārabhogajātam / aho batānuttamaguṇo 'si // KaUBh_2.11/1,2.11 //
body.translated_text: But you [have seen] the fulfillment (<s>āpti</s>), the complete attainment, of desire — for herein all desires are completely fulfilled; the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), the support of the world — both the subjective (<s>ādhyātma</s>), objective (<s>adhibhūta</s>), and divine (<s>adhidaiva</s>) — because it is the Self of all; the endlessness (<s>ānantya</s>) of ritual worship (<s>kratu</s>) — [i.e.,] the state of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> as its fruit; and the far shore, the ultimate ground of fearlessness. The praise (<s>stoma</s>), that which is praiseworthy, great — a mass of manifold qualities such as sovereignty comprising <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness) and the like — and since it is unsurpassable, [it is called] '<s>stoma-mahat</s>.' The wide-extending goal (<s>urugāya</s>), the vast destination. And the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), the supreme abiding of the Self — having seen even all this, with fortitude (<s>dhṛti</s>), with courage, O wise <s>Naciketas</s>, you have renounced (<s>atyasrākṣīḥ</s>) — desiring only the supreme, you have let go of all this, the entire mass of <s>saṃsāric</s> enjoyments. How extraordinary — you are of the highest qualities! ||<s>KaUBh</s> 2.11||

children.text: taṃ durdarśaṃ gūḍham anupraviṣṭaṃ guhāhitaṃ gahvareṣṭhaṃ purāṇam /
children.translated_text: That which is hard to see, hidden, entered into [the cave of the heart], placed in the secret depth, dwelling in the abyss, the ancient one —

children.text: adhyātmayogādhigamena devaṃ matvā dhīro harṣaśokau jahāti // KaU_2.12/1,2.12 //
children.translated_text: knowing that <s>Deva</s> (the luminous Self) through the discipline of inner contemplation (<s>adhyātma-yoga</s>), the wise one abandons both joy and sorrow. ||<s>KaU</s> 2.12||

body.text: yaṃ tvaṃ jñātum icchasy ātmānaṃ taṃ durdarśaṃ duḥkhena darśanam asyeti durdarśo 'tisūkṣmatvāt taṃ gūḍhaṃ gahanam, anupraviṣṭaṃ prākṛtaviṣayavikāravijñānaiḥ pracchannam ity etat / guhāhitaṃ guhāyāṃ buddhau sthitaṃ tatropalabhyamānatvāt / gahvareṣṭhaṃ gahvare viṣame 'nekānarthasaṅkaṭe tiṣṭhatīti gahvareṣṭham / yata evaṃ gūḍham anupraviṣṭo guhāhitaś cāto gahvareṣṭho 'to durdarśaḥ / taṃ purāṇaṃ purātanam adhyātmayogādhigamena viṣayebhyaḥ pratisaṃhṛtya cetasa ātmani samādhānam adhyātmayogas tasyādhigamas tena matvā devam ātmānaṃ dhīro harṣaśokāv ātmana utkarṣāpakarṣayor abhāvaj jahāti // KaUBh_2.12/1,2.12 //
body.translated_text: The Self that you wish to know — it is hard to see (<s>durdarśa</s>), because seeing it is difficult due to its extreme subtlety. It is hidden (<s>gūḍha</s>), concealed; 'entered into' (<s>anupraviṣṭa</s>) means covered over by the cognitions of the modifications of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and sense-objects — this is the meaning. 'Placed in the cave' (<s>guhāhita</s>) means situated in the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), since it is perceived there. 'Dwelling in the abyss' (<s>gahvareṣṭha</s>) — it dwells in what is difficult, uneven, a narrow defile of manifold miseries — hence <s>gahvareṣṭha</s>. Because it is thus hidden, entered into, and placed in the cave, therefore it dwells in the abyss, and therefore it is hard to see. That ancient (<s>purāṇa</s>) one — through <s>adhyātma-yoga</s>, the discipline of inner contemplation (<s>adhyātma-yoga-adhigama</s>): withdrawing the mind from sense-objects and establishing it in the Self — by knowing that luminous Self (<s>deva</s>) through this means, the wise one abandons both joy and sorrow, since there is no superiority or inferiority of the Self. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 2.12||

children.text: etac chrutvā saṃparigṛhya martyaḥ pravṛhya dharmyam aṇum etam āpya /
children.translated_text: Having heard this and fully grasped it, a mortal, drawing forth the subtle essence of <s>Dharma</s>, having attained it,

children.text: sa modate modanīyaṃ hi labdhvā vivṛtaṃ sadma naciketasaṃ manye // KaU_2.13/1,2.13 //
children.translated_text: he rejoices, for he has obtained what is worthy of rejoicing. The abode is open, I think, for <s>Naciketas</s>. ||<s>KaU</s> 2.13||

body.text: kiñ ca, etad ātmatattvaṃ yad ahaṃ vakṣyāmi tac chutvācāryaprasādāt samyag ātmabhāvena parigṛhyopādāya martyo maraṇadharmā dharmād anupetaṃ dharmyaṃ pravṛhyodyamya pṛthak kṛtya śarīrāder aṇuṃ sūkṣmam etam ātmānam āpya prāpya sa martyo vidvān modate modanīyaṃ harṣaṇīyam ātmānaṃ labdhvā / tad etad evaṃvidhaṃ brahma sadma bhavanaṃ naciketasaṃ tvāṃ pratyapāvṛtadvāraṃ vivṛtam abhimukhībhūtaṃ manye, mokṣārhaṃ tvāṃ manya ity abhiprāyaḥ // KaUBh_2.13/1,2.13 //
body.translated_text: Moreover, this truth of the Self which I shall declare — having heard it through the teacher's grace and having fully grasped and taken it up as one's own being, a mortal, one subject to death — having drawn forth (<s>pravṛhya</s>), i.e., having exerted effort and separated from the body and the rest, the subtle (<s>aṇu</s>) and fine Self — having attained (<s>āpya</s>) it, that learned mortal rejoices, having obtained the Self that is worthy of rejoicing. This <s>Brahman</s> of such a nature — this abode — is open (<s>vivṛta</s>), its doors turned toward you, O <s>Naciketas</s> — I think [you are] worthy of liberation; this is the purport. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 2.13||

children.text: anyatra dharmād anyatrādharmād anyatrāsmāt kṛtākṛtāt /
children.translated_text: Beyond <s>dharma</s>, beyond <s>adharma</s>, beyond this [realm of] what is done and not done,

children.text: anyatra bhūtāc ca bhavyāc ca yat tat paśyasi tad vada // KaU_2.14/1,2.14 //
children.translated_text: beyond the past and the future — tell me what you see [that is]. ||<s>KaU</s> 2.14||

body.text: etac chrutvā naciketāḥ punar āha -- yady ahaṃ yogyaḥ, prasannaś cāsi bhagavan māṃ prati, anyatra dharmāc chāstrīyād dharmānuṣṭhānāt tatphalāt tatkārakebhyaś ca pṛthag bhūtam ity arthaḥ / tathānyatrādharmād vihitākaraṇarūpāt pāpāt, tathānyatrāsmāt kṛtākṛtāt / kṛtaṃ kāryam akṛtaṃ kāraṇam asmād anyatra / kiñ cānyatra bhūtāc cātikrāntāt kālād bhavyāc ca bhaviṣyataś ca tathā vartamānāt / kālatrayeṇa yan na paricchidyata ity arthaḥ / yad īdṛśaṃ vastu sarvavyavahāragocarātītaṃ paśyasi jānāsi tadvada mahyam // KaUBh_2.14/1,2.14 //
body.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Naciketas</s> again says: If I am worthy and you are gracious toward me, O <s>Bhagavān</s> — [tell me] that which is beyond <s>dharma</s>, i.e., scriptural righteous conduct, its fruit, and its performers — meaning, something distinct from all these. Likewise beyond <s>adharma</s>, i.e., the sin of not doing what is enjoined. And beyond this [world of] what is done and not done (<s>kṛtākṛta</s>) — '<s>kṛta</s>' is the effect, '<s>akṛta</s>' is the cause — beyond this. Moreover, beyond the past (<s>bhūta</s>), i.e., the elapsed time, and beyond the future (<s>bhavya</s>), and likewise beyond the present. That which is not delimited by the three times — this is the meaning. Whatever reality of such a nature transcends the entire domain of worldly transactions — [whatever] you see, i.e., know — tell it to me! ||<s>KaUBh</s> 2.14||

children.text: sarve vedā yat padam āmananti tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yad vadanti /
children.translated_text: The goal which all the <s>Vedas</s> declare, which all <s>tapas</s> (austerities) proclaim,

children.text: yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ caranti tat te padaṃ saṃgraheṇa bravīmy om ity etat // KaU_2.15/1,2.15 //
children.translated_text: desiring which they practice <s>brahmacarya</s> — that goal I tell you briefly: it is Oṃ. ||<s>KaU</s> 2.15||

body.text: ity evaṃ pṛṣṭavate mṛtyur uvāca pṛṣṭaṃ vastu viśeṣaṇāntaraṃ ca vivakṣan -- sarve vedā yat padaṃ padanīyaṃ gamanīyam avibhāgenāvirodhenāmananti pratipādayanti, tapāṃsi sarvāṇi ca yad vadanti yat prāptyarthānīty arthaḥ / yad icchanto brahmacaryaṃ gurukulavāsalakṣaṇam anyad vā brahmaprāptyarthaṃ caranti, tat te tubhyaṃ padaṃ yaj jñātum icchasi saṅgraheṇa saṅkṣepato bravīmi, om ity etat / tad etat padaṃ yad bubhutsitaṃ tvayā / yad etad om ity oṃ śabdavācyam oṃ śabdapratīkaṃ ca // KaUBh_2.15/1,2.15 //
body.translated_text: To the one who has thus asked, Death spoke, wishing to describe the object asked about and an additional characteristic of it: The goal (<s>pada</s>) — that which is to be reached, to be attained — which all the <s>Vedas</s> unanimously and consistently declare, i.e., set forth; and which all austerities proclaim — meaning, they are for the purpose of attaining that; desiring which they practice <s>brahmacarya</s> — dwelling in the teacher's house as students, or other [practices] for the attainment of <s>Brahman</s> — that goal which you wish to know, I tell you briefly, in summary: it is Oṃ. This goal which you wish to ascertain — this very thing is what the syllable Oṃ denotes, and Oṃ is its symbol (<s>pratīka</s>). ||<s>KaUBh</s> 2.15||

children.text: etad dhy evākṣaraṃ brahma etad dhy evākṣaraṃ param /
children.translated_text: This syllable indeed is <s>Brahman</s>; this syllable indeed is the supreme.

children.text: etad dhy evākṣaraṃ jñātvā yo yad icchati tasya tat // KaU_2.16/1,2.16 //
children.translated_text: Having known this syllable, whatever one desires, that is his. ||<s>KaU</s> 2.16||

body.text: ata etad dhy evākṣaraṃ brahmāparam etad dhy evākṣaraṃ paraṃ ca / tayor hi pratīkam etad akṣaram / etad dhy evākṣaraṃ jñātvopāsya brahmeti, yo yad icchati paramaparaṃ vā tasya tad bhavati / paraṃ cej jñātavyam aparaṃ cet prāptavyam // KaUBh_2.16/1,2.16 //
body.translated_text: Therefore this syllable is indeed the lower <s>Brahman</s>; this syllable is indeed also the supreme. For this syllable is the symbol of both. Having known this syllable — meditating upon it as <s>Brahman</s> — whatever one desires, whether the supreme or the lower, that becomes his. If the supreme is [desired], it is to be known [directly]; if the lower, it is to be attained [through meditation]. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 2.16||

children.text: etad ālambanaṃ śreṣṭham etad ālambanaṃ param /
children.translated_text: This is the best support; this is the supreme support.

children.text: etad ālambanaṃ jñātvā brahmaloke mahīyate // KaU_2.17/1,2.17 //
children.translated_text: Having known this support, one is glorified in the world of <s>Brahman</s>. ||<s>KaU</s> 2.17||

body.text: yata evam ata eva etad ālambanaṃ brahmaprāptyālambanānāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ praśasyatamam / etad ālambanaṃ paramaparaṃ ca parāparabrahmaviṣayatvāt / etad ālambanaṃ jñātvā brahmaloke mahīyate / parasmin brahmaṇy aparasmiṃś ca brahmabhūto brahmavad upāsyo bhavatīty arthaḥ // KaUBh_2.17/1,2.17 //
body.translated_text: Since this is so, therefore this support — among all supports for attaining <s>Brahman</s> — is the best (<s>śreṣṭha</s>), the most excellent. This support is both supreme and lower, since it pertains to both the higher and lower <s>Brahman</s>. Having known this support, one is glorified in the world of <s>Brahman</s> — in the supreme <s>Brahman</s> and in the lower <s>Brahman</s>; having become <s>Brahman</s>, one becomes worthy of worship like <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 2.17||

children.text: "anyatra dharmāt" (KaU 2.15)
children.translated_text: By '<s>anyatra dharmāt</s>' (<s>KaU</s> 2.14)

children.text: ity ādinā pṛṣṭasyātmano 'śeṣaviśeṣarahitasyālambanatvena pratīkatvena coṅkāro nirdiṣṭaḥ / aparasya ca brahmaṇo mandamadhyamapratipattṝn prati // athedānīṃ tasyoṅkārālambanasyātmanaḥ sākṣāt svarūpanirdidhārayiṣayedam ucyate --
children.translated_text: and so on, Oṃkāra has been indicated as the support and symbol of the Self that was asked about — devoid of all particular characteristics. And [this was taught] for the sake of those of dull and middling understanding, with respect to the lower <s>Brahman</s>. Now, with the desire to point directly to the own nature of that Self which has Oṃkāra as its support, this is stated:

children.text: na jāyate mriyate vā vipaścin nāyaṃ kutaścin na babhūva kaścit /
children.translated_text: The wise one is neither born nor dies; it did not come from anywhere, nor did anything come from it.

children.text: ajo nityaḥ śāśvato 'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre // KaU_2.18/1,2.18 //
children.translated_text: Unborn, eternal, everlasting, this ancient one is not killed when the body is killed. ||<s>KaU</s> 2.18||

body.text: na jāyate notpadyate mriyate vā na mriyate cotpattimato vastuno 'nityasyānekā vikriyās tāsām ādyante janmavināśalakṣaṇe vikriya ihātmani pratiṣidhyete prathamaṃ sarvavikriyāpratiṣedhārthaṃ na jāyate mriyate veti / vipaścinmedhāvī, avipariluptacaitanyasvabhāvāt / kiñ ca nāyam ātmā kutaścit kāraṇāntarād babhūva na prabhūtaḥ / asmāc cātmano na babhūva kaścid arthāntarabhūtaḥ / ato 'yam ātmājo nityaḥ śāśvato 'pakṣayavivarjitaḥ / yo hy aśāśvataḥ so 'pakṣīyate, ayaṃ tu śāśvato 'ta eva purāṇaḥ purāpi nava eveti / yo hy avayavopacayadvāreṇābhinirvartyate sa idānīṃ navo yathāṅkarādis tadviparītas tv ātmā purāṇo vṛddhivivarjita ity arthaḥ / yata evam ato na hanyate na hiṃsyate hanyamāne śastrādibhiḥ śarīre / tatstho 'py ākāśavad eva // KaUBh_2.18/1,2.18 //
body.translated_text: 'Is not born' — is not produced; 'nor does it die' — nor is it destroyed. For an entity that has origination and is impermanent has manifold modifications; of these, the first and last — characterized as birth and destruction — are here negated of the Self first, with the purpose of negating all modifications: 'is not born, nor dies.' '<s>Vipaścit</s>' means wise, intelligent — because the nature of consciousness is never lost. Moreover, this Self did not come into being (<s>babhūva</s>) from any other cause; and from this Self, no other thing came into being. Therefore this Self is unborn (<s>aja</s>), eternal (<s>nitya</s>), everlasting (<s>śāśvata</s>) — free from diminution. For that which is not everlasting undergoes diminution; but this is everlasting, and therefore ancient (<s>purāṇa</s>) — even of old it is ever new. For that which is produced through the accumulation of parts — like a sprout — is new at present; but the Self, being the opposite of that, is ancient, meaning free from growth. Since this is so, therefore it is not killed, not destroyed, when the body is killed by weapons and the like — though situated in [the body], it is like space. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 2.18||

children.text: hantā cen manyate hantuṃ hataś cen manyate hatam /
children.translated_text: If the slayer thinks he slays, and if the slain thinks he is slain —

children.text: ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate // KaU_2.19/1,2.19 //
children.translated_text: Neither of the two understands — this [<s>Ātman</s>] neither slays nor is slain. (<s>KaU</s> 2.19)

body.text: evaṃ bhūtam apy ātmānaṃ śarīramātrātmadṛṣṭir hantā ced yadi manyate cintayati hantuṃ haniṣyāmy enam iti yo 'py anyo hataḥ so 'pi cen manyate hatam ātmānaṃ hato 'ham ity ubhāv api tau na vijānītaḥ svam ātmānam, yato nāyaṃ hanty avikriyatvād ātmanas tathā na hanyata ākāśavad avikriyatvād eva / ato 'nātmajñaviṣaya eva dharmādharmādilakṣaṇaḥ saṃsāro nātmajñasya śrutiprāmāṇyānnyāyāccadharmādharmādyanupapatteḥ // KaUBh_2.19/1,2.19 //
body.translated_text: Even though the <s>Ātman</s> is of such a nature, if one whose vision of the self is confined to the body alone thinks 'I am the slayer,' imagining 'I shall kill him' — and if another [who is] killed also thinks 'I am killed, the <s>Ātman</s> is slain' — both of those do not know their own <s>Ātman</s>, because this [<s>Ātman</s>] does not slay, owing to the changeless nature of the <s>Ātman</s>...

children.text: aṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān ātmāsya jantor nihito guhāyām /
children.translated_text: Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great — the <s>Ātman</s> is hidden in the cave [of the heart] of this living being.

children.text: tam akratuḥ paśyati vītaśoko dhātuprasādān mahimānam ātmanaḥ // KaU_2.20/1,2.20 //
children.translated_text: One who is free from desire (<s>akratu</s>) sees that glory of the <s>Ātman</s>, free from sorrow, through the grace of the Creator (<s>dhātuprasāda</s>). (<s>KaU</s> 2.20)

body.text: kathaṃ punar ātmānaṃ jānātīty ucyate -- aṇoḥ sūkṣmād aṇīyāñ śyāmākāder aṇutaraḥ / mahato mahatparimāṇān mahīyān mahattaraḥ pṛthivyādeḥ / aṇu mahad vā yad asti loke vastu tat tenaivātmanā nityenātmavat sambhavati / tad ātmanā vinirmuktam asat sampadyate / tasmād asāv evātmāṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān sarvanāmarūpavastūpādhikatvāt / sa cātmāsya jantor brahmādistambaparyantasya prāṇijātasya guhāyāṃ hṛdaye nihita ātmabhṛtaḥ sthita ity arthaḥ / tam ātmānaṃ darśanaśravaṇamananavijñānaliṅgam akratur akāmo, dṛṣṭādṛṣṭabāhyaviṣayoparatabuddhir ity arthaḥ / yadā caivaṃ tadā mana ādīni karaṇāni dhātavaḥ śarīrasya dhāraṇāt prasīdantīty eṣāṃ dhātūnāṃ prasādād ātmano mahimānaṃ karmanimittavṛddhikṣayarahitaṃ paśyaty ayam aham asmīti, sākṣād vijānāti / tato vītaśoko bhavati // KaUBh_2.20/1,2.20 //
body.translated_text: But how does one know the <s>Ātman</s>? This is stated: subtler than the subtle — more minute than <s>śyāmāka</s> grain and other fine things; greater than the great — larger than that which is of great dimension, such as the earth and the like. Whatever entity in the world is minute or great, that exists by virtue of this very eternal <s>Ātman</s> as its self. That [entity], separated from the <s>Ātman</s>, reaching non-existence...

body.text: anyathā durvijñeyo 'yam ātmā kāmibhiḥ prākṛtapuruṣaiḥ, yasmāt
body.translated_text: Otherwise, this <s>Ātman</s> is difficult to know for desiring persons, i.e., ordinary people, because —

children.text: āsīno dūraṃ vrajati śayāno yāti sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Seated, it travels far; lying down, it goes everywhere.

children.text: kas taṃ madāmadaṃ devaṃ mad anyo jñātum arhati // KaU_2.21/1,2.21 //
children.translated_text: Who, other than me, is able to know that god who is both joyous and joyless? (<s>KaU</s> 2.21)

body.text: āsīno 'vasthito 'cala eva san dūraṃ vrajati śayāno yāti sarvataḥ, evam asāv ātmā devo madāmadaḥ samado 'madaś ca saharṣo 'harṣaś ca viruddhadharmavān ato 'śakyatvāj jñātuṃ kas taṃ madāmadaṃ devaṃ madanyo jñātum arhati / asmadāder eva sūkṣmabuddheḥ paṇḍitasya vijñeyo 'yam ātmā sthitigatinityānityādiviruddhānekadharmopādhitvād viruddhadharmavān viśvarūpa iva cintāmaṇivat kasyacid avabhāsate / ato durvijñeyatvaṃ darśayati kas taṃ madanyo jñātum arhatīti / karaṇānām upaśamaḥ śayanaṃ karaṇajanitasyaikadeśavijñānasyopaśamaḥ śayānasya bhavati / yadā caivaṃ kevalasāmānyavijñānatvāt sarvato yātīva yadā viśeṣavijñānasthaḥ svena rūpeṇa sthita eva san mana ādigatiṣu tadupādhikatvād dūraṃ vrajatīva sa cehaiva vartate // KaUBh_2.21/1,2.21 //
body.translated_text: Seated, i.e., remaining, being motionless — it travels far; lying down, it goes everywhere. Thus, this <s>Ātman</s>, the <s>deva</s> (luminous one), is '<s>madāmada</s>' — both joyous and joyless, both exultant and non-exultant, possessing contradictory attributes. Therefore, because of [its] being impossible to know, who, other than me, is able to know that god who is both joyous and joyless? Only a person of subtle intellect, like us...

children.text: aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu anavastheṣv avasthitam /
children.translated_text: The bodiless [<s>Ātman</s>], established in bodies that are not stable,

children.text: mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati // KaU_2.22/1,2.22 //
children.translated_text: The wise one, having realized the great, all-pervading <s>Ātman</s>, does not grieve. (<s>KaU</s> 2.22)

body.text: tadvijñānāc ca śokātyaya ity api darśayati -- aśarīraḥ svena rūpeṇākāśakalpa ātmā tam aśarīraṃ śarīreṣu devapitṛmanuṣyādiśarīreṣv anavastheṣv avasthitir ahiteṣv anityeṣv avasthitaṃ nityam avikṛtam ity etat / mahāntaṃ mahattvasyopekṣikatvasaṅkāyām āha vibhuṃ vyāpinam ātmānam / ātmagrahaṇaṃ svato 'nanyatvapradarśanārtham / ātmaśabdaḥ pratyagātmaviṣaya eva mukhyas tam īdṛśam ātmānaṃ matvāyam aham iti, dhīro dhīmān na śocati / na hy evaṃvidhasyātmavidaḥ śokopapattiḥ // KaUBh_2.22/1,2.22 //
body.translated_text: And he shows that from the knowledge of that [<s>Ātman</s>], sorrow is transcended: the <s>Ātman</s>, by its own nature like space, is bodiless (<s>aśarīra</s>); [yet] that bodiless [<s>Ātman</s>] is established in bodies — bodies of gods, ancestors, humans, and the like — which are unstable, i.e., not fixed, impermanent — [yet it is] established as eternal, unchanging. This is the meaning. [Regarding] 'great' (<s>mahānta</s>) — lest there be the suspicion of mere indifference [toward a vast entity], he says...

children.text: nāyam ātmā pravacanena labhyo na medhayā na bahunā śrutena /
children.translated_text: This <s>Ātman</s> is not attained through discourse, nor through intellect, nor through much learning.

children.text: yam evaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyas tasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute tanūṃ svām // KaU_2.23/1,2.23 //
children.translated_text: It is attained only by the one whom it chooses; to that one, this <s>Ātman</s> reveals its own form. (<s>KaU</s> 2.23)

body.text: yady api durvijñeyo 'yam ātmā tathāpy upāyena suvijñeya evety āha nāyam ātmā pravacanenānekavedasvīkaraṇena labhyo jñeyo, nāpi medhayā granthārthadhāraṇaśaktyā, na bahunā śrutena kevalena / kena tarhi labhya ity ucyate -- yam eva svātmānam eṣa sādhako vṛṇute prārthayate tenaivātmanā varitrā svayam ātmā labhyo jñāyata ity etat / niṣkāmaś cātmānam eva prārthayate, ātmanaivātmā labhyata ity arthaḥ / kathaṃ labhyata ity ucyate -- tasyātmakāmasyaiṣa ātmā vivṛṇute prakāśayati pāramārthikīṃ tanūṃ svāṃ svakīyāṃ svayāthātmyam ity arthaḥ // KaUBh_2.23/1,2.23 //
body.translated_text: Although this <s>Ātman</s> is difficult to know, nevertheless it is easily knowable through the [right] means — thus he says: This <s>Ātman</s> is not attainable, i.e., not knowable, through discourse (<s>pravacana</s>), i.e., through the mastery of many <s>Vedas</s>; nor through intellect (<s>medhā</s>), i.e., the capacity to retain the meaning of texts; nor through much hearing (<s>śruta</s>) alone. By what then is it attainable? This is stated: The one whom this seeker...

children.text: nāvirato duścaritān nāśānto nāsamāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who has not turned away from bad conduct, who is not tranquil, who is not concentrated,

children.text: nāśāntamānaso vāpi prajñānenainam āpnuyāt // KaU_2.24/1,2.24 //
children.translated_text: Nor one whose mind is not at peace — even he cannot attain this [<s>Ātman</s>] through knowledge. (<s>KaU</s> 2.24)

body.text: kiñ cānyat / na duścaritāt pratiṣiddhāc chrutismṛtyavihitāt pāpakarmaṇo 'virato 'nuparataḥ / nāpīndriyalaulyād aśānto 'nuparataḥ / nāpy asamāhito 'nekāgramanā vikṣiptacittaḥ / samāhitacitto 'pi san samādhānaphalārthitvān nāpy aśāntamānaso vyāpṛtacitto vā / prajñānena brahmavijñānenainaṃ prakṛtam ātmānam āpnuyāt / yas tu duścaritād virata indriyalaulyāc ca, samāhitacittaḥ samādhānaphalād apy upaśāntamānasaś cācāryavān prajñānena yathoktam ātmānaṃ prāpnotīty arthaḥ // KaUBh_2.24/1,2.24 //
body.translated_text: Moreover: one who has not ceased (<s>avirata</s>), i.e., not desisted, from bad conduct — sinful action prohibited by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> and not enjoined [by them]. Nor one who is not tranquil (<s>aśānta</s>), i.e., not desisted from the restlessness of the senses. Nor one who is not concentrated (<s>asamāhita</s>), i.e., whose mind is not one-pointed, whose consciousness is scattered. Even one whose mind is concentrated, if he seeks the fruit of concentration — nor one whose mind is not at peace (<s>aśāntamānasa</s>), i.e., whose consciousness is occupied...

children.text: yasya brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca ubhe bhavata odanaḥ /
children.translated_text: For whom <s>Brahman</s> [the priestly class] and <s>Kṣatra</s> [the warrior class] both become food,

children.text: mṛtyur yasyopasecanaṃ ka itthā veda yatra saḥ // KaU_2.25/1,2.25 //
children.translated_text: And death is but a condiment — who can know where that [<s>Ātman</s>] is? (<s>KaU</s> 2.25)

body.text: iti kāṭhakopaniṣadi iti dvitīyā vallī // 2 //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the second <s>vallī</s> in the <s>Kāṭhakopaniṣad</s>. (2)

body.text: yas tv anevaṃ bhūtaḥ -- yasyātmano brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca brahmakṣatre sarvadharmavidhāraka api sarvatrāṇabhūta ubha ādano 'śanaṃ bhavataḥ syātām / sarvaharo 'pi mṛtyur yasyopasecanam ivaudanasya, aśanatve 'py aparyāptaḥ, taṃ prākṛtabuddhir yathoktasādhanarahitaḥ san ka itthā ittham evaṃ yathoktasādhanavānivety arthaḥ / veda vijānāti yatra sa ātmeti // KaUBh_2.25/1,2.25 //
body.translated_text: But one who is not of such [realized] nature — for whom the <s>Ātman</s>, for which <s>Brahman</s> (the priestly class) and <s>Kṣatra</s> (the warrior class) — which uphold all <s>dharmas</s> and are the protection of all — both become food, as it were. Even all-devouring Death (<s>mṛtyu</s>) is for it like a condiment (<s>upasecana</s>) to the rice — even in [its capacity of] devouring, insufficient [to exhaust it]. One of ordinary intellect [cannot know] where that [<s>Ātman</s>] is, [as described] through the aforementioned means...

body.text: iti kāṭhavallyāṃ dvitīyavallībhāṣyam // 2 //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the commentary on the second <s>vallī</s> of the <s>Kāṭhavallī</s>. (2)

children.text:
atha tṛtīyā vallī /
ṛtaṃ pibantau sukṛtasya loke guhāṃ praviṣṭau parame parārdhe /
chāyātapau brahmavido vadanti pañcāgnayo ye ca triṇāciketāḥ // KaU_3.1/1,3.1 //
children.translated_text:
Now the third <s>vallī</s>:
The two who drink <s>ṛta</s> (truth/order), in the world of good deeds, having entered the cave, in the highest abode —
those who know <s>Brahman</s> call them shadow and light, as do the householders of the five fires and those who have thrice built the <s>Nāciketa</s> [fire]. (<s>KaU</s> 3.1)

body.text: ṛtaṃ pibantāvityasyā vallyāḥ sambandhaḥ / vidyāvidye nānā viruddhaphale ity upanyaste, na tu saphale te yathāvan nirṇīte / tannirṇayārthā ratharūpakakalpanā, tathā ca pratipattisaukaryam / evaṃ ca prāptṛprāpyagantṛgantavyavivekārtharatharūpakadvārā dvāv ātmānāv upanyasyete -- ṛtaṃ satyam avaśyambhāvitvāt karmaphalaṃ pibantau / ekas tatra karmaphalaṃ pibati bhuṅkte netaras tathāpi pātṛsambandhāt pibantāv ity ucyate cchatrinyāyena / sukṛtasya svayaṅkṛtasya karmaṇa ṛtam iti pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ / loke 'smiñ śarīre / guhāṃ guhāyāṃ buddhau praviṣṭau / parame bāhyapuruṣākāśasaṃsthānāpekṣayā paramam / parārdhe parasya brahmaṇo 'rdhaṃ sthānaṃ parārdhaṃ hārdākāśam / tasmin hi paraṃ brahmopalabhyate / tatas tasmin parame parārdhe hārdākāśe praviṣṭāv ity arthaḥ / tau ca cchāyātapāv iva vilakṣanau saṃsāritvāsaṃsāritvena brahmavido vadanti kathayanti / na kevalam akarmiṇa eva vadanti / pañcāgnayo gṛhasthāḥ / ye ca triṇāciketāḥ, triḥ kṛtvo nāciketo 'gniś cito yais te triṇāciketāḥ // KaUBh_3.1/1,3.1 //
body.translated_text: The connection of this <s>vallī</s> [beginning with] '<s>ṛtaṃ pibantau</s>' [is as follows]: Knowledge and ignorance, having opposite fruits, were presented, but their respective fruits were not properly determined. For the purpose of that determination, the chariot-metaphor is devised, and thereby ease of understanding [is achieved]. Thus, through the chariot-metaphor [serving] to discriminate the attainer and the attainable, the goer and the goal...

children.text: yaḥ setur ījānānām akṣaraṃ brahma yat param /
children.translated_text: That which is the bridge for those who perform sacrifices, the imperishable <s>Brahman</s> which is the supreme,

children.text: abhayaṃ titīrṣatāṃ pāraṃ nāciketaṃ śakemahi // KaU_3.2/1,3.2 //
children.translated_text: the fearless [goal] for those who wish to cross to the far shore — may we be able to [know] the <s>Nāciketa</s> [fire].

body.text: yaḥ setuḥ setur iva setur ījānānāṃ yajamānānāṃ karmiṇāṃ duḥkhasantaraṇārthatvāt / nāciketaṃ nāciketo 'gnis tam, vayaṃ jñātuṃ cetuṃ ca śakemahi śaknuvantaḥ / kiñ ca yac cābhayaṃ bhayaśūnyaṃ saṃsārasya pāraṃ titīrṣatāṃ tartum icchatāṃ brahmavidāṃ yatparamāśrayam akṣaram ātmākhyaṃ brahma, tac ca jñātuṃ śakemahi / parāpare brahmaṇī karmibrahmavidāśraye veditavye iti vākyārthaḥ / etayor eva hy upanyāsaḥ kṛta

children.text: "ṛtaṃ pibantau" (KaU 3.1)
children.translated_text: "<s>ṛtaṃ pibantau</s>" (<s>KaU</s> 3.1)
[the verse] thus.

body.translated_text: That which is a <s>setu</s> (bridge) — like a bridge — for the <s>ījānāḥ</s> (those who perform sacrifices), the <s>yajamānāḥ</s> (sacrificers), the performers of <s>karma</s>, because it serves the purpose of crossing over suffering. The <s>Nāciketa</s> [fire] — the fire called <s>Nāciketa</s> — that, may we be able to know and to attain. Moreover, that which is <s>abhaya</s> (fearless), devoid of fear, the ultimate refuge for those who wish to cross, who desire to traverse, the far shore of <s>saṃsāra</s> — the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> — the imperishable <s>Brahman</s> called the <s>Ātman</s>, that too may we be able to know. The meaning of the sentence is that both the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s> — the refuges of the performers of <s>karma</s> and the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> respectively — are to be known. For the presentation of these very two has been made in

children.text: ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ ratham eva tu /
children.translated_text: Know the Self as the rider of the chariot, and the body as the chariot itself.

children.text: buddhiṃ tu sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragraham eva ca // KaU_3.3/1,3.3 //
children.translated_text: Know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins.

body.text: tatra ya upādhikṛtaḥ saṃsārī vidyāvidyāyor adhikṛto mokṣagamanāya saṃsāragamanāya ca, tasya tadubhayagamane sādhano rathaḥ kalpyate / tatrātmānam ṛtapaṃ saṃsāriṇaṃ rathinaṃ rathasvāminaṃ viddhi jānīhi / śarīraṃ ratham eva tu rathabaddhahayasthānīyair indriyair ākṛṣyamāṇatvāc charīrasya / buddhiṃ tv adhyavasāyalakṣaṇāṃ sārathiṃ viddhi, buddhinetṛpradhānatvāc charīrasya sārathinetṛpradhāna iva rathaḥ / sarvaṃ hi dehagataṃ kāryaṃ buddhikartavyam eva prāyeṇa / manaḥ saṃkalpavikalpādilakṣaṇaṃ pragrahaṃ raśanāṃ viddhi / manasā hi pragṛhītāni śrotrādīni karaṇāni pravartante raśanayevāśvāḥ // KaUBh_3.3/1,3.3 //
body.translated_text: Therein, one who is conditioned by <s>upādhi</s> (limiting adjuncts), a being in <s>saṃsāra</s>, qualified for both <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), for the journey toward <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) and for the journey through <s>saṃsāra</s> — for his traveling on both those paths, a chariot is figuratively conceived as the means. Therein, know the <s>Ātman</s>, the individual soul in <s>saṃsāra</s>, as the <s>rathin</s> (chariot-rider), the owner of the chariot. Know the body as the chariot itself, because the body is drawn by the senses which occupy the position of horses yoked to a chariot. Know the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), characterized by determination, as the charioteer, because the body is principally guided by the intellect, just as a chariot is principally guided by a charioteer. For indeed, virtually all activity pertaining to the body is to be accomplished by the intellect alone. Know the <s>manas</s> (mind), characterized by volition, deliberation, and the like, as the reins. For the organs such as hearing and others, when grasped by the mind, function — just as horses [function when controlled] by reins.

children.text: indriyāṇi hayān āhur viṣayāṃs teṣu gocarān /
children.translated_text: They call the senses the horses, and the sense-objects their paths.

children.text: ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ bhoktety āhur manīṣiṇaḥ // KaU_3.4/1,3.4 //
children.translated_text: The wise call the Self, conjoined with the senses and mind, the enjoyer.

body.text: indriyāṇi cakṣurādīni hayān āhū rathakalpanākuśalāḥ, śarīrasthākarṣaṇasāmānyāt / teṣv evendriyeṣu hayatvena parikalpiteṣu gocarān mārgān rūpādīn viṣayān viddhi / ātmendriyamanoyuktaṃ śarīrendriyamanobhiḥ sahitaṃ saṃyuktam ātmānaṃ bhokteti saṃsārīty āhur manīṣiṇo vivekinaḥ / na hi kevalasyātmano bhoktṛtvam asti, buddhyādyupādhikṛtam eva tasya bhoktṛtvam / tathā ca śrutyantaraṃ kevalasyābhotṛtvam eva darśayati

children.text: "dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva" (BĀU 4,4.7)
children.translated_text: "It thinks, as it were; it moves, as it were" (<s>BĀU</s> 4.4.7)

children.text: ity ādi / evañ ca sati vakṣyamāṇarathakalpanayā vaiṣṇavasya padasyātmatayā pratipattir upapadyate, nānyathā svabhāvān atikramāt // KaUBh_3.4/1,3.4 //
children.translated_text: and so on. And this being so, through the chariot metaphor to be described, the comprehension of the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> station (the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) as one's own Self becomes appropriate, and not otherwise, since it would transgress the natural order.

body.translated_text: The senses — the eye and others — are called horses by those skilled in the chariot metaphor, because of the similarity of being drawn while stationed in the body. In those very senses, figuratively conceived as horses, know the <s>viṣayāḥ</s> (sense-objects) — forms and the like — as their paths. The Self conjoined, united with the body, senses, and mind — the wise, the discerning, call that Self the enjoyer, the being in <s>saṃsāra</s>. For the Self by itself does not have the nature of an enjoyer; its enjoyership is produced only through the conditioning adjuncts of <s>buddhi</s> and the rest. And another <s>śruti</s> (scripture) demonstrates that the Self by itself is not an enjoyer:

children.text: yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty ayuktena manasā sadā /
children.translated_text: But one who is without understanding, whose mind is always unrestrained —

children.text: tasyendriyāṇy avaśyāni duṣṭāśvā iva sāratheḥ // KaU_3.5/1,3.5 //
children.translated_text: his senses are uncontrollable, like the vicious horses of a charioteer.

body.text: tatraivaṃ sati yas tv avijñānavān yasya buddhyākhyaḥ sārathir avijñāno 'nipuṇo 'vivekī pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca bhavati, yathetaro rathacaryāyām ayuktenāpragṛhītenāsamāhitena manasā pragrahasthānīyena sadā yukto bhavati, tasyākuśalabuddhisārather indriyāṇy aśvasthānīyāny avaśyāny aśakyanivāraṇāni duṣṭāśvā adāntāśvā ivetarasārather bhavanti // KaUBh_3.5/1,3.5 //
body.translated_text: This being so, the one who is without understanding — whose charioteer called <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is without discernment, unskillful, undiscriminating with regard to both engagement and withdrawal — who is always yoked with an unrestrained, ungrasped, uncontrolled mind which occupies the position of the reins — the senses of that one, whose charioteer-intellect is unskillful, occupying the position of horses, are uncontrollable, impossible to restrain, like the vicious, untamed horses of an [unskillful] charioteer.

children.text: yas tu vijñānavān bhavati yuktena manasā sadā /
children.translated_text: But one who is possessed of understanding, whose mind is always restrained —

children.text: tasyendriyāṇi vaśyāni sadaśvā iva sāratheḥ // KaU_3.6/1,3.6 //
children.translated_text: his senses are controllable, like the good horses of a charioteer.

body.text: yas tu punaḥ pūrvoktaviparītasārathir bhavati vijñānavān pragṛhītamanāḥ samāhitacittaḥ sadā, tasyāśvasthānīyānīndriyāṇi pravartayituṃ nivartayituṃ vā śakyāni vaśyāni dāntāḥ sadaśvā ivetarasāratheḥ // KaUBh_3.6/1,3.6 //
body.translated_text: But one whose charioteer is the opposite of the one described before — who is possessed of understanding, whose mind is grasped, whose thought is always concentrated — his senses, occupying the position of horses, capable of being directed forward or restrained, are controllable, like the tamed, good horses of a [skillful] charioteer.

children.text: yas tv avijñānavān bhavaty amanaskaḥ sadāśuciḥ /
children.translated_text: But one who is without understanding, whose mind is uncontrolled, who is always impure —

children.text: na sa tat padam āpnoti saṃsāraṃ cādhigacchati // KaU_3.7/1,3.7 //
children.translated_text: he does not attain that state, and falls into <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth).

body.text: tasya pūrvoktasyāvijñānavata idaṃ phalam āha -- yas tv avijñānavān bhavati / amanasko 'pragṛhītamanaskaḥ sa tata evāśuciḥ sadaiva / na sa rathī tatpūrvoktam akṣaraṃ yatparaṃ padam āpnoti tena sārathinā / na kevalaṃ tan nāpnoti saṃsāraṃ ca janmamaraṇalakṣaṇam adhigacchati // KaUBh_3.7/1,3.7 //
body.translated_text: He states the result for the one described before who is without understanding: 'But one who is without understanding' — whose mind is uncontrolled, ungrasped — he is, for that very reason, always impure. That chariot-rider does not attain — through such a charioteer — the aforementioned imperishable supreme state. Not only does he not attain that, but he also falls into <s>saṃsāra</s>, characterized by birth and death.

children.text: yas tu vijñānavān bhavati samanaskaḥ sadā śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: But one who is possessed of understanding, whose mind is controlled, who is always pure —

children.text: sa tu tat padam āpnoti yasmād bhūyo na jāyate // KaU_3.8/1,3.8 //
children.translated_text: he indeed attains that state from which he is not born again.

body.text: yas tu dvitīyo vijñānavān vījñānavat sārathyupeto rathī vidvān ity etat / yuktamanāḥ samanaskaḥ sa tata eva sadā śuciḥ, sa tu tatpadam āpnoti, yasmād āptāt padād apracyutaḥ san bhūyaḥ punar na jāyate saṃsāre // KaUBh_3.8/1,3.8 //
body.translated_text: But the second one, who is possessed of understanding — that is, who has a charioteer endowed with discernment, a learned chariot-rider; this is the meaning. Having a controlled mind — <s>samanaskaḥ</s> — he is for that very reason always pure. He indeed attains that state, from which, having attained that state, being undeviated, he is not born again in <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: vijñānasārathir yas tu manaḥ pragrahavān naraḥ /
children.translated_text: The person who has understanding as his charioteer and who holds the reins of the mind —

children.text: so 'dhvanaḥ pāram āpnoti tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam // KaU_3.9/1,3.9 //
children.translated_text: he reaches the end of the journey: that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

body.text: kiṃ tatpadam ity āha vijñānasārathir yas tu yo vivekabuddhisārathiḥ pūrvokto manaḥpragrahavān pragṛhītamanāḥ samāhitacittaḥ sañ śucir naro vidvān so 'dhvanaḥ saṃsāragateḥ pāraṃ param evādhigantavyam ity etad āpnoti mucyate sarvasaṃsārabandhanaiḥ / tad viṣṇor vyāpanaśīlasya brahmaṇaḥ paramātmano vāsudevākhyasya paramaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ padaṃ sthānam, satattvaṃ ity etad yad asāv āpnoti vidvān // KaUBh_3.9/1,3.9 //
body.translated_text: What is that state? He says: the one who has understanding as his charioteer — the aforementioned one whose charioteer is the intellect of discrimination — who holds the reins of the mind, whose mind is grasped, whose thought is concentrated, being pure, that wise man reaches the end, the far shore of the journey of <s>saṃsāra</s> — that which is the ultimate [reality] to be attained; this is what he reaches. He is freed from all the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s>. That supreme, most excellent <s>pada</s> (abode) of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — of the all-pervading <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Paramātman</s> known as <s>Vāsudeva</s> — that abode, that reality of Being — this is what that wise one attains.

body.text: adhunā yatpadaṃ gantavyaṃ tasyendriyāṇi sthūlāny ārabhya sūkṣmatāratamyakrameṇa pratyagātmatayādhigamaḥ kartavya ity evam artham idam ārabhyate --
body.translated_text: Now, in order to show that the state to be reached should be comprehended as the innermost Self by proceeding from the gross senses in order of increasing subtlety, this [passage] is commenced:

children.text: indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā arthebhyaś ca paraṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Higher than the senses are the objects; higher than the objects is the mind.

children.text: manasas tu parā buddhir buddher ātmā mahān paraḥ // KaU_3.10/1,3.10 //
children.translated_text: Higher than the mind is the intellect; higher than the intellect is the great Self (<s>Mahān Ātmā</s>).

body.text: sthūlāni tāvad indriyāṇi, tāni yair arthair ātmaprakāśanāyārabdhāni tebhya indriyebhyaḥ svakāryebhyas te parā hy arthāḥ sūkṣmā mahāntaś ca pratyagātmabhūtāś ca / tebhyo 'py arthebhyaś ca paraṃ sūkṣmataraṃ mahatpratyagātmabhūtaṃ ca manaḥ / manaḥśabdavācyaṃ manasa ārambhakaṃ bhūtasūkṣmaṃ saṅkalpavikalpādyārambhakatvāt / manaso 'pi parā sūkṣmatarā mahattarā pratyagātmabhūtā ca buddhiḥ, buddhiśabdavācyām adhyavasāyādyārambhakaṃ bhūtasūkṣmam / uddher ātmā sarvaprāṇibuddhīnāṃ pratyagātmabhūtatvād ātmā mahān sarvamahattvād avyaktād yat prathamaṃ jātaṃ hairaṇyagarbhaṃ tattvaṃ bodhābodhātmakaṃ mahān ātmā buddheḥ param ity ucyate // KaUBh_3.10/1,3.10 //
body.translated_text: The senses are gross to begin with. Those objects for whose self-manifestation they were created — those objects are higher than the senses, their own effects, for they are subtler, greater, and more inward in nature. Higher, subtler, greater, and more inward than those objects too is the <s>manas</s> (mind). What is denoted by the word <s>manas</s> is the subtle element (<s>bhūtasūkṣma</s>) that gives rise to the mind, because it gives rise to volition, deliberation, and the like. Higher, subtler, greater, and more inward than the mind is the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect); what is denoted by the word <s>buddhi</s> is the subtle element that gives rise to determination and the like. The <s>Ātman</s> is the inner Self of the intellects of all living beings — because it is their innermost nature, it is called <s>Ātman</s>. <s>Mahān</s> (the Great) — because it is greater than everything, being the principle born first from the <s>Avyakta</s> (Unmanifest), the <s>Hairaṇyagarbha</s> (pertaining to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>) principle, consisting of both consciousness and unconsciousness — the <s>Mahān Ātmā</s> is said to be higher than the intellect.

children.text: mahataḥ param avyaktam avyaktāt puruṣaḥ paraḥ /
children.translated_text: Higher than the Great is the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>); higher than the Unmanifest is <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: puruśān na paraṃ kiṃcit sā kāṣṭhā sā parā gatiḥ // KaU_3.11/1,3.11 //
children.translated_text: Beyond <s>Puruṣa</s> there is nothing — that is the ultimate limit, that is the supreme goal.

body.text: mahato 'pi paraṃ sūkṣmataraṃ pratyagātmabhūtaṃ sarvamahattaraṃ cāvyaktaṃ sarvasya jagato bījabhūtam avyākṛtanāmarūpaṃ satattvaṃ sarvakāryakāraṇaśaktisamāhārarūpam avyaktam avyākṛtākāśādinām avācyaṃ paramātmany otaprotabhāvena samāśritaṃ vaṭakaṇikāyām iva vaṭavṛkṣaśaktiḥ / tasmād avyaktāt paraḥ sūkṣmataraḥ sarvakāraṇakāraṇatvāt pratyagātmatvāc ca mahāṃś ca, ata eva puruṣaḥ sarvapūraṇāt / tato 'nyasya parasya prasaṅgaṃ nivārayann āha -- puruṣān na paraṃ kiñcid iti / yasmān nāsti puruṣāc cinmātrāghanāt paraṃ kiñcid api vastvantaram, tasmāt sūkṣmatvamahattvapratyagātmatvānāṃ sā kāṣṭhā niṣṭhā paryavasānam / atra hīndriyebhya ārabhya sūkṣmatvādi parisamāptam / ata eva ca gantṝṇāṃ sarvagatimatāṃ saṃsāriṇāṃ sā parā prakṛṣṭā gatiḥ /

children.text: "yad gatvā na nivartante" (BhG 15.6)
children.translated_text: "from which they do not return" (<s>BhG</s> 15.6)

children.text: iti smṛteḥ // KaUBh_3.11/1,3.11 //
children.translated_text: — thus states the <s>Smṛti</s>.

body.translated_text: Higher even than the Great, subtler, more inward in nature, and greater than everything, is the <s>Avyakta</s> (Unmanifest) — the seed of the entire universe, whose name and form are undifferentiated, whose nature is Being, consisting of the aggregate of the powers of all effects and causes, unexpressed, indescribable [as] the unmanifest space and other [elements], resting upon the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) in a warp-and-woof fashion, like the power of a banyan tree within a banyan seed. Higher than that <s>Avyakta</s> is <s>Puruṣa</s> — subtler, because he is the cause of all causes, and because he is the innermost Self, and thus great; and for this very reason he is called <s>Puruṣa</s>, because he fills everything (<s>sarvapūraṇāt</s>). Forestalling the suggestion that there might be something else beyond, he says: beyond <s>Puruṣa</s> there is nothing whatsoever. Since there is not a single other entity beyond <s>Puruṣa</s>, who is pure concentrated consciousness, that is the <s>kāṣṭhā</s> (ultimate limit), the final terminus, the conclusion of subtlety, greatness, and inwardness beginning from the senses. For here, the [progression of] subtlety and the rest, beginning from the senses, reaches its completion. And for this very reason, for all travelers, for all beings in <s>saṃsāra</s> who possess [various] destinations, that is the supreme, the highest goal —

children.text: eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho 'tmā na prakāśate /
children.translated_text: This Self, hidden in all beings, does not shine forth.

children.text: dṛṣyate tv agryayā buddhyā sūkṣmayā sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ // KaU_3.12/1,3.12 //
children.translated_text: But it is seen by those of subtle vision, through the foremost, refined intellect. // KaU 3.12 //

body.text: nanu gatiś ced āgatyāpi bhavitavyam, kathaṃ

children.text: "yasmād bhūyo na jāyate" (KaU 3.8)
children.translated_text: 'from which one is not born again' (KaU 3.8)?

children.text: iti / naiṣa doṣaḥ / sarvasya pratyagātmatvād avagatir eva gatir ity upacaryate / pratyagātmatvañ ca darśitam indriyamanobuddhiparatvena / yo hi gantā so 'yam apratyagrūpaṃ gacchaty anātmabhūtaṃ na vindati svarūpeṇa / tathā ca śrutiḥ --
children.translated_text: This is not a fault. Because [the <s>Ātman</s>] is the innermost Self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) of all, realization (<s>avagati</s>) alone is figuratively called 'going' (<s>gati</s>). And the nature of the innermost Self has been shown through the ascending sequence of senses, mind, and intellect. For the one who 'goes' — he does not find, in his own essential nature, anything that is of the form of the non-inner, that is, of the nature of the non-Self. And thus the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) [states] —

children.text: "anadhvagā adhvasu pārayiṣṇavaḥ" (Itihāsa-Upaniṣad 18)
children.translated_text: 'Not travelers on a road, [yet] able to traverse the paths' (<s>Itihāsa-Upaniṣad</s> 18)

children.text: ity ādyā / tathā ca darśayati pratyagātmatvaṃ sarvasya / eṣa puruṣaḥ sarveṣu brahmādistambaparyanteṣu bhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ saṃvṛto darśanaśravaṇādikarmāvidyāmāyāc channo 'ta evātmā na prakāśata ātmatvena kasyacit / āho 'tigambhīrā duravagāhyā vicitrā ceyaṃ māyā, yad ayaṃ sarvo jantuḥ paramārthataḥ paramārthasatattvo 'py evaṃ bodhyamāno 'haṃ paramātmeti na gṛhṇāti, anātmānaṃ dehendriyādisaṅghātam ātmano dṛśyamānam api ghaṭādivad ātmatvenāham amuṣya putra ity anucyamāno 'pi gṛhṇāti / nūnaṃ parasyaiva māyayā momuhyamānaḥ sarvo loko bambhramīti / tathā ca smaraṇam
children.translated_text: — and other such [passages]. And thus [the <s>śruti</s>] shows the innermost-Self-nature of everything. This <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person) is hidden — concealed — in all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a clump of grass, covered by the <s>māyā</s> (illusion) of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) consisting of the activities of seeing, hearing, and the like. For this very reason, the <s>Ātman</s> does not shine forth as the Self of anyone. Ah, how exceedingly profound, unfathomable, and wondrous is this <s>māyā</s> (illusion)! For every living being, though in ultimate reality being of the nature of the supreme reality (<s>paramārthasatattva</s>), and though being thus instructed — 'I am the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self)' — does not grasp [this truth]; and though the non-Self — the aggregate of body, senses, and the like — is seen to be [separate from oneself] like a pot and the like, and though it is not even taught to be the Self, [yet one] grasps it as the Self — 'I am the son of so-and-so.' Surely, being deluded by the <s>māyā</s> of the Supreme alone, the entire world wanders about. And thus the <s>smṛti</s> (remembered scripture) [states] —

children.text: "nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ" (BhG 7.25)
children.translated_text: 'I am not manifest to all, being veiled by <s>Yogamāyā</s>' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 7.25)

children.text: ity ādi / nanu viruddham idam ucyate
children.translated_text: — and other such [passages]. Objection: But is this not contradictory — saying

children.text: "matvā dhīro na śocati" (KaU 2.22)
children.translated_text: 'knowing [it], the wise one does not grieve' (KaU 2.22)

children.text: "na prakāśate" (KaU 3.12)
children.translated_text: [and] 'does not shine forth' (KaU 3.12)?

children.text: iti ca / naitad evam / asaṃskṛtabuddher avijñeyatvān na prakāśata ity uktam / dṛśyate tu saṃskṛtayāgryayā agram ivāgryayā tayā, ekāgratayopetayety etat sūkṣmayā sūkṣmavastunirūpaṇaparayā / kaiḥ / sūkṣmadarśibhir indriyebhyaḥ parā hy arthā ity ādiprakāreṇa sūkṣmatāpāramparyadarśanena paraṃ sūkṣmaṃ draṣṭuṃ śīlaṃ yeṣāṃ te sūkṣmadarśinas taiḥ sūkṣmadarśibhiḥ paṇḍitair ity etat // KaUBh_3.12/1,3.12 //
children.translated_text: This is not so. It was said 'does not shine forth' because it is unknowable to one whose intellect is uncultivated. But it is seen — by means of a cultivated, foremost intellect — foremost meaning supreme, that is, endowed with one-pointedness — [and] subtle, devoted to the discernment of subtle realities. By whom? By those of subtle vision — those who, through the sequential vision of subtlety in the manner of 'the objects are beyond the senses' and so on, have the disposition to see the supremely subtle — by those subtle seers, that is, by the wise — this is the meaning. // KaUBh 3.12 //

body.translated_text: Objection: If there is a 'going' [to the <s>Ātman</s>], then there must also be a 'coming' [from it]; how then

children.text: yacched vāṅmanasī prājñas tad yacchej jñāna ātmani /
children.translated_text: The wise one should restrain speech in the mind; that [mind] he should restrain in the knowing Self (<s>jñāna ātman</s>).

children.text: jñānam ātmani mahati niyacchet tad yacchec chānta ātmani // KaU_3.13/1,3.13 //
children.translated_text: Knowledge he should restrain in the great Self (<s>mahat ātman</s>); that he should restrain in the peaceful Self (<s>śānta ātman</s>). // KaU 3.13 //

body.text: tatpratipattyupāyam āha yacchen niyacched upasaṃharet prājño vivekī / kim? vāgvācam / vāgatropalakṣaṇārthā sarveṣām indriyāṇām / kva? manasī / manasi chāndasaṃ dairghyam / tac ca mano yacchej jñāne prakāśasvarūpe buddhāv ātmani / buddhir hi mana ādikaraṇānyāpnotīty ātmā pratyak ca teṣām / jñānaṃ buddhim ātmani mahati prathamaje niyacchet / prathamajavat svacchasvabhāvakam ātmano vijñānam āpādayed ity arthaḥ / tañ ca mahāntam ātmānaṃ yacchec chānte sarvaviśeṣapratyastamitarūpe 'vikriye sarvāntare sarvabuddhipratyayasākṣiṇi mukhya ātmani // KaUBh_3.13/1,3.13 //
body.translated_text: [The <s>śruti</s>] states the means to that realization: the wise one, the discriminating person, should restrain — should withdraw. What? Speech — the word 'speech' here is representative of all the senses. Where? In the mind. The lengthening [of the vowel] in '<s>manasī</s>' is a Vedic irregularity. And that mind he should restrain in <s>jñāna</s> — in the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), whose nature is luminosity — in the Self (<s>ātman</s>). For the intellect encompasses the mind and other instruments, and is their inner Self. Knowledge — the intellect — he should restrain in the great Self (<s>mahat</s>), the firstborn. The meaning is: he should bring the cognition of the Self to a state as pure as that of the firstborn. And that great Self he should restrain in the peaceful [Self] — in that which is of the nature of the cessation of all distinctions, unchanging, innermost of all, the witness of all mental cognitions — in the principal <s>Ātman</s>. // KaUBh 3.13 //

children.text: uttiṣṭhata jāgrata prāpya varān nibodhata /
children.translated_text: Arise! Awake! Having obtained the excellent [teachers], understand!

children.text: kṣurasya dhārā niśitā duratyayā durgaṃ pathas tat kavayo vadanti // KaU_3.14/1,3.14 //
children.translated_text: The edge of a razor is sharp and difficult to cross — the wise declare that path to be impassable. // KaU 3.14 //

body.text: evaṃ puruṣa ātmani sarvaṃ pravilāpya nāmarūpakarmatrayaṃ yan mithyājñānavijṛmbhitaṃ kriyākārakaphalalakṣaṇaṃ svātmayāthātmyajñānena marīcyudakarajjusarpagaganamalānīva marīcirajjugaganasvarūpadarśanenaiva svasthaḥ praśāntaḥ kṛtakṛtyo bhavati yataḥ, atas taddarśanārtham anādyāprasuptā uttiṣṭhata he jantavaḥ, ātmajñānābhimukhā bhavata, jāgratājñānanidrāyā ghorarūpāyāḥ sarvānarthabījabhūtāyāḥ kṣayaṃ kuruta / katham / prāpyopagamya varān prakṛṣṭān ācāryāṃs tattvavidaḥ, tadupadiṣṭaṃ sarvāntaram ātmānam aham asmīti nibodhatāvagacchata / na hy upekṣatavyam iti śrutir anukampayāha mātṛvat / atisūkṣmabuddhiviṣayatvāj jñeyasya / kim iva sūkṣmabuddhir ity ucyate / kṣurasya dhārāgraṃ niśitā tīkṣṇīkṛtā duratyayā duḥkhenātyayo yasyāḥ sā duratyayā / yathā sā padbhyāṃ durgamanīyā tathā durgaṃ duḥsampādyam ity etat pathaḥ panthānaṃ tat taṃ jñānalakṣaṇaṃ mārgaṃ kavayo medhāvino vadanti / jñeyasyātisūkṣmatvāt tadviṣayasya jñānamārgasya duḥsampādyatvaṃ vadantīty abhiprāyaḥ // KaUBh_3.14/1,3.14 //
body.translated_text: Thus, having dissolved in the <s>Ātman</s> the entire triad of name, form, and action — which is the manifestation of false knowledge, characterized by action, agent, and fruit — through the knowledge of the true nature of one's own Self, just as [one dissolves] mirage-water, rope-snake, and sky-stain by seeing the true nature of the mirage, rope, and sky respectively — one becomes self-abiding, tranquil, and one who has accomplished all that is to be accomplished. Therefore, for the purpose of that vision, O beings, who have been asleep from beginningless time — arise! Become directed toward Self-knowledge! Awake — bring about the cessation of the sleep of ignorance, which is of a terrible nature and is the seed of all calamity! How? Having obtained — having approached — the excellent, the eminent teachers who know the truth, understand — comprehend — the <s>Ātman</s>, the innermost of all, as taught by them — [the understanding] 'I am that.' For this is not to be neglected — the <s>śruti</s> says this with compassion, like a mother. Because the object to be known is of exceedingly subtle intellectual scope. What is it like? — it is said: the edge of a razor — its sharpened tip — is sharp, honed, difficult to cross, hard to traverse. Just as that [edge] is difficult to walk upon, so too that path — the path characterized by knowledge — is difficult to accomplish — this is the meaning. The wise, the intelligent, declare this. The purport is: because the object to be known is exceedingly subtle, the path of knowledge pertaining to it is difficult to accomplish — so they say. // KaUBh 3.14 //

body.text: tatkatham atisūkṣmatvaṃ jñeyasyety ucyate / sthūlā tāvad iyaṃ medinī śabdasparśarūparasagandhopacitā sarvendriyaviṣayabhūtā tathā śarīram / tatraikaikaguṇāpakarṣeṇa gandhādīnāṃ sūkṣmatvamahattvaviśuddhatvanityatvāditāratamyaṃ dṛṣṭamabādiṣu yāvad ākāśam iti / te gandhādayaḥ sarva eva sthūlatvād vikārāḥ śabdāntā yatra na santi kim u tasya sūkṣmatvādiniratiśayatvaṃ vaktavyam ity etad darśayati śrutiḥ --
body.translated_text: How then is the object to be known exceedingly subtle? — this is stated. To begin with, this earth is gross, composed of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, being the object of all the senses; so too the body. Among these, by the successive removal of one quality each — of smell and the others — a gradation of increasing subtlety, greatness, purity, and permanence is observed in the water-element and others up to <s>ākāśa</s> (space). Those [qualities] — smell and the others — all being gross, are modifications ending with sound. Where these do not exist — what need is there to speak of its unsurpassed subtlety and the like? To show this, the <s>śruti</s> [states] —

children.text: aśabdam asparśam arūpam avyayaṃ tathārasaṃ nityam agandhavac ca yat /
children.translated_text: That which is without sound, without touch, without form, imperishable, likewise without taste, eternal, and without smell —

children.text: anādy anantaṃ mahataḥ paraṃ dhruvaṃ nicāyya tan mṛtyumukhāt pramucyate // KaU_3.15/1,3.15 //
children.translated_text: without beginning, without end, beyond the great (<s>mahat</s>), immutable — having discerned that, one is freed from the mouth of death. // KaU 3.15 //

body.text: aśabdam asparśam arūpam arasam agandhavac ca yad etad vyākhyātaṃ brahmāvyayaṃ yad dhi śabdādimattadvyetīdaṃ tv aśabdādimattvād avyayaṃ na vyeti na kṣīyate, ata eva ca nityam, yad dhi vyeti tad anityam idaṃ tu na vyety ato nityam / itaś ca nityam anādyavidyamāna ādiḥ kāraṇam asya tad idam anādi / yad dhy ādimattatkāryatvād anityaṃ kāraṇe pralīyate yathā pṛthivyādi / idaṃ tu sarvakāraṇatvād akāryam akāryatvān nityam, na tasya kāraṇam asti yasmin pralīyate / tathānantam avidyamāno 'ntaḥ kāryam asya tad anantam / yathā kadalyādeḥ phalādikāryotpādanenāpy anityatvaṃ dṛṣṭam, na ca tathāpy antavattvaṃ brahmaṇo 'to 'pi nityam / mahato mahattattvād buddhyākhyāt paraṃ vilakṣaṇaṃ nityavijñaptisvarūpatvāt sarvasākṣi hi sarvabhūtātmatvād brahma / uktaṃ hi

children.text: "eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu" (KaU 3.12)
children.translated_text: 'This [<s>Puruṣa</s>] in all beings' (KaU 3.12)

children.text: ity ādi / dhruvaṃ ca kūṭasthaṃ nityaṃ na pṛthivyādivad āpekṣikaṃ nityatvam / tad evambhūtaṃ brahmātmānaṃ nicāyyāvagamya tam ātmānaṃ mṛtyumukhān mṛtyugocarād avidyākāmakarmalakṣaṇāt pramucyate vimucyate // KaUBh_3.15/1,3.15 //
children.translated_text: — and other such [passages]. And immutable — standing firm like an anvil — eternal, not in the relative sense like earth and the other [elements]. Having discerned — having understood — such a <s>Brahman</s>-<s>Ātman</s>, one is freed, liberated, from the mouth of death — from the domain of death characterized by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>karma</s> (action). // KaUBh 3.15 //

body.translated_text: Without sound, without touch, without form, without taste, and without smell — that which has been thus described is <s>Brahman</s>. Imperishable — for that which possesses sound and the like perishes; but this, being without sound and the like, is imperishable — does not perish, does not decay. And for this very reason it is eternal — for that which perishes is impermanent, but this does not perish, hence it is eternal. It is also eternal for another reason: without beginning — that whose beginning, whose cause, does not exist — that is without beginning. For that which has a beginning, being an effect, is impermanent and dissolves into its cause, like earth and the other [elements]. But this, being the cause of all, is not an effect; being not an effect, it is eternal — it has no cause into which it could dissolve. Likewise without end — that whose end, whose product, does not exist — that is without end. Just as for the plantain tree and the like, even impermanence is observed through the production of fruit and other products — but no such endingness [pertains to] <s>Brahman</s>, hence it is eternal for this reason also. Beyond the great — distinct from the <s>mahat-tattva</s>, the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) — because it is of the nature of eternal consciousness, because it is the witness of all, being the Self of all beings — for <s>Brahman</s> [is such]. As stated —

children.text: nāciketam upākhyānaṃ mṛtyuproktaṃ sanātanam /
children.translated_text: The narrative of <s>Naciketas</s>, told by <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death), is eternal.

children.text: uktvā śrutvā ca medhāvī brahmaloke mahīyate // KaU_3.16/1,3.16 //
children.translated_text: Having spoken and having heard it, the wise one is glorified in the world of <s>Brahman</s>. // KaU 3.16 //

body.text: prastutavijñānastutyartham āha śrutiḥ -- nāciketaṃ naciketasā prāptaṃ nāciketaṃ mṛtyunā proktaṃ mṛtyuproktam idam ākhyānam upākhyānaṃ vallītrayalakṣaṇaṃ sanātanaṃ cirantanaṃ vaidikatvād uktvā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ śrutvā cācāryebhyo medhāvī brahmaiva loko brahmalokas tasmin brahmaloke mahīyata ātmabhūta upāsyo bhavatīty arthaḥ // KaUBh_3.16/1,3.16 //
body.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> states this for the purpose of praising the knowledge that has been presented: The <s>Nāciketa</s> [narrative] — that which was obtained by <s>Naciketas</s> — told by <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) — this narrative, this account, characterized by the three <s>vallīs</s> (sections), is <s>sanātana</s> (eternal, ancient), because it is Vedic. Having spoken it to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (learned ones) and having heard it from teachers, the wise one — in the world of <s>Brahman</s> — <s>Brahman</s> itself being the world, in that <s>Brahmaloka</s> — is glorified, becomes one who has become the Self, becomes worthy of worship — this is the meaning. // KaUBh 3.16 //

children.text: ya imaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śrāvayed brahmasaṃsadi /
children.translated_text: Whoever would cause this supreme secret to be heard in an assembly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: prayataḥ śrāddhakāle vā tad ānantyāya kalpate tad ānantyāya kalpata iti // KaU_3.17/1,3.17 //
children.translated_text: or reverently at the time of <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) — that conduces to infinity, that conduces to infinity. // KaU 3.17 //

body.text: iti kāṭhakopaniṣadi tṛtīyā vallī // 3 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>Vallī</s> in the <s>Kāṭhakopaniṣad</s>. // 3 //

body.text: yaḥ kaścid imaṃ granthaṃ paramaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ guhyaṃ gopyaṃ śrāvayed granthato 'rthataś ca brāhmaṇānāṃ saṃsadi brahmasaṃsadi prayataḥ śucir bhūtvā śrāddhakāle vā śrāvayed bhuñjānān tacchūddham asyānantyāyānantaphalāya kalpate sampadyate / dvir vacanam adhyāyaparisamāpty artham // KaUBh_3.17/1,3.17 //
body.translated_text: Whoever would cause this text — supreme, excellent, secret, to be kept hidden — to be heard, both in letter and in meaning, in an assembly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having become purified, or at the time of <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites) — would cause it to be heard to those who are eating — that [act], being pure, conduces to infinity, to infinite fruit — it is effective [for that purpose]. The repetition [of the phrase] is for the purpose of concluding the chapter. // KaUBh 3.17 //

body.text: iti kaṭhavallyāṃ tṛtīyāvallībhāṣyam // 3 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the commentary on the third <s>Vallī</s> of the <s>Kaṭhavallī</s>. // 3 //

body.text: atha dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Now the second <s>Adhyāya</s> (chapter).

children.text: "eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍho 'tmā na prakāśate dṛśyate tv agryayā buddhyā" (KaU 3.12)
children.translated_text: "This <s>Ātman</s>, hidden in all beings, does not shine forth; but it is seen by means of the supreme intellect." (<s>KaU</s> 3.12)

children.text: ity uktam / kaḥ punaḥ pratibandho 'grayāyā buddher yena tadabhāvād ātmā na dṛśyata iti tadadarśanakāraṇapradarśanārthā vally ārabhyate / vijñāte hi śreyaḥpratibandhakāraṇe tadapanayanāya yatna ārabdhuṃ śakyate nānyatheti --
children.translated_text: Thus it was stated. But what, then, is the obstacle to the supreme intellect, due to whose absence the <s>Ātman</s> is not seen? To show the cause of that non-seeing, [this] <s>vallī</s> commences. For only when the cause that obstructs the good (<s>śreyas</s>) is known can effort be undertaken to remove it; not otherwise —

children.text: parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayaṃbhūs tasmāt parāṅ paśyati nāntarātman /
children.translated_text: The Self-existent (<s>Svayambhū</s>) pierced the openings [of the senses] outward; therefore, one sees outward, not the inner <s>Ātman</s>.

children.text: kaścid dhīraḥ pratyag ātmānam aikṣad āvṛttacakṣur amṛtatvam icchan // KaU_4.1/2,1.1 //
children.translated_text: Some wise one, with eyes turned inward, desiring immortality, beheld the inner <s>Ātman</s>. (<s>KaU</s> 4.1/2.1.1)

body.text: parāñci parāgañcanti gacchantīti, khāni tadupalakṣitāni śrotrādīnīndriyāṇi khānīty ucyante / tāni parāñcy eva śabdādiviṣayaprakāśanāya pravartante / yasmād evaṃ svābhāvikāni tāni vyatṛṇaddhiṃsitavān hananaṃ kṛtavān ity arthaḥ / ko 'sau / svayambhūḥ parameśvaraḥ svayam eva svatantro bhavati sarvadā na paratantra iti / tasmāt parāṅ parāg rūpān anātmabhūtāñ śabdādīn paśyaty upalabhata upalabdhā nāntarātman nāntarātmānam ity arthaḥ / evaṃsvabhāve 'pi sati lokasya kaścin nadyāḥ pratisrotaḥ pravartanam iva dhīro dhīmān vivekī pratyagātmānaṃ pratyak cāsāv ātmā ceti pratyagātmā / pratīcyevātmaśabdo rūḍho loke nānyatra / vyutpattipakṣe 'pi tatraivātmaśabdo vartate /

children.text: "yac cāpnoti yadādatte yac cātti viṣayān iha / yac cāsya santato bhāvas tasmād ātmeti kīrtyate" (LiP 1,70.96)
children.translated_text: "That which pervades, that which takes, that which enjoys objects here, and that whose existence is continuous — therefore it is called '<s>Ātman</s>.'" (<s>LiP</s> 1.70.96)

children.text: ity ātmaśabdavyutpattismaraṇāt / taṃ pratyagātmānaṃ svaṃ svabhāvam aikṣad apaśyat paśyatīty arthaḥ / chandasi kālāniyamāt / kathaṃ paśyatīty ucyate -- āvṛttacakṣurāvṛttaṃ vyāvṛttaṃ cakṣuḥśrotrādikamindriyajātam aśeṣaviṣayādyasya sa āvṛttacakṣuḥ / sa evaṃ saṃskṛtaḥ pratyagātmānaṃ paśyati / na hi bāhyaviṣayālocanaparatvaṃ pratyagātmekṣaṇaṃ caikasya sambhavati / kim arthaṃ punar itthaṃ mahatā prayāsena svabhāvapravṛttinirodhaṃ kṛtvā dhīraḥ pratyagātmānaṃ paśyatīty ucyate -- amṛtatvam amaraṇadharmatvaṃ nityasvabhāvatām icchann ātmana ity arthaḥ // KaUBh_4.1/2,1.1 //
children.translated_text: — because the etymology of the word '<s>ātman</s>' is thus recorded [in <s>smṛti</s>]. That '<s>pratyagātman</s>' (inner self), one's own nature — he '<s>aikṣat</s>' (beheld), meaning 'he sees' — that is the meaning. [The past tense is used because] in the Vedic [language] there is no restriction of tense. How does he see? — it is said: '<s>āvṛttacakṣuḥ</s>' — one whose '<s>cakṣus</s>' (eye), [meaning] the entire sense-apparatus beginning with the eye and ear, has been '<s>āvṛtta</s>' (turned back, withdrawn) from all objects without exception — he is '<s>āvṛttacakṣuḥ</s>.' He who is thus prepared sees the inner <s>Ātman</s>. For the simultaneous engagement in perceiving external objects and seeing the inner <s>Ātman</s> is impossible for the same person. For what purpose, then, does the wise one see the inner <s>Ātman</s> with such great effort, having blocked the natural activity [of the senses]? — it is said: desiring '<s>amṛtatva</s>' (immortality) — the nature of non-dying, the eternal nature — of the <s>Ātman</s>, that is the meaning. (<s>KaUBh</s> 4.1/2.1.1)

body.translated_text: '<s>Parāñci</s>' means they go outward. '<s>Khāni</s>' — the senses beginning with hearing, characterized by them [the openings], are called 'openings.' They function outward only, for the illumination of objects such as sound and the like. Since they are thus naturally [outward-directed], he '<s>vyatṛṇat</s>' — struck, pierced, injured them — meaning 'he inflicted destruction' — that is the meaning. Who is he? '<s>Svayambhū</s>' — the Supreme Lord, who always exists independently by himself, never dependent on another. Therefore, one sees outward — perceives outward forms that are non-self, such as sound and the like — the perceiver does not [see] the inner <s>Ātman</s> — that is the meaning. Even though such is the nature [of the senses] for [all] people, some [rare one] — as if [making water] flow against the current of a river — the '<s>dhīra</s>' (wise one), the intelligent, the discriminating one — [beholds] the '<s>pratyagātman</s>' (inner self): '<s>pratyak</s>' (inward) and '<s>ātmā</s>' (self) — [together mean] the '<s>pratyagātman</s>' (inner self). The word '<s>ātman</s>' is conventionally established only in the reflexive sense, not elsewhere. Even according to the etymological derivation, the word '<s>ātman</s>' applies there only —

children.text: parācaḥ kāmān anuyanti bālās te mṛtyor yanti vitatasya pāśam /
children.translated_text: The childish pursue outward desires; they enter the widely-spread snare of death.

children.text: atha dhīrā amṛtatvaṃ viditvā dhruvam adhruveṣv iha na prārthayante // KaU_4.2/2,1.2 //
children.translated_text: But the wise, having known the permanent immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>), do not seek the permanent among impermanent things here. (<s>KaU</s> 4.2/2.1.2)

body.text: yat tāvat svābhāvikaṃ parāg evānātmadarśanaṃ tad ātmadarśanasya pratibandhakāraṇam avidyā tatpratikūlatvād yā ca parāg evāvidyopapradarśiteṣu dṛṣṭādṛṣṭeṣu bhogeṣu tṛṣṇā tābhyām avidyātṛṣṇābhyāṃ pratibaddhātmadarśanaḥ parāco bahirgatān eva kāmān kāmyān viṣayān anuyanty anugacchanti bālā alpaprajñāḥ, te tena kāraṇena mṛtyor avidyākāmakarmasamudāyasya yanti gacchanti vitatasya vistīrṇasya sarvato vyāptasya pāśaṃ pāśyate badhyate yena taṃ pāśaṃ dehendriyādisaṃyogalakṣaṇam / anavarataṃ janmamaraṇajarārogādyanekānarthavrātaṃ pratipadyanta ity arthaḥ / yata evam atha tasmād dhīrā vivekinaḥ pratyagātmasvarūpāvasthān alakṣaṇam amṛtatvaṃ dhruvaṃ viditvā / dehādyamṛtatvaṃ hy abruvam idaṃ tu pratyagātmasvarūpāvasthān alakṣaṇaṃ dhruvaṃ

children.text: "na karmaṇā vardhate no kanīyān" (BĀU 4,4.23)
children.translated_text: "It does not increase by action nor does it become less." (<s>BĀU</s> 4.4.23)

children.text: iti śruteḥ / tad evambhūtaṃ kūṭastham avicālyam amṛtatvaṃ viditvādhruveṣu sarvapadārtheṣv anityeṣu nirdhāryaṃ brāhmaṇā iha saṃsāre 'narthaprāye na prārthayante kiñcid api pratyagātmadarśanapratikūlatvāt / putravittalokaiṣaṇābhyo vyuttiṣṭhanty evety arthaḥ // KaUBh_4.2/2,1.2 //
children.translated_text: — so says the <s>śruti</s> (scripture). That which is of such a nature — immutable (<s>kūṭastha</s>), unshakable — having known that <s>amṛtatva</s> (immortality), among impermanent things, among all objects that are transient — the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (knowers of <s>Brahman</s>) here in <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), which is mostly full of calamity, do not seek anything at all, because [seeking] is contrary to the vision of the inner <s>Ātman</s>. [They] withdraw from the desire for sons, wealth, and worlds — that is the meaning. (<s>KaUBh</s> 4.2/2.1.2)

body.translated_text: As for the natural outward seeing of non-self — that is the obstructive cause of <s>Ātman</s>-vision, namely <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), being contrary to it; and the <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) for the seen and unseen enjoyments displayed by that outward-directed <s>avidyā</s> — by both these, <s>avidyā</s> and <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, those whose vision of the <s>Ātman</s> is obstructed — '<s>parācaḥ</s>' (outward-going) — pursue, follow after outward '<s>kāmān</s>' (desires), desirable objects. The '<s>bālāḥ</s>' (childish), those of little wisdom — they, for that reason, enter the snare of <s>mṛtyu</s> (death), the aggregate of <s>avidyā</s>, desire, and action, which is '<s>vitata</s>' (widely spread), extended, pervading everywhere — the '<s>pāśa</s>' (snare) by which one is bound, characterized by the conjunction with body, senses, and the like. [They] constantly undergo the multitude of manifold misfortunes such as birth, death, old age, disease, and the like — that is the meaning. Since it is so, therefore — the '<s>dhīrāḥ</s>' (wise), the discriminating ones — having known, having realized, the '<s>amṛtatva</s>' (immortality) that consists in abiding in the nature of the inner <s>Ātman</s>, which is '<s>dhruva</s>' (permanent) —

children.text: yena rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśīṃś ca maithunān /
children.translated_text: By which [one knows] form, taste, smell, sounds, and the pleasures of touch —

children.text: etenaiva vijānāti kim atra pariśiṣyate // etad vai tat // KaU_4.3/2,1.3 //
children.translated_text: by this alone does one know [everything] — what remains here that is [unknown]? This verily is That. (<s>KaU</s> 4.3/2.1.3)

body.text:
yad vijñānān na kiñcid anyat prārthayante brahmaṇāḥ, kathaṃ tadadhigama ity ucyate --
yena vijñānasvabhāvenātmanā rūpaṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ śabdān sparśāṃś ca maithunān maithunanimittān sukhapratyayān vijānāti vispaṣṭaṃ jānāti sarvo lokaḥ / nanu naivaṃ prasiddhir lokasyātmanā dehādivilakṣaṇenāhaṃ vijānāmīti / dehādisaṅghāto 'haṃ vijānāmīti tu sarvo loko 'vagacchati / na tv evam / dehādisaṅghātasyāpi śabdādisvarūpatvāviśeṣād vijñeyatvāviśeṣāc ca na yuktaṃ vijñātṛtvam / yadi hi dehādisaṅghāto rūpādyātmakaḥ san rūpādīn vijānīyāt tarhi bāhyā api rūpādayo 'nyonyaṃ svaṃ svaṃ rūpañ ca vijānīyuḥ / na caitad asti / tasmād dehādilakṣaṇāṃś ca rūpādīn etenaiva dehādivyatiriktenaiva vijñānasvabhāvenātmanā vijānāti lokaḥ / yathā yena loho dahati so 'gnir iti tadvat / ātmano 'vijñeyaṃ kim atrāsmiṃl loke pariśiṣyate na kiñcit pariśiṣyate / sarvam eva tv ātmanā vijñeyam / yasyātmano 'vijñeyaṃ na kiñcit pariśiṣyate sa ātmā sarvajñaḥ / etad vai tat / kiṃ tad yan naciketasā pṛṣṭaṃ devādibhir api vicikitsitaṃ dharmādibhyo 'nyad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ yasmāt paraṃ nāsti tadvai etad adhigatam ity arthaḥ // KaUBh_4.3/2,1.3 //
body.translated_text: That which the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> do not seek anything other than knowing — how is that attained? It is said: by which — by the <s>Ātman</s> whose nature is consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) — [one knows] form, taste, smell, sounds, and the pleasures of touch — the pleasurable cognitions caused by sexual union — [all this] one knows, clearly perceives — the whole world [does so]. [Objection:] But this is not how the world commonly understands it — 'I know through an <s>Ātman</s> distinct from the body and the like'; rather, the entire world understands 'I, the aggregate of body and the like, know.' [Reply:] Not so. Because the aggregate of body and the like, being not different in nature from sound and other [objects] — being equally of the nature of the knowable — it is not reasonable [for it] to be the knower. For if the aggregate of body and the like, being of the nature of form and the like, were to know form and the like, then even external forms and the like would know one another and their own respective forms. But this is not so. Therefore, it is by this alone — by the <s>Ātman</s> whose nature is consciousness, distinct from body and the like — that the world knows the forms and the like characterized by body and the like. Just as that by which iron burns is fire — similarly. What remains here, in this world, that is unknowable to the <s>Ātman</s>? Nothing remains. Everything is indeed knowable by the <s>Ātman</s>. That <s>Ātman</s> for which nothing unknowable remains — that <s>Ātman</s> is omniscient. 'This verily is That' — what is that? That which was asked about by <s>Naciketas</s>, doubted even by the gods and the like, other than <s>dharma</s> and the like — the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, beyond which there is nothing — that has verily been attained, that is the meaning. (<s>KaUBh</s> 4.3/2.1.3)

children.text: svapnāntaṃ jāgaritāntaṃ cobhau yenānupaśyati /
children.translated_text: By which one perceives both the state of dream and the state of waking —

children.text: mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvā dhīro na śocati // KaU_4.4/2,1.4 //
children.translated_text: having known that great, all-pervading <s>Ātman</s>, the wise one does not grieve. (<s>KaU</s> 4.4/2.1.4)

body.text: atisūkṣmatvād durvijñeyam iti matvaitam evārthaṃ punaḥ punar āha -- svapnāntaṃ svapnamadhyaṃ svapnavijñeyam ity etat / tathā jāgaritāntaṃ jāgaritamadhyaṃ jāgaritavijñeyaṃ ca / ubhau svapnajāgaritāntau yenātmanānupaśyati loka iti sarvaṃ pūrvavat / taṃ mahāntaṃ vibhum ātmānaṃ matvāvagamyātmabhāvena sākṣād aham asmi paramātmeti dhīro na śocati // KaUBh_4.4/2,1.4 //
body.translated_text: Because [this <s>Ātman</s>] is extremely subtle and difficult to know, thinking thus, he states this same meaning again and again: '<s>svapnānta</s>' means the state within dream, what is knowable in dream. Similarly, '<s>jāgaritānta</s>' means the state within waking, what is knowable in waking. Both — the states of dream and waking — by which <s>Ātman</s> one perceives — the whole world [perceives them] — everything is as before. Having known (<s>matvā</s>), having realized, that great and all-pervading <s>Ātman</s> as one's own self — directly [knowing] 'I am the Supreme <s>Ātman</s>' — the wise one does not grieve. (<s>KaUBh</s> 4.4/2.1.4)

children.text: ya imaṃ madhvadaṃ veda ātmānaṃ jīvamantikāt /
children.translated_text: Whoever knows this <s>Ātman</s>, the enjoyer of honey [the fruits of action], the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), from nearby —

children.text: īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate // etad vai tat // KaU_4.5/2,1.5 //
children.translated_text: the lord of past and future — he does not shrink from it [in fear]. This verily is That. (<s>KaU</s> 4.5/2.1.5)

body.text: kiñca yaḥ kaścid imaṃ madhvadaṃ karmaphalabhujaṃ jīvaṃ prāṇādikalāpasya dhārayitāram ātmānaṃ veda vijānāty antikād antike samīpa īśānam īśitāraṃ bhūtabhavyasya kālatrayasya, tatas tadvijñānād ūrdhvam ātmānaṃ na vijugupsate na gopāyitum icchaty abhayaprāptatvāt / yāvad dhi bhayam adhyastho 'nityam ātmānaṃ manyate tāvad gopāyitum icchaty ātmānaḥ / yadā tu nityam advaitam ātmānaṃ vijānāti tadā kaḥ kiṃ kuto vā gopāyitum icchet / etad vai tad iti pūrvavat // KaUBh_4.5/2,1.5 //
