body.translated_text: Moreover, whoever — any person — knows this '<s>madhvada</s>' (honey-eater), the enjoyer of the fruits of action, the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), the sustainer of the aggregate beginning with the vital breaths — knows the <s>Ātman</s>, understands [it] from nearby (<s>antikāt</s>), in close proximity — [as] the lord (<s>īśāna</s>), the ruler of past and future, of the three times — from that knowledge onward, he does not '<s>vijugupsate</s>' (shrink from), does not wish to protect, the <s>Ātman</s>, because fearlessness has been attained. For as long as one superimposes [attributes] and considers the <s>Ātman</s> to be impermanent, so long does one wish to protect the <s>Ātman</s>. But when one knows the <s>Ātman</s> to be eternal and non-dual, then who would wish to protect what, from what? 'This verily is That' — as before. (<s>KaUBh</s> 4.5/2.1.5)

children.text: yaḥ pūrvaṃ tapaso jātam adbhyaḥ pūrvam ajāyata /
children.translated_text: That which was born before <s>tapas</s> (creative heat), which was born before the waters —

children.text: guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantaṃ yo bhūtebhir vyapaśyata // etad vai tat // KaU_4.6/2,1.6 //
children.translated_text: having entered the cave and abiding [there], that which one beheld through the beings — this verily is That. (<s>KaU</s> 4.6/2.1.6)

body.text: yaḥ pratyagātmeśvarabhāvena nirdiṣṭaḥ sa sarvātmety etad darśayati -- yaḥ kaścin mumukṣuḥ pūrvaṃ prathamaṃ tapaso jñānādilakṣaṇabrahmaṇa ity etaj jātam utpannaṃ hiraṇyagarbham / kim apekṣya pūrvam ity āha -- adbhyaḥ pūrvam apsahitebhyaḥ pañcabhūtebhyo na kevalābhyo 'dbhya ity abhiprāyaḥ / ajāyata utpanno yas taṃ prathamajaṃ devādiśarīrāṇy utpādya sarvaprāṇiguhāṃ hṛdayākāśaṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantaṃ śabdādīn upalabhamānaṃ bhūtebhir bhūtaiḥ kāryakaraṇalakṣaṇaiḥ saha tiṣṭhantaṃ yo vyapaśyata yaḥ paśyatīty etat / ya evaṃ paśyati sa etad eva paśyati yat tat prakṛtaṃ brahma // KaUBh_4.6/2,1.6 //
body.translated_text: That which has been indicated as being the inner Self, the Lord — He is the Self of all; this is now shown: Whoever — any seeker of liberation — [sees] the first-born, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, who was born (<s>jātam</s>) from <s>tapas</s> (austerity) — characterized as knowledge and the rest — which is <s>Brahman</s>. Prior to what? He says: prior to the waters (<s>adbhyaḥ</s>) — meaning prior to the five elements associated with water, not from water alone — this is the purport. He who was born, produced — that first-born one, having produced the bodies of gods and the like, having entered the cave of the heart (<s>guhā</s>) of all beings, abiding there, perceiving sounds and other [objects] — him, abiding together with the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>), the assemblage of effects and instruments — whoever beholds, whoever sees — this is the meaning. One who sees thus, sees this very <s>Brahman</s> that is the subject [under discussion]. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.6||

children.text: yā prāṇena saṃbhavati aditir devatāmayī /
children.translated_text: That which arises from <s>Prāṇa</s> — <s>Aditi</s>, consisting of all deities —

children.text: guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantīṃ yā bhūtebhir vyajāyata // etad vai tat // KaU_4.7/2,1.7 //
children.translated_text: having entered the cave and abiding there, that which was born together with the elements — this indeed is That. ||<s>KaU</s> 4.7||

body.text: kiñ ca -- yā saravadevatāmayī saravadevatātmikā prāṇena hiraṇyagarbharūpeṇa parasmād brahmaṇaḥ sambhavati śabdādīnām adanād aditis tāṃ pūrvavad guhāṃ praviśya tiṣṭhantīm aditim / tām eva viśinaṣṭi -- yā bhūtebhir bhūtaiḥ samanvitā vyajāyata utpannety etat // KaUBh_4.7/2,1.7 //
body.translated_text: Moreover — that which consists of all deities, whose self is all the deities, which arises from <s>Prāṇa</s>, i.e., from <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, from the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; <s>Aditi</s> — because she devours (<s>adanāt</s>) sounds and other [objects]; that <s>Aditi</s>, having entered the cave and abiding there, as before. She is further qualified: that which was born, produced, endowed with the elements. This indeed is That. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.7||

children.text: araṇyor nihito jātavedā garbha iva subhṛto garbhiṇībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Jātavedas</s> (the fire, knower of all births), hidden in the two fire-sticks, like a well-nurtured embryo by pregnant women —

children.text: divediva īḍyo jāgṛvadbhir haviṣmadbhir manuṣyebhir agniḥ // etad vai tat // KaU_4.8/2,1.8 //
children.translated_text: day after day, [this] fire is to be worshipped by wakeful men who bring oblations. This indeed is That. ||<s>KaU</s> 4.8||

body.text: kiñ ca -- yo 'dhiyajña uttarādharāraṇyor nihitaḥ sthito jātavedā agniḥ punaḥ sarvahaviṣāṃ bhoktā adhyātmaṃ ca yogibhir garbha iva garbhiṇībhir antarvatnībhir agarhitānnabhojanādinā yathā garbhaḥ subhṛtaḥ suṣṭhu samyagbhṛto loke, ivettham eva rtvigbhir yogibhiś ca sumṛta ity etat / kiñ ca dive dive 'hany ahanīḍyaḥ stutyo vandyaś ca karmibhir yogibhiś cādhvare hṛdaye ca jāgṛvadbhir jāgaraṇaśīlair apramattair ity etat / haviṣmadbhir ājyādimadbhir dhyānabhāvanāvadbhiś ca, manuṣyebhir manuṣyair agnir etad vai tat tad eva prakṛtaṃ brahma // KaUBh_4.8/2,1.8 //
body.translated_text: Moreover — in the sacrificial context, the fire that is placed, stationed, in the upper and lower fire-sticks, <s>Jātavedas</s>, the consumer of all oblations — and in the inner context (<s>adhyātma</s>), [the Self that is nurtured] by <s>yogins</s> like an embryo by pregnant women — who through proper conduct such as non-blameworthy eating nourish [their embryo] well. Just as the embryo is well-nurtured (<s>subhṛta</s>), properly sustained in the world, in exactly the same way [the Self] is well-contemplated by the priests and the <s>yogins</s> — this is the meaning. Moreover, day after day, it is to be worshipped (<s>īḍya</s>), to be praised and venerated, by ritual practitioners and <s>yogins</s> — in the sacrificial fire and in the heart — who are wakeful (<s>jāgṛvat</s>), i.e., of vigilant disposition, not negligent — this is the meaning. Who bring oblations (<s>haviṣmat</s>) — who possess ghee and the like, and who possess meditation and contemplation — by such men, this fire [is to be worshipped]. This indeed is That — the very <s>Brahman</s> under discussion. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.8||

children.text: yataś codeti sūryo astaṃ yatra ca gacchati /
children.translated_text: That from which the sun rises and into which it sets —

children.text: taṃ devāḥ sarve arpitās tad u nātyeti kaścana // etad vai tat // KaU_4.9/2,1.9 //
children.translated_text: in that all the gods are fixed; no one ever goes beyond it. This indeed is That. ||<s>KaU</s> 4.9||

body.text: kiñ ca -- yataś ca yasmāt prāṇād udety uttiṣṭhati sūryo 'staṃ nimlocanaṃ yatra yasminn eva ca prāṇo 'hanyahani gacchati, taṃ prāṇam ātmānaṃ devāḥ, sarva agnyādayo 'dhidaivaṃ vāgādayaś cādhyātmaṃ sarve viśve 'rā iva rathanābhāv arpitāḥ sampraveśitāḥ sthitikāle / so 'pi brahmaiva / tad etat sarvātmakaṃ brahma / tad u nātyeti nātītya tadātmakatāṃ tadanyatvaṃ gacchati kaścana kaścid api / etad vai tat // KaUBh_4.9/2,1.9 //
body.translated_text: Moreover — that from which, from which <s>Prāṇa</s> (vital breath), the sun rises, i.e., ascends; and into which that very <s>Prāṇa</s> sets (<s>astam</s>), i.e., subsides, day after day. In that <s>Prāṇa</s>, the Self — all the gods: <s>Agni</s> and the others in the cosmic context, and the voice and others in the individual context — all of them are fixed (<s>arpitāḥ</s>), placed, like spokes in a wheel's hub, during the time of [their] existence. And that too is <s>Brahman</s> alone. This is that all-encompassing <s>Brahman</s>. No one ever goes beyond it — no one passes beyond its nature, to become something other than it. This indeed is That. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.9||

children.text: yad eveha tad amutra yad amutra tad anv iha /
children.translated_text: What is here, that is there; what is there, that is here.

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati // KaU_4.10/2,1.10 //
children.translated_text: He goes from death to death who sees here any plurality. ||<s>KaU</s> 4.10||

body.text: yad brahmādisthāvarānteṣu vartamānaṃ tat tadupādhitvād brahmavadavabhāsamānaṃ saṃsāry anyat parasmād brahmaṇa iti mā bhūt kasyacid āśaṅketīdam āha -- yad eveha kāryakāraṇopādhisamanvitaṃ saṃsāradharmavadavabhāsamānam avivekināṃ tad eva svātmastham amutra nityavijñānaghanasvabhāvaṃ sarvasaṃsāradharmavarjitaṃ brahma / yac cāmutrāmuṣminn ātmani sthitaṃ tad eveha nāmarūpakāryakaraṇopādhim anu vibhāvyamānaṃ nānyat / tatraivaṃ saty upādhisvabhāvabhedadṛṣṭilakṣaṇayāvidyayā mohitaḥ san ya iha brahmaṇyanānābhūte parasmād anyo 'haṃ matto 'nyatparaṃ brahmeti nāneva bhinnam iva paśyaty upalabhate, sa mṛtyor maraṇān mṛtyuṃ maraṇaṃ punaḥ punar jananamaraṇabhāvam āpnoti pratipadyate / tasmāt tathā na paśyet / vijñānaikarasaṃ nairantaryeṇākāśavat paripūrṇa brahmaivāham asmīti paśyed iti vākyārthaḥ // KaUBh_4.10/2,1.10 //
body.translated_text: Lest anyone suspect that what exists in <s>Brahman</s> and its various limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) — from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the immovable — appears like a being in <s>saṃsāra</s>, different from the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, due to those adjuncts — to prevent this, he says: What is here (<s>iha</s>), endowed with the limiting adjuncts of cause and effect, appearing as if possessing the properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> to those lacking discrimination — that very same thing, when situated in its own Self there (<s>amutra</s>), is the eternal, of the nature of concentrated consciousness, devoid of all properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> — that is <s>Brahman</s>. And what is there, situated in that Self — that very same thing is here, manifest through the limiting adjuncts of name, form, effects, and instruments — not something other. This being so, one who, deluded by the <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) characterized by the vision of difference based on the nature of the adjuncts, sees here, in <s>Brahman</s> which is not manifold — as if manifold, as if different: 'I am other than the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is other than me' — such a one goes from death to death, attains death after death — the condition of repeated birth and death. Therefore one should not see thus. 'I am <s>Brahman</s> alone, filled continuously like space, of the single essence of consciousness' — one should see thus; this is the purport of the sentence. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.10||

children.text: manasaivedam āptavyaṃ neha nānāsti kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: By the mind alone is this to be attained — there is no plurality here whatsoever.

children.text: mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyuṃ gacchati ya iha nāneva paśyati // KaU_4.11/2,1.11 //
children.translated_text: He goes from death to death who sees here any plurality. ||<s>KaU</s> 4.11||

body.text: prāgekatvavijñānācāryāgamasaṃskṛtena manasaivedaṃ brahmaikarasam āptavyam ātmaiva nānyad astīti / āpte ca nānātvapratyupasthāpikāyā avidyāyā nivṛttatvād iha brahmaṇi nānā nāsti kiñcanāṇumātram api / yas tu punar avidyātimiradṛṣṭiṃ na muñcatīha brahmaṇi nāneva paśyati, sa mṛtyor mṛtyuṃ gacchaty eva svalpam api bhedam adhyāropayann ity arthaḥ // KaUBh_4.11/2,1.11 //
body.translated_text: By the mind alone — purified by the instruction of the teacher and by scripture — this <s>Brahman</s>, of the single essence, is to be attained: the Self alone is, nothing else exists — thus. And once it is attained, since the <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) that presents plurality has ceased, in this <s>Brahman</s> there is no plurality whatsoever, not even the slightest trace. But one who does not abandon the vision afflicted by the darkness of <s>avidyā</s> and sees here, in <s>Brahman</s>, as if there were plurality — he goes from death to death, superimposing even the slightest difference — this is the meaning. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.11||

body.text: punar api tad eva prakṛtaṃ brahmāha --
body.translated_text: Again, he states that very <s>Brahman</s> which is the subject [under discussion]:

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo madhya ātmani tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the measure of a thumb, abides in the middle of the Self.

children.text: īśāno bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate // etad vai tat // KaU_4.12/2,1.12 //
children.translated_text: The Lord of the past and the future — one does not shrink from it thereafter. This indeed is That. ||<s>KaU</s> 4.12||

body.text: aṅguṣṭhamātro 'ṅguṣṭhaparimāṇo 'ṅguṣṭhaparimāṇaṃ hṛdayapuṇḍarīkaṃ tacchidravarty antaḥ -- karaṇopādhir aṅguṣṭhamātro 'ṅguṣṭhamātravaṃśaparvamadhyavarty ambaravat / puruṣaḥ pūrṇam anena sarvam iti / madhya ātmani śarīre tiṣṭhati yas tam ātmānam īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya viditvā na tad ity ādi pūrvavat // KaUBh_4.12/2,1.12 //
body.translated_text: Of the measure of a thumb (<s>aṅguṣṭhamātra</s>) — of the dimension of a thumb; the heart-lotus is of the dimension of a thumb, and [the <s>Puruṣa</s>] dwells in its cavity — inwardly, the conditioning adjunct (<s>karaṇopādhi</s>) is of the measure of a thumb, like the space within the middle section of a bamboo joint that is a thumb in length. <s>Puruṣa</s> — because everything is filled by it. It abides in the middle of the Self, i.e., in the body. One who knows that Self as the Lord (<s>Īśāna</s>) of the past and future — [the rest] as before [in the previous commentary]. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.12||

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo jyotir iva adhūmakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the measure of a thumb, like a light without smoke,

children.text: īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa evādya sa u śvaḥ // etad vai tat // KaU_4.13/2,1.13 //
children.translated_text: the Lord of the past and future — He is the same today, and He [is the same] tomorrow. This indeed is That. ||<s>KaU</s> 4.13||

body.text: kiṃ cāṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo jyotir ivādhūmakaḥ, adhūmakam iti yuktaṃ jyotiṣparatvāt / yas tv evaṃ lakṣito yogibhir hṛdaya īśāno bhūtabhavyasya sa eva nityaḥ kūṭastho 'dyedānīṃ prāṇiṣu vartamānaḥ sa u śvo 'pi vartiṣyate, nānyas tatsamo 'nyaś ca janiṣyata ity arthaḥ / anena

children.text: "nāyamastīti caika" (KaU 1.20)
children.translated_text: 'This [Self] does not exist' — held by some (<s>KaU</s> 1.20)

children.text: ity ayaṃ pakṣo nyāyato 'prāpto 'pi svavacanena śrutyā pratyuktas tathā kṣaṇabhaṅgavādaś ca // KaUBh_4.13/2,1.13 //
children.translated_text: — this position, though unjustifiable by reasoning, is also contradicted by scripture's own statement; likewise the doctrine of momentary destruction [is refuted]. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.13||

body.translated_text: Moreover, the <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the measure of a thumb, like a smokeless light — '<s>adhūmaka</s>' (smokeless) is appropriate since the comparison is with light. That one who is thus perceived by <s>yogins</s> in the heart, the Lord of the past and future — He is the same, eternal, immutable, today — now, present among living beings — and He will be [the same] tomorrow also. No other being equal to him will be born — this is the meaning. By this,

children.text: yathodakaṃ durge vṛṣṭaṃ parvateṣu vidhāvati /
children.translated_text: As water rained upon a craggy height runs off in various directions among the mountains,

children.text: evaṃ dharmān pṛthak paśyaṃs tān evānu vidhāvati // KaU_4.14/2,1.14 //
children.translated_text: so one who sees the <s>dharmas</s> (properties) as separate runs after them indeed. ||<s>KaU</s> 4.14||

body.text: punar api bhedadarśanāpavādaṃ brahmaṇa āha -- yathodakaṃ durge durgame deśa ucchrite vṛṣṭaṃ siktaṃ parvateṣu parvavatsu nimnapradeśeṣu vidhāvati vikīrṇaṃ sad vinaśyati, evaṃ dharmān ātmano 'bhinnān pṛthak paśyan pṛthag eva pratiśarīraṃ paśyaṃs tān eva śarīrabhedānuvartino 'nuvidhāvati / śarīrabhedam eva pṛthak punaḥ punaḥ pratipadyata ity arthaḥ // KaUBh_4.14/2,1.14 //
body.translated_text: Again, he states the refutation of the vision of difference in <s>Brahman</s>: Just as water rained upon a difficult, inaccessible, elevated terrain runs off in various directions among the mountains, into the low-lying areas — being scattered, it perishes. In the same way, one who sees the <s>dharmas</s> (properties) — which are not different from the Self — as separate, i.e., as distinct in each body, runs after those very [properties] that follow the bodily differences. He attains bodily difference itself again and again — this is the meaning. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.14||

children.text: yathodakaṃ śuddhe śuddham āsiktaṃ tādṛg eva bhavati /
children.translated_text: As pure water poured into pure [water] becomes the same indeed,

children.text: evaṃ muner vijānata ātmā bhavati gautama // KaU_4.15/2,1.15 //
children.translated_text: so becomes the Self of the sage who knows, O <s>Gautama</s>! ||<s>KaU</s> 4.15||

body.text: iti kāṭhakopaniṣadi caturthī vallī //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>vallī</s> of the <s>Kāṭhakopaniṣad</s>.

body.text: asya punar vidyāvato vidhvastopādhikṛtabhedadarśanasya viśuddhavijñānaghanaikarasam advayam ātmānaṃ paśyato vijānato muner mananaśīlasyātmasvarūpaṃ kathaṃ sambhavatīty ucyate yathodakaṃ śuddhe prasanne śuddhaṃ prasannam āsiktaṃ prakṣiptam ekarasam eva nānyathā tādṛg eva bhavaty ātmāpy evam eva bhavaty ekatvaṃ vijānato muner mananaśīlasya he gautama. tasmāt kutārkikabhedadṛṣṭiṃ nāstikakudṛṣṭiṃ cojjhitvā mātṛpitṛsahastrebhyo 'pi hitaiṣiṇā vedenopadiṣṭam ātmaikatvadarśanaṃ śāntadarpair ādaraṇīyam ity arthaḥ // KaUBh_4.15/2,1.15 //
body.translated_text: But for the one who possesses knowledge, whose vision of difference created by the limiting adjuncts has been destroyed, who sees the Self as non-dual, of the single essence of pure consciousness — for such a sage (<s>muni</s>), one given to contemplation, who knows and discerns — how is the nature of the Self possible? It is said: Just as pure, clear water poured into pure, clear [water] becomes the same, of a single essence, not otherwise — just so does the Self become [one] for the sage given to contemplation who knows the unity. O <s>Gautama</s>! Therefore, having abandoned the vision of difference held by sophists and the false views of nihilists, the vision of the unity of the Self — taught by the <s>Veda</s>, which is more beneficial than thousands of mothers and fathers — should be honored by those of peaceful disposition. This is the meaning. ||<s>KaUBh</s> 4.15||

body.text: iti kaṭhavallyāṃ caturthavallī bhāṣyam // 4 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the commentary on the fourth <s>vallī</s> of the <s>Kāṭhavallī</s>. ||4||

body.text: atha pañcamī vallī /
body.translated_text: Now the fifth <s>vallī</s>.

body.text: punar api prakārāntareṇa brahmatattvanirdhāraṇārtho 'yam ārambho durvijñeyatvād brahmaṇaḥ --
body.translated_text: Once again, this commencement is for the purpose of ascertaining the reality of <s>Brahman</s> through another approach, due to the difficulty of knowing <s>Brahman</s>:

children.text: puram ekādaśadvāram ajasyāvakracetasaḥ /
children.translated_text: The city of eleven gates, of the unborn one whose mind is not crooked —

children.text: anuṣṭhāya na śocati vimuktaś ca vimucyate // etad vai tat // KaU_5.1/2,2.1 //
children.translated_text: having meditated upon [him], one does not grieve; and being liberated, one is [fully] released. This verily is That.

body.text: puraṃ puram iva puram / dvārapālādhiṣṭhātrādyanekapuropakaraṇasampattidarśanāccharīraṃ puram / puraś ca sopakaraṇaṃ svātmanāsaṃhatasvatantrasvāmyarthaṃ dṛṣṭam / tathedaṃ purasāmānyād anekopakaraṇasaṃhataṃ śarīraṃ svātmanāsaṃhatarājasthānīyasvāmyarthaṃ bhavitum arhati / tac cedaṃ śarīrākhyaṃ puram ekādaśadvāram ekādaśa dvārāṇy asya sapta śīrṣaṇyāni, nābhyā sahārvāñci trīṇi, śirasy ekam, tair ekādaśadvāraṃ puram / kasya? ajasya janmādivikriyārahitasyātmano rājasthānīyasya puradharmavilakṣaṇasya / avakracetaso 'vakram akuṭilam ādityaprakāśavan nityam evāvasthitam ekarūpaṃ ceto vijñānam asyety avakracetās tasyāvakracetaso rājasthānīyasya brahmaṇaḥ / yasyedaṃ puraṃ taṃ parameśvaraṃ purasvāminam anuṣṭhāya dhyātvā / dhyānaṃ hi tasyānuṣṭhānaṃ samyag vijñānapūrvakam / taṃ sarvaiṣaṇāvinirmuktaḥ san samaṃ sarvabhūtasthaṃ dhyātvā na śocati / tadvijñānād abhayaprāpteḥ śokāvasarābhāvāt kuto bhayekṣā / ihaivāvidyākṛtakāmakarmabandhanair vimukto bhavati / vimuktaś ca san vimucyate punaḥ śarīraṃ na gṛhṇātīty arthaḥ // KaUBh_5.1/2,2,1 //
body.translated_text: A <s>pura</s> (city) — like a city, [the body] is a city. Because one observes in it the wealth of numerous city-appurtenances such as gate-keepers, presiding officers, and the like, the body is [called] a city. And a city with its appurtenances is seen to exist for the sake of an independent master who is himself not a composite. Likewise, this body, being an aggregate of many appurtenances — by analogy with a city — ought to exist for the sake of a master who occupies the position of a king and is himself not a composite. And this city called the body has eleven gates — it has eleven doors: seven in the head, three below including the navel, and one at the crown of the head — a city with eleven gates through these. Of whom? Of the <s>aja</s> (unborn), the <s>Ātman</s> who is free from modifications such as birth and the like, who occupies the position of king, who is distinct from the properties of the city. Of the one whose mind is not crooked — <s>avakra</s> means not crooked, like the light of the sun, eternally abiding, of one single form; <s>cetas</s> means consciousness — the one who has such [consciousness] is <s>avakracetās</s>; of that <s>avakracetās</s> who occupies the position of king, of <s>Brahman</s>. Having meditated upon (<s>anuṣṭhāya</s>) him, the supreme Lord, the master of the city — for meditation accompanied by right knowledge is his <s>anuṣṭhāna</s> (practice). Having meditated upon him as the same [Self] abiding in all beings, being freed from all desires, one does not grieve. Because through the knowledge of That, fearlessness is attained, and there is no occasion for grief — whence any apprehension of fear? Right here [in this life], one becomes freed from the bonds of desire and action created by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). And being freed, one is [fully] released — one does not take up a body again; this is the meaning.

children.text: haṃsaḥ śuciṣad vasur antarikṣasad dhotā vediṣad atithir duroṇasat /
children.translated_text: He is the swan (<s>Haṃsa</s>) dwelling in the light, the <s>Vasu</s> dwelling in the atmosphere, the invoking priest (<s>Hotā</s>) seated at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house,

children.text: nṛṣad varasad ṛtasad vyomasad abjā gojā ṛtajā adrijā ṛtaṃ bṛhat // KaU_5.2/2,2.2 //
children.translated_text: dwelling among men, dwelling among the gods, dwelling in truth, dwelling in space; born of water, born of earth, born of sacrifice, born of mountains — the great Truth.

body.text: sa tu naikaśarīrapuravarttyevātmā kiṃ tārhi sarvapūravartī / katham -- haṃso hanti gacchatīti / śuciṣacchucau divyādityātmanā sīdatīti / vasur vāsayati sarvāniti / vāyvātmanāntarikṣe sīdatīty antarikṣasat / hotāgniḥ, "agnir vai hotā" iti śruteḥ / vedyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ sīdatīti vediṣad

children.text: "iyaṃ vediḥ paro 'ntaḥ pṛthivyāḥ" (RS 2,3.20)
children.translated_text: as stated in the <s>mantra</s> "This is the altar, the far end of the earth" (<s>ṚS</s> 2.3.20)

children.text: ity ādimantravarṇāt / atithiḥ somaḥ san duroṇe kalaśe sīdatīti duroṇasat / brāhmaṇo 'tithirūpeṇa vā duroṇeṣu gṛheṣu sīdatīti / nṛṣanṛṣu manuṣyeṣu sīdatīti / varasad vareṣu deveṣu sīdatīti / ṛtasad ṛtaṃ satyaṃ yajño vā tasmin sīdatīti / vyomasad vyomnyākāśe sīdatīti / abjā apsu śaṅkhakhaśuktimakarādirūpeṇa jāyata iti / gojā gavi pṛthivyāṃ vrīhiyavādirūpeṇa jāyata iti / ṛtajā yajñāṅgarūpeṇa jāyata iti / adrijāḥ parvatebhyo nadyādirūpeṇa jāyata iti / sarvātmāpi sann ṛtam avitathasvabhāva eva / bṛhan mahān sarvakāraṇatvāt / yadāpy āditya eva mantreṇocyate tad apy ātmasvarūpatvam ādityasyāṅgīkṛtatvād brāhmaṇo vyākhyāne 'py avirodhaḥ / sarvavyāpy eka evātmā jagato nātmabheda iti mantrārthaḥ // KaUBh_5.2/2,2.2 //
children.translated_text: and other <s>mantra</s> passages. As <s>Soma</s>, he is the guest (<s>atithi</s>) who dwells in the <s>duroṇa</s> (vessel, receptacle) — hence <s>duroṇasat</s>. Or, in the form of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> guest, he dwells in <s>duroṇas</s> (houses). <s>Nṛṣat</s>: he dwells among <s>nṛs</s> (men, human beings). <s>Varasat</s>: he dwells among <s>varas</s> (the gods, the excellent ones). <s>Ṛtasat</s>: <s>ṛta</s> is truth, or sacrifice — he dwells in that. <s>Vyomasat</s>: he dwells in <s>vyoman</s> (space, the sky). <s>Abjā</s>: he is born in waters in the form of conch, oyster, pearl-shell, crocodile, and the like. <s>Gojā</s>: he is born on <s>go</s> (earth) in the form of rice, barley, and the like. <s>Ṛtajā</s>: he is born in the form of the limbs of sacrifice. <s>Adrijā</s>: he is born from mountains in the form of rivers and the like. Though he is the Self of all, he is <s>ṛtam</s> — of unfailing nature indeed. <s>Bṛhat</s> — great, because he is the cause of everything. Even when the <s>mantra</s> speaks specifically of <s>Āditya</s> (the sun), since <s>Āditya</s> is accepted as being of the nature of the <s>Ātman</s>, there is no contradiction even in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> exposition. The meaning of the <s>mantra</s> is: the <s>Ātman</s> of the universe is one alone; there is no differentiation of the Self.

body.translated_text: But that <s>Ātman</s> does not dwell in one single body-city alone. What then? He dwells in all cities. How? — <s>Haṃsa</s>: he moves (<s>hanti gacchati</s>). <s>Śuciṣat</s>: he dwells in the bright [heaven] as the <s>Āditya</s> (sun). <s>Vasu</s>: he causes all to dwell (<s>vāsayati sarvān</s>). He dwells in the atmosphere as <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) — hence <s>antarikṣasat</s>. <s>Hotā</s> means <s>Agni</s> (fire), from the <s>śruti</s> "<s>Agni</s> is indeed the <s>Hotā</s>." He sits on the <s>vedī</s>, the earth — hence <s>vediṣat</s>,

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ prāṇam unnayati apānaṃ pratyag asyati /
children.translated_text: He leads the <s>prāṇa</s> (out-breath) upward and casts the <s>apāna</s> (in-breath) downward.

children.text: madhye vāmanam āsīnaṃ viśve devā upāsate // KaU_5.3/2,2.3 //
children.translated_text: All the gods worship that adorable one seated in the middle.

body.text: ātmanaḥ svarūpādhigame liṅgam ucyate -- ūrdhvaṃ hṛdayāt prāṇaṃ prāṇavṛttiṃ vāyum unnayaty ūrdhvaṃ gamayati / tathāpānaṃ pratyagadho 'syati kṣipati ya iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / taṃ madhye hṛdayapuṇḍarīkākāśa āsīnaṃ buddhāv abhivyaktavijñānaprakāśanaṃ vāmanaṃ vananīyaṃ sambhajanīyaṃ viśve sarve devāś cakṣurādayaḥ prāṇā rūpādivijñānaṃ balim upāharanto viśva iva rājānam upāsate tādarthyenānuparatavyāpārā bhavantīty arthaḥ / yad arthā yat prayuktāś ca sarve vāyukaraṇavyāpārāḥ, so 'nyaḥ siddha iti vākyārthaḥ // KaUBh_5.3/2,2.3 //
body.translated_text: A characteristic mark for comprehending the true nature of the <s>Ātman</s> is stated: He leads the <s>prāṇa</s> — the vital breath, the function of <s>prāṇa</s>, the wind — upward from the heart, causing it to move upward. Likewise, the <s>apāna</s> he casts (<s>asyati</s>) downward inward — the one who [does this]; this is the completion of the sentence. Him, seated in the middle, in the space within the lotus of the heart, the adorable one (<s>vāmana</s>) — worthy of worship, worthy of reverence — whose manifestation of consciousness is expressed in the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — all the gods, namely the <s>prāṇas</s> (vital functions) such as the eye and others, worship, offering tribute of the cognition of form and the like, just as all [subjects worship] a king, being engaged in unceasing activity for his sake; this is the meaning. That for whose purpose all the functions of wind and the organs operate — he is established as another, distinct [from them]; this is the purport of the sentence.

children.text: asya visraṃsamānasya śarīrasthasya dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of this embodied one dwelling in the body, as it falls apart,

children.text: dehād vimucyamānasya kim atra pariśiṣyate // etad vai tat // KaU_5.4/2,2.4 //
children.translated_text: as it is released from the body — what remains here? This verily is That.

body.text: kiñ cāsya śarīrasthasyātmano visraṃsamānasya bhraṃśamānasya dehino dehavataḥ / visraṃsanaśabdārtham āha -- dehād vimucyamānasyeti / kim atra pariśiṣyate prāṇādikalāpe na kiñcana pariśiṣyate 'tra dehe purasvāmividravaṇa iva paravāsināṃ yasyātmanopagame kṣaṇamātrāt kāryakaraṇakalāparūpaṃ sarvam idaṃ hatabalaṃ vidhvastaṃ bhavati vinaṣṭaṃ bhavati so 'nyaḥ siddha ātmā // KaUBh_5.4/2,2.4 //
body.translated_text: Moreover, of this <s>Ātman</s> dwelling in the body, as it falls apart, disintegrates — of the <s>dehin</s> (embodied one), the one possessing a body. He explains the meaning of the word 'falling apart': 'as it is released from the body.' What remains here in the aggregate of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital functions) and the rest? Nothing whatsoever remains here in the body — just as when the owner of a city departs, the foreign residents [scatter]; upon whose arrival, the entire assemblage in the form of the body-mind complex is instantly rendered powerless, scattered, destroyed — that one is established as another, as the [independent] <s>Ātman</s>.

children.text: na prāṇena nāpānena martyo jīvati kaścana /
children.translated_text: No mortal lives by <s>prāṇa</s> (the out-breath) nor by <s>apāna</s> (the in-breath).

children.text: itareṇa tu jīvanti yasminn etāv upāśritau // KaU_5.5/2,2.5 //
children.translated_text: They live by something else, upon which these two depend.

body.text: syān mataṃ prāṇāpānādyapagamād evedaṃ vidhvastaṃ bhavati na tu tadvyatiriktātmāpagamāt prāṇādibhir eveha martyo jīvatīti / naitad asti / na prāṇena nāpānena cakṣurādinā vā martyo manuṣyo dehavān kaścana jīvati na ko 'pi jīvati / na hy eṣāṃ parārthānāṃ saṃhatyakāritvāj jīvanahetutvam upapadyate / svārthanāsaṃhatena pareṇa kenacid aprayuktaṃ saṃhatānām avasthānaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ yathā gṛhādīnāṃ loke, tathā prāṇādīnām api saṃhatatvād bhavitum arhati / ata itareṇa itareṇaiva saṃhataprāṇādivilakṣaṇena tu sarve saṃhatāḥ santo jīvanti prāṇān dhārayanti / yasmin saṃhatavilakṣaṇa ātmani sati parasminn etau prāṇāpānau cakṣurādibhiḥ saṃhatāv upāśritau, yasyāsaṃhatasyārthe prāṇāpānādiḥ sarvaṃ vyāpāraṃ kurvan vartate saṃhataḥ san sa tato 'nyaḥ siddha ity abhiprāyaḥ // KaUBh_5.5/2,2.5 //
body.translated_text: One might think: it is merely from the departure of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the rest that all this is destroyed, and not from the departure of a Self distinct from them — that a mortal lives by <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest alone. This is not so. No mortal, no human being possessing a body, lives by <s>prāṇa</s>, nor by <s>apāna</s>, nor by the eye and other [senses] — no one whatsoever lives [by them alone]. For it is not possible that these, which serve another's purpose and function as a composite, could be the cause of life. It is not observed that composite things can maintain their functioning without being directed by some independent, non-composite entity that serves its own purpose — just as houses and the like in the world [require an owner]. Similarly, <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest too, being composites, must be [directed by another]. Therefore, by the other — by something else, distinct from the composite of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — all beings, being composites, live, sustain their vital functions. In the presence of which — that <s>Ātman</s> distinct from the composite, the supreme one — these two, <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, together with the eye and other [senses] as composites, are dependent; for whose sake — the non-composite one's sake — the entire composite of <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, and the rest performs all its functions — that one is established as another, distinct [from them]; this is the purport.

children.text: hanta ta idaṃ pravakṣyāmi guhyaṃ brahma sanātanam /
children.translated_text: Come! I will tell you this secret, eternal <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text: yathā ca maraṇaṃ prāpya ātmā bhavati gautama // KaU_5.6/2,2.6 //
children.translated_text: and how the <s>Ātman</s> fares after reaching death, O <s>Gautama</s>.

body.text: hantedānīṃ punar api te tubhyam idaṃ guhyaṃ gopyaṃ brahma sanātanaṃ cirantanaṃ pravakṣyāmi / yad vijñānāt sarvasaṃsāroparamo bhavati, avijñānāc ca yasya maraṇaṃ prāpya yathā cātmā bhavati yathātmā saṃsarati tathā śṛṇu he gautama // KaUBh_5.6/2,2.6 //
body.translated_text: Come now! Again I will tell you — tell you this <s>guhya</s> (secret), that which is to be kept hidden — the eternal, ancient <s>Brahman</s>. Through the knowledge of which, the cessation of all <s>saṃsāra</s> occurs, and through ignorance of which — how the <s>Ātman</s> fares after reaching death, how the <s>Ātman</s> transmigrates — hear that, O <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: yonim anye prapadyante śarīratvāya dehinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some embodied beings enter a womb for [obtaining] a body;

children.text: sthāṇum anye 'nusaṃyanti yathākarma yathāśrutam // KaU_5.7/2,2.7 //
children.translated_text: others follow the course of immobility — according to their <s>karma</s>, according to their knowledge.

body.text: yoniṃ yonidvāraṃ śukrabījasamanvitāḥ santo 'nye kecid avidyāvanto mūḍhāḥ prapadyante śarīratvāya śarīragrahaṇārthaṃ dehino dehavantaḥ, yoniṃ praviśantīty arthaḥ / sthāṇuṃ vṛkṣādisthāvarabhāvam anye 'tyantādhamā maraṇaṃ prāpyānusaṃyanty anugacchanti / yathākarma yady asya karma tadyathākarma yair yādṛśaṃ karmeha janmani kṛtaṃ tadvaśenety etat / tathā ca yathāśrutaṃ yādṛśaṃ ca vijñānam upārjitaṃ tadanurūpam eva śarīraṃ pratipadyanta ity arthaḥ / "yathāprajñaṃ hi saṃbhavāḥ" iti śrutyantarāt // KaUBh_5.7/2,2.7 //
body.translated_text: Some — certain ignorant, deluded beings, endowed with seed and semen — enter a womb, the gateway of birth, for the purpose of obtaining a body, being embodied ones — they enter a womb; this is the meaning. Others, the most extremely degraded ones, having reached death, follow, proceed to the state of immobile beings (<s>sthāṇu</s>) such as trees and the like. According to their <s>karma</s> — if they have <s>karma</s>, then according to that <s>karma</s>: by the force of whatever kind of <s>karma</s> was performed in this life; this is what is meant. And likewise, according to their <s>śruta</s> (learning) — whatever knowledge was acquired, they obtain a body corresponding to that exactly; this is the meaning. From another <s>śruti</s>: "For births are according to one's knowledge."

children.text:
ya eṣa supteṣu jāgarti kāmaṃ kāmaṃ puruṣo nirmimāṇaḥ /
tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate /
tasmiṃl lokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana // etad vai tat // KaU_5.8/2,2.8 //
children.translated_text: He who, among all sleeping beings, remains awake, shaping desire after desire — that <s>Puruṣa</s> — that alone is the Bright, that is <s>Brahman</s>, that alone is called the Immortal. In it all worlds rest; no one transcends it. This verily is That.

body.text:
yatpratijñātaṃ guhyaṃ brahma pravakṣyāmīti tadāha -- ya eṣa supteṣu prāṇādiṣu jāgartiṃ na svapiti / katham / kāmaṃ kāmaṃ taṃ tam abhipretaṃ stryādyartham avidyayā nirmimāṇo
niṣpādayañjāgartiṃ puruṣo yaḥ, tad eva śukraṃ śubhraṃ śuddhaṃ tad brahma nānyad guhyaṃ brahmāsti / tad evāmṛtam avināśy ucyate sarvaśāstreṣu / kiñ ca pṛthivyādayo lokās tasminn eva sarve brahmaṇi śritā āśritāḥ sarvalokakāraṇatvāt tasya / tad u nātyeti kaścanety ādi pūrvavad eva // KaUBh_5.8/2,2.8 //
body.translated_text: What was promised — 'I shall declare the secret <s>Brahman</s>' — that he now states: That which, among the sleeping [faculties] — the <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest — remains awake, does not sleep. How? Fashioning — producing — through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), each and every desired object such as women and the like — that <s>Puruṣa</s> who remains awake — that alone is the radiant, the luminous, the pure; that is <s>Brahman</s>, there is no other secret <s>Brahman</s>. That alone is called <s>amṛta</s> (immortal, imperishable) in all scriptures. Moreover, all the worlds — earth and the rest — are established in that <s>Brahman</s> alone, because it is the cause of all worlds. 'That none transgresses' — and so on, is as explained before. // KaUBh 5.8 //

children.text: agnir yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva /
children.translated_text: Just as fire, though one, having entered the world, became corresponding to each form,

children.text: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca // KaU_5.9/2,2.9 //
children.translated_text: so the one inner Self of all beings became corresponding to each form, and [yet remains] outside. // KaU 5.9 //

body.text: anekatārkikakubuddhivicālitāntaḥkaraṇānāṃ pramāṇopapannam apy ātmaikatvavijñānam asakṛd ucyamānam apy anṛjubuddhīnāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ cetasi nādhīyata iti tatpratipādana ādaravatī punaḥ punar āha śrutiḥ -- agnir yathaika eva prakāśātmā san bhuvanaṃ bhavanty asmin bhūtānīti bhuvanam ayaṃ lokas tam imaṃ praviṣṭo 'nupraviṣṭaḥ, rūpaṃ rūpaṃ prati dārvādidāhyabhedaṃ pratīty arthaḥ, pratirūpas tatra tatra pratirūpavān dāhyabhedena bahuvidho babhūva / eka eva tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām abhyantara ātmātisūkṣmatvād dārvādiṣv iva sarvadehaṃ prati praviṣṭatvāt pratirūpo babhūva bahiś ca svenāvikṛtena svarūpeṇākāśavat // KaUBh_5.9/2,2.9 //
body.translated_text: The knowledge of the oneness of the <s>Ātman</s>, though well-supported by valid means of knowledge and though stated repeatedly, does not take root in the minds of those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (seekers) of crooked understanding whose inner faculties have been shaken by the perverse reasoning of the many logicians. Therefore, the <s>śruti</s>, being zealous in establishing that [truth], states it again and again: Just as fire, though one alone, being of the nature of light, having entered the world — '<s>bhuvana</s>' [means] that in which beings exist, i.e., this world — having entered, having pervaded it — became, with respect to each form, each variation of combustible material such as wood and the like, a counterpart (<s>pratirūpa</s>), that is, having a counterpart form corresponding to each [combustible], became manifold due to the variety of combustible material. Similarly, the one inner Self (<s>antarātmā</s>) of all beings, [became] corresponding to each form of all beings — being inwardly [present] as the <s>Ātman</s> due to extreme subtlety, having entered each body like [fire enters] wood and the like — [yet also] outside, in its own unmodified essential nature, like space. // KaUBh 5.9 //

children.text: vāyur yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva /
children.translated_text: Just as wind, though one, having entered the world, became corresponding to each form,

children.text: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo bahiś ca // KaU_5.10/2,2.10 //
children.translated_text: so the one inner Self of all beings became corresponding to each form, and [yet remains] outside. // KaU 5.10 //

body.text: tathānyo dṛṣṭāntaḥ -- vāyur yathaika ity ādi / prāṇātmanā deheṣv anupraviṣṭo, rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūvety ādi samānam // KaUBh_5.10/2,2.10 //
body.translated_text: Similarly, another illustration: 'Just as wind, though one' — and so on. Having entered the bodies in the form of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), 'became corresponding to each form' — and the rest is the same [as before]. // KaUBh 5.10 //

children.text: sūryo yathā sarvalokasya cakṣur na lipyate cākṣuṣair bāhyadoṣaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the sun, the eye of the whole world, is not tainted by the external defects [perceived] by the eye,

children.text: ekas tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ // KaU_5.11/2,2.11 //
children.translated_text: so the one inner Self of all beings is not tainted by the suffering of the world, being external [to it]. // KaU 5.11 //

body.text: ekasya sarvātmatve saṃsāraduḥkhitvaṃ parasyaiva syād iti prāpta idam ucyate -- sūryo yathā cakṣuṣa ālokenopakāraṃ kurvan mūtrapurīṣādyaśuciprakāśanena taddarśinaḥ sarvalokasya cakṣur api san na lipyate cākṣuṣair aśucyādidarśananimittair ādhyātmikaiḥ pāpadoṣair bāhyaiś cāśucyādisaṃsaṅgadoṣair ekaḥ saṃs tathā sarvabhūtāntarātmā na lipyate lokaduḥkhena bāhyaḥ / loko hy avidyayā svātmany adhyastayā kāmakarmodbhavaṃ duḥkham anubhavati / na tu sā paramārthataḥ svātmani / yathā rajjuśuktikoṣaragaganeṣu sarparajatodakamalāni na rajjvādīnāṃ svato doṣarūpāṇi santi, saṃsargiṇi viparītabuddhyadhyāsanimittāt tad doṣavadvibhāvyante / na taddoṣais teṣāṃ lepo viparītabuddhyadhyāsabāhyā hi te / tathātmani sarvo lokaḥ kriyākārakaphalātmakaṃ vijñānaṃ sarpādisthānīyaṃ viparītamadhyasya tannimittaṃ janmamaraṇādiduḥkham anubhavati, na tv ātmā sarvalokātmāpi san viparītādhyāropanimittena lipyate lokaduḥkhena / kuto bāhyo rajjvādivad eva viparītabuddhyadhyāsabāhyo hi sa iti // KaUBh_5.11/2,2.11 //
body.translated_text: The objection arises that if one [<s>Ātman</s>] is the Self of all, then <s>saṃsāra</s>-suffering would belong to the Supreme itself. To this, it is said: Just as the sun, though benefiting the eye through illumination, though causing the manifestation of impure things such as urine, excrement, and the like, though being the eye of the entire world — is not tainted by the defects perceived by the eye, whether subjective (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) faults arising from seeing impure things and the like, or external faults of contact with impurity and similar [things]; similarly, the one inner Self of all beings is not tainted by the suffering of the world — [it remains] external. For the world, through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) superimposed upon its own Self, experiences suffering born of desire and action. But that [<s>avidyā</s>] does not truly [belong to] one's own Self. Just as in [the case of] a rope, a shell, a cavern, and the sky — the snake, silver, water, and stain do not truly constitute defects of the rope and the like; [yet] to one who superimposes [them] due to erroneous cognition, they are perceived as possessing those defects. Those [rope and the like] are not tainted by those defects, for they are external to the superimposition of erroneous cognition. Similarly, upon the <s>Ātman</s>, the entire world superimposes knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>) consisting of action, agent, and fruit — analogous to the snake and the like — [superimposes it] erroneously, and experiences suffering such as birth, death, and the like caused by that [superimposition]. But the <s>Ātman</s>, though being the Self of the entire world, is not tainted by worldly suffering through the cause of erroneous superimposition. Why? Because it is external — just like the rope and the like, it is indeed external to the superimposition of erroneous cognition. // KaUBh 5.11 //

children.text: eko vaśī sarvabhūtāntarātmā ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti /
children.translated_text: The one controller, the inner Self of all beings, who makes one form manifold —

children.text: tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām // KaU_5.12/2,2.12 //
children.translated_text: the wise who perceive Him as abiding in the Self — to them belongs eternal happiness, not to others. // KaU 5.12 //

body.text: kiñ ca sa hi parameśvaraḥ sarvagataḥ svatantra eko na tatsamo 'bhyadhiko vānyo 'sti / vaśī sarvaṃ hy asya jagadvaśe vartate / kutaḥ? sarvabhūtāntarātmā / yata ekam eva sadekarasam ātmānaṃ viśuddhavijñānarūpaṃ nāmarūpādyaśuddhopādhibhedavaśena bahudhānekaprakāraṃ yaḥ karoti svātmasattāmātreṇācintyaśaktitvāt tam ātmasthaṃ svaśarīrahṛdayākāśe buddhau caitanyākāreṇābhivyaktam ity etat / na hi śarīrasyādhāratvam ātmanaḥ / ākāśavad amūrtatvāt / ādarśasthaṃ mukham iti yadvat / tam etam īśvaram ātmānaṃ ye nivṛttabāhyavṛttayo 'nupaśyanty ācāryāgamopadeśam anu sākṣād anubhavanti dhīrā vivekinas teṣāṃ parameśvarabhūtānāṃ śāśvataṃ nityaṃ sukham ātmānandalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati, netareṣāṃ bāhyāsaktabuddhīnām avivekināṃ svātmabhūtam apy avidyāvyavadhānāt // KaUBh_5.12/2,2.12 //
body.translated_text: Moreover, that Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), being all-pervading, is independent — one, with no other equal to or greater than Him. He is the controller (<s>vaśī</s>), for the entire universe is under His control. Why? Because He is the inner Self of all beings. Since He makes the one — the homogeneous <s>Ātman</s> of pure consciousness — manifold, in many ways, through the power of the impure limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) of name, form, and the like, by the mere existence of His own Self, due to His inconceivable power — Him, abiding in the Self, that is, manifest in the form of consciousness in the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) within the space of the heart of one's own body — this is the meaning. For the <s>Ātman</s> does not literally reside in the body; being formless like space. [It is] like [saying] a face is 'in' a mirror. Those who, having withdrawn from external activities, perceive — directly experience — Him, this Lord, as the <s>Ātman</s>, following the teaching of the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) and the <s>āgama</s> (scripture) — the wise, the discriminating — to them, who have become one with the Supreme Lord, belongs eternal, permanent happiness, characterized by the bliss of the <s>Ātman</s>; not to others — those of outward-directed intellect, the undiscriminating, [for whom it remains unavailable] despite being their very own Self, due to the obstruction of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). // KaUBh 5.12 //

children.text: nityo 'nityānāṃ cetanaś cetanānām eko bahūnāṃ yo vidadhāti kāmān /
children.translated_text: The eternal among the non-eternal, the conscious among the conscious, the one among the many, who fulfills desires —

children.text: tam ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣaṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām // KaU_5.13/2,2.13 //
children.translated_text: the wise who perceive Him as abiding in the Self — to them belongs eternal peace, not to others. // KaU 5.13 //

body.text: kiñ ca nityo 'vināśyanityānāṃ vināśinām / cetanaś cetanānāṃ cetayitṝṇāṃ brahmādīnāṃ prāṇinām agninimittam iva dāhakatvam anagnīnām udakādīnām ātmacaitanyanimittam eva cetayitṛtvam anyeṣām / kiñ ca sa sarvajñaḥ sarveśvaraḥ kāmināṃ saṃsāriṇāṃ karmānurūpaṃ kāmān karmaphalāni svānugrahanimittāś ca kāmāny eko bahūnām anekeṣāmanāyāsena vidadhāti prayacchatīty etat / tām ātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrās teṣāṃ śāntir uparatiḥ śāśvatī nityā svātmabhūtaiva syān netareṣām anevaṃ vidhānām // KaUBh_5.13/2,1.13 //
body.translated_text: Moreover: the eternal — the imperishable — among the non-eternal, the perishable. The conscious — among the conscious, among those that are [seemingly] sentient — <s>Brahmā</s> and other living beings — just as burnability, which is caused by fire, does not belong to non-fire things like water and the like, so the sentience of others is caused solely by the consciousness of the <s>Ātman</s>. Furthermore, He — the omniscient, the Lord of all — fulfills the desires of the desirous beings in <s>saṃsāra</s>, [giving] the fruits of action in accordance with their <s>karma</s>, as well as desires that arise from His own grace — the one [fulfills the desires] of the many, of the countless, effortlessly — this is the meaning. The wise who perceive Him as abiding in the Self — to them belongs peace, cessation [of suffering], eternal, permanent — being their very own Self — not to others, those who are not of such nature. // KaUBh 5.13 //

children.text: tad etad iti manyante 'nirdeśyaṃ paramaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: 'This is that' — [thus] they consider [it to be] the supreme happiness that is indescribable.

children.text: kathaṃ nu tad vijānīyāṃ kim u bhāti vibhāti vā // KaU_5.14/2,2.14 //
children.translated_text: How shall I know that? Does it shine or does it shine variously? // KaU 5.14 //

body.text: yat tad ātmavijñānasukham anirdeśyaṃ nirdeṣṭum aśakyaṃ paramaṃ prakṛṣṭaṃ prākṛtapuruṣavāṅmanasayor agocaram api san nivṛttaiṣaṇā ye brāhmaṇās ta etat pratyakṣam eveti manyante, kathaṃ nu kena prakāreṇa tat sukham ahaṃ vijānīyām / idam ity ātmabuddhiviṣayam āpādayeyaṃ yathā nivṛttaiṣaṇā yatayaḥ / kim u tad bhāti dīpyate prakāśātmakaṃ tad yato 'smadbuddhigocaratvena vibhāti vispaṣṭaṃ dṛśyate kiṃ vā neti // KaUBh_5.14/2,1.14 //
body.translated_text: That bliss of Self-knowledge — indescribable, impossible to express, supreme, excellent, beyond the scope of speech and mind of ordinary persons — yet those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (seekers) who have renounced all desires perceive this as directly evident — [they think:] 'This is that.' [<s>Naciketas</s> asks:] How — by what means — shall I know that bliss? [How shall I] bring it within the scope of my own cognition, as do the renunciants who have abandoned all desires? Does it shine — is it luminous, of the nature of light — so that it shines variously (<s>vibhāti</s>), that is, becomes clearly visible as within the range of our cognition — or not? // KaUBh 5.14 //

children.text: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ nemā vidyuto bhānti kuto 'yam agniḥ /
children.translated_text: The sun does not shine there, nor the moon and stars, nor do these lightnings shine — how then this fire?

children.text: tam eva bhāntam anu bhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti // KaU_5.15/2,2.15 //
children.translated_text: Him alone shining, everything shines after; by His radiance, all this is illuminated. // KaU 5.15 //

body.text: atrottaram idaṃ bhāti ca vibhāti ceti / katham? na tatra tasmin svātmabhūte brahmaṇi sarvāvabhāsako 'pi sūryo bhāti tad brahma na prakāśayatīty arthaḥ / tathā na candratārakam, nemā vidyuto bhānti, kuto 'yam asmaddṛṣṭigocaro 'gniḥ / kiṃ bahunā, yad idam ādikaṃ sarvaṃ bhāti tat tam eva parameśvaraṃ bhāntaṃ dīpyamānam anubhāty anudīpyate / tathā jalolmukādy agnisaṃyogād agniṃ dahantam anudahati na svatas tadvat / tasyaiva bhāsā dīptyā sarvam idaṃ sūryādi vibhati / yata evaṃ tad eva brahma bhāti ca vibhāti ca / kāryagatena vividhena bhāsā tasya brahmaṇo bhārūpatvaṃ svato 'vagamyate / na hi svato 'vidyamānaṃ bhāsanam anyasya kartuṃ śaktam / ghaṭādīnām anyāvabhāsakatvādarśanād bhārūpāṇāṃ cādityādīnāṃ taddarśanāt // KaUBh_5.15/2,2.15 //
body.translated_text: Here is the answer: it both shines and shines variously. How? There — in that <s>Brahman</s> which is one's own Self — the sun does not shine, [meaning] even the sun, though illuminating everything, does not illumine that <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning. Likewise, neither the moon nor the stars; nor do these lightnings shine [there]; how then this fire within the range of our sight? What more [need be said]? Whatever this entire [universe] that shines — it shines after (<s>anubhāti</s>), it shines following Him alone, the Supreme Lord, who shines, who is luminous. Just as water, a torch, and the like — through contact with fire — burn after the burning fire, but not of themselves — so too. By His radiance alone, His luminosity, all this — the sun and the rest — shines variously. Since this is so, that <s>Brahman</s> alone both shines and shines variously. Through the manifold radiance present in [His] effects, the luminous nature (<s>bhārūpatva</s>) of that <s>Brahman</s> is understood of itself. For that which does not itself possess luminosity cannot produce illumination in another. Since pots and the like are not seen to illumine other things, while things of luminous nature like the sun and the like are [seen to do so]. // KaUBh 5.15 //

body.text: iti kaṭhavallyāṃ pañcamavallī bhāṣyam // 5 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the commentary on the fifth <s>Vallī</s> of the <s>Kaṭhavallī</s>. // 5 //

body.text: atha ṣaṣṭha vallī /
body.translated_text: Now the sixth <s>Vallī</s>.

body.text: tūlāvadhāraṇenaiva mūlāvadhāraṇaṃ vṛkṣasya yathā kriyate loke, evaṃ saṃsārakāryavṛkṣāvadhāraṇena tanmūlasya brāhmaṇaḥ svarūpāvadidhārayiṣayeyaṃ ṣaṣṭhī vally ārabhyate --
body.translated_text: Just as in the world one ascertains the root of a tree by ascertaining its crown, so too, by ascertaining the tree of the effects of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (seeker) may wish to ascertain the essential nature of its root — for this purpose, this sixth <s>Vallī</s> is commenced.

children.text:
ūrdhvamūlo avākśākha eṣo 'śvatthaḥ sanātanaḥ /
tad eva śukraṃ tad brahma tad evāmṛtam ucyate /
tasmiṃl lokāḥ śritāḥ sarve tad u nātyeti kaścana // etad vai tat // KaU_6.1/2,3.1 //
children.translated_text: With roots above and branches below, this is the eternal <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig tree). That alone is the Bright, that is <s>Brahman</s>, that alone is called the Immortal. In it all worlds rest; no one transcends it. This verily is That.

body.text: ūrdhvamūla ūrdhvaṃ mūlaṃ yat tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam asyeti so 'yam avyaktādisthāvarāntaḥ saṃsāravṛkṣa ūrdhvamūlaḥ / vṛkṣaś ca vraścanāt / avicchinnajanmajarāmaraṇaśokādyanekānarthātmakaḥ pratikṣaṇam anyathā svabhāvo māyāmarīcyudakagandharvanagarādivad dṛṣṭanaṣṭasvarūpatvād avasāne ca vṛkṣavad abhāvātmakaḥ kadalīstambhavan niḥsāro 'nekaśatapākhaṇḍabuddhivikalpāspadas tattvavijijñāsubhir anirdhāritedantattvo vedāntanirdhāritaparabrahmamūlasāro 'vidyākāmakarmāvyaktabījaprabhavo 'parabrahmavijñānakriyāśaktidvayātmakahiraṇyagarbhāṅkuraḥ sarvaprāṇiliṅgabhedaskandhas tat tat tṛṣṇājalāsekodbhūtadarpano buddhīndriyaviṣayapravālāṅkuraḥ śrutismṛtinyāyavidyopadeśapalāśo yajñadānatapodyanekakriyāsupuṣpaḥ sukhaduḥkhavedanānekarasaḥ prāṇyupajīvyānantaphalas tat tṛṣṇāsalilāvasekaprarūḍhajaṭilīkṛtadṛḍhabaddhamūlaḥ satyanāmādisaptalokabrahmādibhūtapakṣikṛtanīḍaḥ prāṇisukhaduḥkhodbhūtaharṣaśokajātanṛtyagītavāditrakṣvelitāsphoṭitahasitākṛṣṭaruditahāhāmuñcamuñcetyādyanekaśabdakṛtatumulībhūtamahāravo vedāntavihitabrahmātmadarśanāsaṅgaśastrakṛtoccheda eṣa saṃsāravṛkṣo 'śvattho 'śvatthavat kāmakarmavāteritanityapracalitasvabhāvaḥ / svarganarakatiryakpretādibhiḥ śākhābhir avākśākhaḥ / sanātano 'nāditvāc ciraṃ pravṛttaḥ / yad asya saṃsāravṛkṣasya mūlaṃ tad eva śukraṃ śubhraṃ śuddhaṃ jyotiṣmac caitanyātmajyotiḥsvabhāvaṃ tad eva brahma sarvamahattvāt / tad evāmṛtam avināśasvabhāvam ucyate kathyate satyatvāt / vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyam anṛtam anyadato martyam / tasmin paramārthasatye brahmaṇi lokā gandharvanagaramarīcyudakamāyāsamāḥ paramārthadarśanābhāvāvagamanāḥ śritāśritāḥ sarve samastā utpattisthitilayeṣu / tad u tadbrahma nātyeti nātivartate mṛdādikam iva ghaṭādikāryaṃ kaścana kaścid api vikāraḥ / etad vai tat // KaUBh_6.1/2,3.1 //
body.translated_text: With roots above — that whose root is above, which is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s>, extending from the <s>Avyakta</s> (Unmanifest) down to immobile beings, has its roots above. And it is a tree (<s>vṛkṣa</s>) because it is cut down (<s>vraścanāt</s>). It consists of the countless miseries of unbroken birth, old age, death, grief, and the like; its nature changes from moment to moment; like the water of a mirage, a <s>gandharva</s>-city, or <s>māyā</s>, its form appears and vanishes; ultimately, like a tree, it is of the nature of non-existence; like a plantain trunk, it is without substance; it is the locus of hundreds of divisions of false intellectual constructions; its true nature cannot be determined by those who wish to know reality; its essential core is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> as root, as established by <s>Vedānta</s>; it arises from the seed of the <s>Avyakta</s> (Unmanifest), consisting of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), desire, and <s>karma</s>; its sprout is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the lower <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is the dual power of knowledge and action; its trunk is the various <s>liṅga</s>-bodies (subtle bodies) of all living beings; its branches grow tall, watered by the flowing waters of the thirst for this and that; its tender shoots and leaves are the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), the senses, and their objects; its foliage is the teachings of <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, logic, and the sciences; its abundant flowers are the many rites such as sacrifice, charity, <s>tapas</s> (austerity), and worship; its diverse flavors are the experiences of pleasure and pain; its endless fruits are what sustain all living beings; its roots, grown strong, matted, and firmly bound, are nourished by the waters of the thirst for this and that; its nests are built by the bird-like beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to the [lowest creatures] in the seven worlds beginning with <s>Satya</s>; its tremendous noise is the tumultuous sound created by the manifold sounds of rejoicing and lamentation born of the pleasure and pain of living beings — dancing, singing, playing instruments, clapping, striking, laughing, pulling, weeping, cries of 'alas!' and 'let go! let go!' and the like; and this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> is cut down by the weapon of non-attachment through the vision of <s>Brahman</s> as the Self, as prescribed by <s>Vedānta</s>. This is the <s>Aśvattha</s> — like an <s>Aśvattha</s> tree, whose nature is eternally in motion, agitated by the winds of desire and <s>karma</s>. With branches below — <s>avākśākha</s> — through [its] branches in the form of heaven, hell, animal, ghost realms, and the like. It is <s>sanātana</s> (eternal) — being beginningless, it has been in operation for a long time. The root of this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> — that alone is the <s>śukra</s> (bright), the pure, the luminous, of the nature of the light of consciousness as the Self. That alone is <s>Brahman</s>, because it is greater than everything great. That alone is called <s>amṛta</s> (immortal), of indestructible nature, because it is real. 'What is expressed by speech is a modification, a mere name, unreal' — all else besides it is mortal. In that <s>Brahman</s> which is the ultimate reality, all the worlds — comparable to a <s>gandharva</s>-city, mirage-water, or <s>māyā</s> — cognized [only] in the absence of the realization of the ultimate truth — rest, are established, all of them in their entirety, in their arising, abiding, and dissolution. And no modification whatsoever transcends that <s>Brahman</s>, just as pots and the like [never transcend] clay and the like. This verily is That.

children.text: yad idaṃ kiṃca jagat sarvaṃ prāṇa ejati niḥsṛtam /
children.translated_text: Whatever there is in this world — all of it moves, having issued forth from <s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath, i.e., <s>Brahman</s>).

children.text: mahad bhayaṃ vajram udyataṃ ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti // KaU_6.2/2,3.2 //
children.translated_text: It is the great fear, the thunderbolt raised aloft. Those who know this become immortal.

body.text: yad vijñānād amṛtā bhavantīty ucyate, jagato mūlaṃ tad eva nāsti brahmāsata evedaṃ niḥsṛtam iti tan na / yad idaṃ kiñ ca yat kiṃ cedaṃ jagatsarvaṃ prāṇe / parasmin brahmaṇi satyejati kampate, tata eva niḥsṛtaṃ nirgataṃ satpracalati niyamena ceṣṭate / yad evaṃ jagadutpattyādikāraṇaṃ brahma tanmahadbhayam / mahac ca tad bhayaṃ ca bibhety asmād iti mahadbhayam / vajram udyatam udyatām iva vajram / yathā vajrodyatakaraṃ svāminam abhimukhībhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhṛtyā niyamena tac chāsane vartante, tathedaṃ candrādityagrahanakṣatratārakādilakṣaṇaṃ jagatseśvaraṃ niyamena kṣaṇam apy aviśrāntaṃ vartata ity uktaṃ bhavati / ya etad viduḥ svātmapravṛttisākṣibhūtam ekaṃ brahmāmṛtā amaraṇadharmāṇāste bhavanti // KaUBh_6.2/2,3.2 //
body.translated_text: If it were said that since 'they become immortal through its knowledge,' the root of the universe does not exist — that <s>Brahman</s> does not exist and this [universe] has issued from non-being — that is not so. Whatever there is, whatever exists as this universe — all of it moves, trembles, in <s>Prāṇa</s>, in the supreme <s>Brahman</s> which is real. Having issued forth from that very [<s>Brahman</s>], having emerged, it moves, functions in a regulated manner. That <s>Brahman</s> which is thus the cause of the origin and the like of the universe — that is the great fear. It is great and it is fear — because [everything] fears it, hence 'the great fear.' Like a thunderbolt raised aloft — like a thunderbolt held high. Just as servants, seeing a master with a raised thunderbolt facing them, function in a regulated manner under his command, so too this universe — characterized by the moon, sun, planets, constellations, stars, and the like — together with its lord, functions in a regulated manner, not resting even for a moment; this is what is stated. Those who know this — the one <s>Brahman</s> that is the witness of one's own activity — they become immortal, attaining the nature of deathlessness.

children.text: bhayād asyāgnis tapati bhayāt tapati sūryaḥ /
children.translated_text: Out of fear of it, <s>Agni</s> (fire) burns; out of fear, the sun shines.

children.text: bhayād indraś ca vāyuś ca mṛtyur dhāvati pañcamaḥ // KaU_6.3/2,3.3 //
children.translated_text: Out of fear, <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), and Death as the fifth, all run.

body.text: kathaṃ tadbhayāj jagadvartata ity āha -- bhayād bhītyāsya parameśvarasyāgnis tapati, bhayāt tapati sūryo, bhayād indraś ca vāyuś ca mṛtyur dhāvati pañcamaḥ / na hīśvarāṇāṃ lokapālānāṃ samarthānāṃ satāṃ niyantā ced vajrodyatakaravan na syāt svāmibhayabhītānām iva bhṛtyānāṃ niyatā pravṛtir upapadyate // KaUBh_6.3/2,3.3 //
body.translated_text: How does the universe function out of fear of it? He says: Out of fear, out of dread of this supreme Lord, <s>Agni</s> (fire) burns; out of fear, the sun shines; out of fear, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), and Death as the fifth, all run. For if there were no controller over the mighty lords, the guardians of the worlds, like [a master] with raised thunderbolt, the regulated activity [of the cosmic forces] — as of servants afraid of their master's authority — would not be possible.

children.text: iha ced aśakad boddhuṃ prākśarīrasya visrasaḥ /
children.translated_text: If one was able to know [it] here [in this life], before the dissolution of the body —

children.text: tataḥ sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya kalpate // KaU_6.4/2,3.4 //
children.translated_text: then, in the created worlds, one becomes fit for embodiment.

body.text: tac ceha jīvann eva ced yady aśakac chaknoti śaktaḥ san jānāty etad bhayakāraṇaṃ brahma boddhum avagantuṃ prak pūrvaṃ śarīrasya visraso 'vasraṃsanāt patanāt saṃsārabandhanād vimucyate / na ced aśakadboddhum, tato 'navabodhāt sargeṣu, sṛjyante yeṣu sraṣṭavyāḥ prāṇina iti sargāḥ pṛthivyādayo lokās teṣu sargeṣu lokeṣu śarīratvāya śarīrabhāvāya kalpate samartho bhavati śarīraṃ gṛhṇātīty arthaḥ // tasmāc charīravisraṃsanāt prāgātmāvabodhāya nāstheyaḥ / yasmād ihaivātmano darśanam ādarśasthasyeva mukhasya spaṣṭamupapadyate na lokāntareṣu brahmalokād anyatra / sa ca duṣprāpaḥ // KaUBh_6.4/2,3.4 //
body.translated_text: And if here, while still alive, if one was able — if one is capable, being empowered — to know this <s>Brahman</s>, the cause of [universal] fear, to comprehend it, before the dissolution, the falling, the disintegration of the body — then one is released from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. But if one was not able to know [it], then, due to non-comprehension, in the created realms — the worlds such as earth and others in which creatures are to be created, the <s>sargas</s> (creations) — one becomes fit for embodiment, for the state of having a body; that is, one takes on a body; this is the meaning. Therefore, one should strive for the knowledge of the Self before the dissolution of the body. Since here [in this life] alone the vision of the Self is possible clearly — as of one's face in a mirror — and not in other worlds, except in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>. And that [world of <s>Brahmā</s>] is hard to attain.

body.text: katham ity ucyate --
body.translated_text: How so? It is said:

children.text: yathādarśe tathātmani yathā svapne tathā pitṛloke /
children.translated_text: As in a mirror, so in one's own self; as in a dream, so in the world of the fathers.

children.text: yathāpsu parīva dadṛśe tathā gandharvaloke chāyātapayor iva brahmaloke // KaU_6.5/2,3.5 //
children.translated_text: As if seen in water, so in the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s>; as of shadow and light, so in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

body.text: yathādarśe pratibimbabhūtam ātmānaṃ paśyati loko 'tyantaviviktam, tathehātmani svabuddhāvādarśavan nirmalībhūtāyāṃ viviktam ātmano darśanaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ / yathā svapne 'viviktaṃ jāgradvāsanodbhūtam, tathā pitṛloke 'viviktam eva darśanam ātmanaḥ karmaphalopabhogāsaktatvāt / yathā cāpsv aviviktāvayavam ātmarūpaṃ parīva dadṛśe paridṛśyata iva, tathā gandharvaloke 'viviktam eva darśanam ātmanaḥ / evañ ca lokāntareṣv api śāstraprāmāṇyād avagamyate / chāyātapayor ivātyantaviviktaṃ brahmaloka evaikasmin / sa ca duṣprāpo 'tyantaviśiṣṭakarmajñānasādhyatvāt / tasmād ātmadarśanāyehaiva yatnaḥ kartavya ity abhiprāyaḥ // KaUBh_6.5/2,3.5 //
body.translated_text: Just as one sees one's reflection in a mirror — utterly distinct — so here, in one's own <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), when it has become pure like a mirror, the distinct vision of the Self occurs; this is the meaning. Just as in a dream, [the vision is] indistinct, arising from waking impressions, so in the world of the fathers the vision of the Self is indistinct alone, because of being engaged in the enjoyment of the fruits of <s>karma</s>. Just as in water, one's form with indistinct parts <s>parīva dadṛśe</s> (is seen as if), so in the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s> the vision of the Self is indistinct alone. And thus, from the authority of scripture, it is understood that in other worlds too [the vision is indistinct]. Only in the world of <s>Brahmā</s> alone is [the vision] utterly distinct, as of shadow and light. And that [world of <s>Brahmā</s>] is hard to attain, because it requires the most distinguished <s>karma</s> and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) as means. Therefore, effort for the vision of the Self should be made here [in this life] alone; this is the purport.

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāvam udayāstamayau ca yat /
children.translated_text: The separate nature of the senses, and their rising and setting —

children.text: pṛthag utpadyamānānāṃ matvā dhīro na śocati // KaU_6.6/2,3.6 //
children.translated_text: knowing that they arise separately, the wise one does not grieve.

body.text: katham asau boddhavyaḥ kiṃ vā tadavabodhe prayojanam ity ucyate -- indriyāṇāṃ śrotrādīnāṃ svasvaviṣayagrahaṇaprayojanena svakāraṇebhya ākāśādibhyaḥ pṛthagutpadyamānānām atyantaviśuddhāt kevalāc cinmātrātmasvarūpāt pṛthagbhāvaṃ svabhāvavilakṣaṇātmakatām, tathā teṣām evendriyāṇām udayāstamayau cotpattipralayau jāgratsvāpnāvasthāpekṣayā nātmanas tāv iti matvā jñātvā vivekato dhīro dhīmān na śocati / ātmano nityaikasvabhāvatvāvyabhicārāc chokakāraṇatvānupapatteḥ / tathā ca śrutyantaraṃ

children.text: "tarati śokam ātmavit" (ChU 7,1.3)
children.translated_text: "The knower of the Self crosses over sorrow" (<s>ChU</s> 7.1.3)
— thus.

body.translated_text: How is that [Self] to be known? And what is the purpose of knowing it? It is said: The senses — hearing and the others — arising separately from their respective causes, the elements such as space and the like, each for the purpose of grasping its own respective object — [knowing] their separate nature (<s>pṛthagbhāva</s>), their having a nature distinct from the utterly pure, bare, purely conscious Self, as well as their rising and setting — their origination and dissolution with reference to the waking and dream states, [knowing that] these belong to the senses and not to the Self — having known, having discerned this discriminatively, the wise one, the one possessed of wisdom, does not grieve. Because the Self is of an eternally single nature that never deviates, the causation of grief is impossible [for it]. And another <s>śruti</s> [states]:

children.text: indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mano manasaḥ sattvam uttamam /
children.translated_text: Higher than the senses is the mind; higher than the mind is <s>sattva</s> (the pure intellect).

children.text: sattvād adhi mahānātmā mahato 'vyaktam uttamam // KaU_6.7/2,3.7 //
children.translated_text: Higher than <s>sattva</s> is the great Self (<s>Mahān Ātmā</s>); higher than the Great is the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>).

body.text: yasmād ātmana indriyāṇāṃ pṛthagbhāva ukto nāsau bahir adhigantavyo yasmāt pratyagātmā sa sarvasya, tat katham ity ucyate -- indriyebhyaḥ paraṃ mana ity ādi / arthānām ihendrayasamānajātīyatvād indriyagrahaṇenaiva grahaṇam / pūrvavad anyat / sattvaśabdād buddhir ihocyate // KaUBh_6.7/2,3.7 //
body.translated_text: Since it was stated that the senses have a nature separate from the Self, that [Self] is not to be sought externally, because it is the inner Self of everything. How then? It is said: higher than the senses is the mind, and so on. Here, because the objects are of the same class as the senses, the mention of the senses includes [the objects] as well. The rest is as before. By the word <s>sattva</s>, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is meant here.

children.text: avyaktāt tu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako 'liṅga eva ca /
children.translated_text: But higher than the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>) is <s>Puruṣa</s> — all-pervading and indeed without any mark.

children.text: yaṃ jñātvā mucyate jantur amṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati // KaU_6.8/2,3.8 //
children.translated_text: Knowing whom, a living being is liberated and attains immortality.

body.text: avyaktāt tu paraḥ puruṣo vyāpako, vyāpakasyāpy ākāśādeḥ sarvasya kāraṇatvād aliṅgo liṅgyate gamyate yena tal liṅgaṃ budhyādi, tad avidyamānaṃ yasya so 'yam aliṅga eva ca / sarvasaṃsāradharmavarjita ity etat / yaṃ jñātvācāryataḥ śāstrataś ca mucyate jantur avidyādihṛdayagranthibhir jīvann eva, patite 'pi śarīre 'mṛtatvaṃ ca gacchati / so 'liṅgaḥ paro 'vyaktāt puruṣa iti pūrveṇaiva sambandhaḥ // KaUBh_6.8/2,3.8 //

children.text: na saṃdṛśe tiṣṭhati rūpam asya na cakṣuṣā paśyati kaścanainam /
hṛdā manīṣā manasābhikḷpto ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti // KaU_6.9/2,3.9 //

body.text: kathaṃ tarhi tasyāliṅgasya darśanam upapadyata ity ucyate na san dṛśe san darśanaviṣaye na tiṣṭhati pratyagātmano 'sya rūpam / ato na cakṣuṣā sarvendriyeṇa, cakṣurgrahaṇasyopalākṣaṇārthatvāt, paśyati nopalabhate kaścana kaścid apy enaṃ prakṛtam ātmānam / kathaṃ tarhi taṃ paśyed ity ucyate -- hṛdā hṛtsthayā buddhyā / manīṣā manasaḥ saṅkalpādirūpasyeṣṭe niyantṛtveneti manīṭ tayā manīṣāvikalpayitryā buddhyā / manasā mananarūpeṇa samyag darśanenābhikḷpto 'bhisamarthito 'bhiprakāśita ity etat / ātmā jñātuṃ śakya iti vākyaśeṣaḥ / tam ātmānaṃ brahmaitad ye vidur amṛtās te bhavanti // KaUBh_6.9/2,3.9 //

children.text: yadā pañcāvatiṣṭhante jñānāni manasā saha /
buddhiś ca na viceṣṭati tām āhuḥ paramāṃ gatim // KaU_6.10/2,3.10 //

body.text: sā hṛnmanīṭ kathaṃ prāpyata iti tad artho yoga ucyate -- yadā yasmin kāle svaviṣayebhyo nivartitānyātmany eva pañca jñānāni / jñānārthatvāc chrotrādīnīndriyāṇi jñānāny ucyante / avatiṣṭhante saha manasā yad anugatāni, tena saṃkalpādivyāvṛttenāntaḥkaraṇena / buddhiś cādhyavasāyalakṣaṇā na viceṣṭati svavyāpāreṣu na viceṣṭate na vyāpriyate, tām āhuḥ paramā gatim // KaUBh_6.10/2,3.10 //

children.text: tāṃ yogam iti manyante sthirām indriyadhāraṇām /
apramattas tadā bhavati yogo hi prabhavāpyayau // KaU_6.11/2,3.11 //

body.text: tām īdṛśīṃ tadavasthāṃ yogam iti manyante viyogam eva santam / sarvānarthasaṃyogaviyogalakṣaṇā hīyam avasthā yoginaḥ / etasyāṃ hy avasthāyām avidyādhyāropaṇavarjitasvarūpapratiṣṭha ātmā / sthirām indrayadhāraṇāṃ sthirām acalām indrayadhāraṇāṃ bāhyāntaḥkaraṇānāṃ dhāraṇam ity arthaḥ / apramattaḥ pramādavarjitaḥ samādhānaṃ prati nityaṃ yatnavāṃs tadā tasmin kāle, yadaiva pravṛttayogo bhavatīti sāmarthyād avagamyate / na hi buddhyādiceṣṭābhāve pramādasaṃbhavo 'sti / tasmāt prāg eva buddhyādiceṣṭoparamād apramādo vidhīyate / athavā yadaivendriyāṇāṃ sthirā dhāraṇā, tadānīm eva niraṅkuśam apramattatvam ity ato 'bhidhīyate 'pramattas tadā bhavatīti / kutaḥ / yogo hi yasmāt prabhavāpyayāv upajanāpāyadharmaka ity arthaḥ / ato 'pāyaparihārāyāpramādaḥ kartavya ity abhiprāyaḥ // KaUBh_6.11/2,3.11 //

children.text: naiva vācā na manasā prāptuṃ śakyo na cakṣuṣā /
astīti bruvato 'nyatra kathaṃ tad upalabhyate // KaU_6.12/2,3.12 //

body.text: buddhyādiceṣṭāviṣayaṃ ced brahmedaṃ tad iti viśeṣato gṛhyeta, buddhyādyuparame ca grahaṇakāraṇābhāvād anupalabhyamānaṃ nāsty eva brahma / yad dhi karaṇagocaraṃ tad astīti prasiddhaṃ loke viparītaṃ cāsad iti / ataś cānarthako yogo 'anupalabhyamānatvād vā nāstīty upalabdhavyaṃ brahmety evaṃ prāpta idam ucyate / satyam / naiva vācā na manasā na cakṣuṣā nānyair apīndriyaiḥ prāptuṃ śakyata ity arthaḥ / tathāpi sarvaviśeṣarahito 'pi jagato mūlam ity avagatatvād asty eva, kāryapravilāpanasyāstitvaniṣṭhatvāt / tathā hīdaṃ kāryaṃ sūkṣmatāratamyapāramparyeṇānugamyamānaṃ sadbuddhiniṣṭhām evāvagamayati / yadāpi viṣayapravilāpanena pravilāpyamānā buddhis tadāpi sā satpratyayagarbhaiva vilīyate / buddhir hi naḥ pramāṇaṃ sadasator yāthātmyāvagame / mūlaṃ cej jagato na syād asad anvitam evedaṃ kāryam asad ity evaṃ gṛhyeta, na tv etad asti, satyasad ity eva tu gṛhyate, yathā mṛdādikāryaṃ ghaṭādi mṛdādyanvitam / tasmāj jagato mūlam ātmāstīty evopalabdhavyaḥ / kasmāt / astīti bruvato 'stitvavādina āgamārthānusāriṇaḥ śraddadhānād anyatra nāstikavādini nāsti jagato mūlam ātmā niranvayam evedaṃ kāryam abhāvāntaṃ pravilīyata iti manyamāne viparītadarśini, kathaṃ tad brahma tattvata upalabhyate, na kathañcanopalabhyata ity arthaḥ // KaUBh_6.12/2,3.12 //

children.text: astīty evopalabdhavyas tattvabhāvena cobhayoḥ /
astīty evopalabdhasya tattvabhāvaḥ prasīdati // KaU_6.13/2,3.13 //

body.text: tasmād apohyāsadvādipakṣam āsuram astīty evātmopalabdhavyaḥ satkāryabuddhyādyupādhibhiḥ / yadā tu tadrahito 'vikriya ātmā kāryaṃ ca kāraṇavyatirekeṇa nāsti

children.text: "vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyaṃ mṛttikety eva satyam" (ChU 6,1.4)

iti śruteḥ / tadā tasya nirupādhikasyāliṅgasya sadasadādipratyayaviṣayatvavarjitasyātmanas tattvabhāvo bhavati / tena ca rūpeṇātmopalabdhavya ity anuvartate / tatrāpy ubhayoḥ sopādhikanirupādhikayor astitvatattvabhāvayoḥ -- nirdhāraṇārthā ṣaṣṭhī -- pūrvam astīty evopalabdhasyātmanaḥ satkāryopādhikṛtāstitvapratyayenopalabdhasyety arthaḥ / paścāt pratyastamitasarvopādhirūpa ātmanas tattvabhāvo viditāviditābhyāmanyo 'dvayasvabhāvo "neti neti"
"asthūlam anaṇv ahrasvam" (BĀU 3,8.8)
"adṛśye 'nātmye 'nirukte 'nilayane" (TaittU 2,7.1)
ity ādi śrutinirdiṣṭaḥ prasīdatyabhimukhībhavati / ātmaprakāśanāya pūrvam astīty upalabdhavata ity etat // KaUBh_6.13/2,3.13 //
yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ /
atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty atra brahma samaśnute // KaU_6.14/2,3.14 //

body.text: evaṃ paramārthātmadarśino yadā yasmin kāle sarve kāmāḥ kāmayitavyasyānyasyābhāvāt, pramucyante, viśīryante, ye 'sya prāk pratibodhād viduṣo hṛdi buddhau śritā āśritāḥ / buddhir hi kāmānām āśrayo nātmā

children.text: "kāmaḥ saṅkalpaḥ" (BĀU 1,5.3)

ity ādiśrutyantarāc ca / atha tadā martyaḥ prāk prabodhād āsīt sa prabodhottarakālam avidyākāmakarmalakṣaṇasya mṛtyor vināśād amṛto bhavati, gamanaprayojakasya mṛtyor vinaśād gamanānupapatter atrehaiva pradipanirvāṇavatsarvabandhanopaśamād brahma samaśnute brahmaiva bhavatīty arthaḥ // KaUBh_6.14/2,3.14 //
yadā sarve prabhidyante hṛdayasyeha granthayaḥ /
atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty etāvad dhy anuśāsanam // KaU_6.15/2,3.15 //

body.text: kadā punaḥ kāmānāṃ mūlato vināśa ity ucyate -- yadā sarve prabhidyante bhedam upayānti vinaśyanti hṛdayasya buddher iha jīvata eva granthayo granthivad dṛḍhabandhanarūpā avidyāpratyayā ity arthaḥ / aham idaṃ śarīraṃ mamedaṃ dhanaṃ sukhī duḥkhī cāham ity evam ādilkṣaṇās tadviparītabrahmātmapratyayopajananād brahmaivāham asmy asaṃsārīti vinaṣṭeṣv avidyāgranthiṣu tannimittāḥ kāmā mūlato vinaśyanti / atha matryo 'mṛto bhavaty etāvad dhy etāvad evaitāvan mātraṃ nādhikam astīty āśaṅkā kartavyā / anuśāsanam anuśiṣṭir upadeśaḥ sarvavedāntānām iti vākyaśeṣaḥ // KaUBh_6.15/2,3.15 //
body.translated_text: When, then, does the root-destruction of desires occur? — it is said: when all the knots (<s>granthayaḥ</s>) of the heart, of the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), are severed (<s>prabhidyante</s>), i.e., undergo destruction, broken apart — here, in this very life — the knots that are like tight bindings in the form of <s>avidyā</s>-cognitions, that is the meaning. [Such as:] 'I am this body,' 'this wealth is mine,' 'I am happy,' 'I am miserable' — characterized by such [misconceptions]. When those <s>avidyā</s>-knots are destroyed through the arising of the opposite cognition of the <s>Brahman</s>-<s>Ātman</s> — 'I am <s>Brahman</s> alone, I am not a being in <s>saṃsāra</s>' — then the desires caused by those [knots] are destroyed at their root. Then the mortal becomes immortal. This much indeed — precisely this much and no more — one should suspect [i.e., this is all that need be said]. The teaching — the instruction, the <s>upadeśa</s> — of all the <s>Vedāntas</s> (Upaniṣads) — this is the completion of the sentence. (<s>KaUBh</s> 6.15/2.3.15)

children.text: śataṃ caikā ca hṛdayasya nāḍyas tāsāṃ mūrdhānam abhiniḥsṛtaikā /
children.translated_text: One hundred and one are the channels (<s>nāḍīs</s>) of the heart; of these, one passes out through the crown of the head.

children.text: tayordhvam āyann amṛtatvam eti viṣvaṅṅ anyā utkramaṇe bhavati // KaU_6.16/2,3.16 //
children.translated_text: Going upward by it, one attains immortality; the others, going in various directions, serve as [paths of] departure [into <s>saṃsāra</s>]. (<s>KaU</s> 6.16/2.3.16)

body.text: nirastāśeṣaviśeṣavyāpibrahmātmapratipattyā prabhinnasamastāvidyādigranther jīvata eva brahmabhūtasya viduṣo na gatir vidyate

children.text: "atra brahma samaśnute" (BĀU 4,4.7)
children.translated_text: "Here he attains <s>Brahman</s>" (<s>BĀU</s> 4.4.7)

children.text: ity uktatvāt
children.translated_text: — because it has been so stated;

children.text: "na tasya prāṇā utkāmanti brahmaiva san brahmāpyeti" (BĀU 4,4.6)
children.translated_text: "Being <s>Brahman</s>, he merges in <s>Brahman</s>; his vital breaths do not depart" (<s>BĀU</s> 4.4.6)

children.text: iti śrutyantarāc ca / ye punar mandabrahmavido vidyāntaraśīlinaś ca brahmalokabhājo ye ca tadviparītāḥ saṃsārabhājaḥ, teṣām eva gativiśeṣa ucyate prakṛtotkṛṣṭabrahmavidyāphalastutaye / kiñ cānyad agnividyā pṛṣṭā pratyuktā ca / tasyāś ca phalaprāptiprakāro vaktavya iti mantrārambhaḥ / tatra -- śataṃ ca śatasaṅkhyākā ekā ca suṣumnā nāma puruṣasya hṛdayād viniḥsṛtā nāḍyaḥ śirāḥ, tāsāṃ madhye mūrdhānaṃ bhittvābhiniḥsṛtā nirgatā ekā suṣumnā nāma / tayāntakāle hṛdaya ātmānaṃ vaśīkṛtya yojayet / tayā nāḍyor dhvam uparyāyan gacchann ādityadvāreṇāmṛtatvam amaraṇadharmatvam āpekṣikam --
children.translated_text: — and because of another <s>śruti</s> (scripture) as well. But for those who are knowers of <s>Brahman</s> of a lesser degree, and those who practice other kinds of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and are destined for <s>Brahmaloka</s>, and those of the opposite kind who are destined for <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — for them alone the specific [paths of] departure are stated, in order to glorify the fruit of the supreme knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> that is the main subject. Moreover, the fire-knowledge (<s>agnividyā</s>) was asked about and answered; its mode of fruit-attainment must also be stated — hence the commencement of the <s>mantra</s>. Regarding that: one hundred and one — numbering one hundred — and one [more] called <s>suṣumnā</s> — emerging from the heart of a person, are the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels), the veins. Among them, one, named <s>suṣumnā</s>, having pierced through the crown of the head, has emerged — gone out. By that [<s>suṣumnā</s>], at the time of death, having placed the <s>Ātman</s> in the heart under [its] control and directed [it], one goes upward, ascending through the gateway of the sun and attains '<s>amṛtatva</s>' (immortality) — the relative state of non-dying —

children.text: "ābhūtasamplavaṃ sthānam amṛtatvaṃ hi bhāṣyate" (ViP 2,8.17)
