children.translated_text: "The state lasting until the dissolution of the elements (<s>ābhūtasamplava</s>) is called immortality" (<s>ViP</s> 2.8.17)

children.text: iti smṛteḥ -- brahmaṇā vā saha kālāntareṇa mukhyam amṛtatvam eti bhuktvā bhogān anupamān brahmalokagatān / viṣvaṅnānāvidhagatayo 'nyā nāḍya utkramaṇe bhavanti saṃsārapratipattyarthā eva bhavantīty arthāḥ // KaUBh_6.16/2,3.16 //
children.translated_text: — according to this <s>smṛti</s>. Or, in due course of time, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, one attains absolute immortality — having enjoyed the incomparable pleasures of <s>Brahmaloka</s>. The other <s>nāḍīs</s>, going in various directions, of manifold courses, at the time of departure, serve as [paths] for the return to <s>saṃsāra</s> indeed — that is the meaning. (<s>KaUBh</s> 6.16/2.3.16)

body.translated_text: For the <s>vidvān</s> (knower) who, through the realization of the <s>Brahman</s>-<s>Ātman</s> pervading all particularities without exception, has become <s>Brahman</s> itself while still living, with all knots of <s>avidyā</s> and the like severed — there is no [separate] departure (<s>gati</s>),

children.text:
aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ /
taṃ svāc charīrāt pravṛhen muñjād iveṣīkāṃ dhairyeṇa /
taṃ vidyāc chukram amṛtaṃ taṃ vidyāc chukram amṛtam iti // KaU_6.17/2,3.17 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣa</s> of the measure of a thumb, the inner <s>Ātman</s>, is always seated in the heart of beings. One should draw him out from one's own body, as one draws a reed from <s>muñja</s> grass, with firmness. One should know him as the pure, the immortal — one should know him as the pure, the immortal. (<s>KaU</s> 6.17/2.3.17)

body.text: idānīṃ sarvavallyarthopasaṃhārārtham āha -- aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo 'ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ sambandhini hṛdaye san niviṣṭo yathā vyākhyātaḥ, taṃ svādātmīyāc charīrāt pravṛhed udyacchen niṣkarṣet pṛthak kuryād ity arthaḥ / kim ivety ucyate -- muñjādiveṣīkāmantasthāṃ dhairyeṇāpramādena / taṃ śarīrān niṣkṛṣṭaṃ cinmātraṃ vidyādvijānīyāc chukraṃ śuddham amṛtaṃ yathoktaṃ brahmeti / dvir vacanam upaniṣat parisamāpty artham iti śabdaś ca // KaUBh_6.17/2,3.17 //
body.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of summarizing the meaning of all the <s>vallīs</s>, he says: The <s>Puruṣa</s> of the measure of a thumb, the inner <s>Ātman</s>, always seated in the heart that belongs to beings — as has been explained. One should draw him out (<s>pravṛhet</s>), extract, pull out, separate him from one's own body — that is the meaning. Like what? — it is said: like a reed from <s>muñja</s> [grass], the inner stalk — with firmness (<s>dhairya</s>), with unfailing vigilance. Having thus extracted him from the body, one should know — should understand — that consciousness alone (<s>cinmātra</s>) as '<s>śukra</s>' (pure, bright), as '<s>amṛta</s>' (immortal) — as <s>Brahman</s>, as described. The repetition [of the last phrase] is for the purpose of concluding the <s>Upaniṣad</s>; and the word '<s>iti</s>' [marks the same]. (<s>KaUBh</s> 6.17/2.3.17)

children.text: mṛtyuproktāṃ naciketo 'tha labdhvā vidyām etāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnam /
children.translated_text: <s>Naciketas</s>, having received this knowledge taught by Death (<s>Mṛtyu</s>), together with the complete discipline of <s>yoga</s> —

children.text: brahmaprāpto virajo 'bhūd vimṛtyur anyo 'py evaṃ yo vid adhyātmam eva // KaU_6.18/2,3.18 //
children.translated_text: attained <s>Brahman</s>, became free from impurity and free from death; so too any other who thus knows the inner Self. (<s>KaU</s> 6.18/2.3.18)

body.text: vidyāstutyartho 'yam ākhyāyikārthopasaṃhāro 'dhunocyate -- mṛtyuproktām etāṃ yathoktāṃ brahmavidyāṃ yogavidhiṃ ca kṛtsnaṃ samastaṃ sopakaraṇaṃ saphalam ity etat / naciketo 'tha varapradānān mṛtyor labdhvā prāpyety arthaḥ / kim? brahma prāpto 'bhūn mukto 'bhavad ity arthaḥ / katham? vidyāprāptyā virajo vigatadharmādharmo vimṛtyur vigatakāmāvidyaś ca san pūrvam ity arthaḥ / na kevalaṃ naciketā evānyo 'pi ya evaṃ naciketovad ātmavid adhyātmam eva nirupacaritaṃ pratyak svarūpaṃ prāpya tattvam evety abhiprāyaḥ / nānyad rūpam apratyag rūpam / tad evam adhyātmam evam uktaprakāreṇa veda vijānātīty evaṃvit so 'pi virajāḥ san brahma prāpya vimṛtyur bhavatīti vākyaśeṣaḥ // KaUBh_6.18/2,3.18 //
body.translated_text: This concluding summary of the narrative is now stated, for the purpose of glorifying the knowledge: Having received from Death, through the granting of boons, this knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> as described, together with the complete, entire discipline of <s>yoga</s> — complete with its auxiliary means and its fruit — that is the meaning. <s>Naciketas</s>, having obtained [it] — having received, that is the meaning. What [happened]? He attained <s>Brahman</s>, he became liberated — that is the meaning. How? Through the attainment of knowledge, he became '<s>viraja</s>' (free from impurity) — free from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>; '<s>vimṛtyu</s>' (free from death) — free from desire and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); having become so previously — that is the meaning. Not <s>Naciketas</s> alone, but any other too who thus, like <s>Naciketas</s>, knows the <s>Ātman</s> — '<s>adhyātmam eva</s>' means the inner Self without superimposition, the inward reality — having attained that very truth, the essence — this is the purport. Not any other, outward form [is to be sought]. Thus, one who knows '<s>adhyātmam eva</s>' — the inner Self in the manner described — that knower too, being free from impurity, having attained <s>Brahman</s>, becomes free from death — this is the completion of the sentence. (<s>KaUBh</s> 6.18/2.3.18)

children.text: saha nāv avatu / saha nau bhunaktu / saha vīryaṃ karavāvahai //
children.translated_text: May He protect us both together. May He nourish us both together. May we both work together with vigor.

children.text: tejasvi nāvadhītam astu mā vidviṣāvahai // KaU_6.19/2,3.19 //
children.translated_text: May our study be luminous. May we not hate each other. (<s>KaU</s> 6.19/2.3.19)

body.text: oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Peace, peace, peace.

body.text: iti kaṭhopaniṣadi dvitīyādhyāye tṛtīyā vallī //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>vallī</s> of the second <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Kaṭhopaniṣad</s>.

body.text: śiṣyācāryayoḥ pramādakṛtānyāyena vidyāgrahaṇapratipādananimittadoṣapraśamanārtheyaṃ śāntir ucyate -- saha nāv āvām avatu pālayatu vidyāsvarūpaprakāśanena / kaḥ? sa eva parameśvara upaniṣat prakāśitaḥ / kiñ ca saha nau bhunaktu tatphalaprakāśanena nau pālayatu / sahaivāvāṃ vidyākṛtaṃ vīryaṃ sāmathryaṃ karavāvahai niṣpādayāvahai / kiñ ca tejasvi nau tejasvi naurāvayor yad adhītaṃ tat svadhītam astu / athavā tejasvi nāvāvābhyāṃ yad adhītaṃ tad atīva tejasvi vīryavad astv ity arthaḥ / mā vidviṣāvahai śiṣyācāryāv anyonyaṃ pramādakṛtānyāyādhyayanādhyāpanadoṣanimittaṃ dveṣaṃ mā karavāvahai ity arthaḥ / śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntir iti trir vacanaṃ sarvadoṣopaśamanārtham ity om iti // KaUBh_6.19/2,3.19 //
body.translated_text: This <s>śānti</s> (peace invocation) is uttered for the purpose of pacifying faults caused by inadvertent impropriety on the part of both student and teacher: 'May He protect us both' — may He nourish us, guard us, through the illumination of the true nature of the knowledge. Who? That very Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) revealed in the <s>Upaniṣad</s>. Moreover, 'May He nourish us both' — may He protect us through the illumination of its fruit. 'Together may we both accomplish' — may we together bring about the vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), the power, produced by knowledge. Moreover, 'May our study be luminous' — may what has been studied by us both, by teacher and student, be well-studied. Or alternatively: may what has been studied by us both be exceedingly luminous, powerful — that is the meaning. 'May we not hate each other' — may we, teacher and student, not harbor hatred toward each other on account of faults arising from careless, improper study and teaching — that is the meaning. The threefold utterance of '<s>śāntiḥ</s>, <s>śāntiḥ</s>, <s>śāntiḥ</s>' is for the purpose of pacifying all faults — thus <s>Oṃ</s>. (<s>KaUBh</s> 6.19/2.3.19)

body.text: iti śrīmat paramahaṃsaparivrājakācāryasya śrī govindabhagavatpūjyapādaśiṣyasya śrī śaṅkarabhagavataḥ kṛtau kāṭhakopaniṣadbhāṣyaṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the <s>Kāṭhakopaniṣadbhāṣya</s> composed by the revered <s>Śaṅkara Bhagavat</s>, disciple of the venerable <s>Govinda Bhagavatpūjyapāda</s>, who is the foremost among the wandering mendicants of the order of <s>Paramahaṃsa</s>.
